title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in New Zealand.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                    • Additional qualifications considered an advantage

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Community credentials or roles such as CNCF Ambassador, AWS Community Builder, or Microsoft MVP.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

                      • Cloud certifications from providers such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.

                        • Benefits:

                        • Competitive fixed fee per course, agreed upfront based on course length and topic complexity, with higher compensation for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

title: Systems Engineer IV

  • Proven experience owning the integrated technical baseline for complex systems through the full Systems Engineering Lifecycle

title: Rental Counter Specialist

Position Overview

True Zero is seeking a Portfolio Manager, Commercial & SLED to own the delivery performance, financial results, growth, and people of a defined market segment. This is a working-leader role: the Portfolio Manager is accountable for a portfolio of customers, contracts, and programs, and serves as the business owner for that segment — responsible for revenue and gross margin, delivery quality and contract compliance, customer relationships, account growth, and the leadership and development of the people assigned to the segment.

The Portfolio Manager is the first-line supervisor for the Program Manager and Project Manager tier within the segment (which in turn supervises delivery staff), and remains partially billable — maintaining 40–50% billable or chargeable utilization while leading the business. The ideal candidate brings a track record of P&L ownership, team leadership, and customer management in consulting, professional services, or government program delivery. This role will be reporting to the Director, Commercial/SLED Services.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, implementation, and oversight of enterprise application security and cybersecurity engineering solutions, ensuring alignment with federal security requirements and industry best practices.
  • Provide subject matter expertise in application security, cloud security, vulnerability management, and secure system architecture across complex enterprise environments.
  • Establish technical objectives, develop project plans, and direct security engineering activities to ensure successful delivery of program requirements.
  • Evaluate security risks, identify vulnerabilities, and recommend mitigation strategies to strengthen enterprise applications, cloud infrastructure, and overall security posture.
  • Provide technical and management leadership for major cybersecurity initiatives, including oversight of engineering resources, staffing, budgets, and project deliverables.
  • Collaborate with government stakeholders, senior leadership, and cross-functional technical teams to define security requirements, resolve complex challenges, and support strategic decision-making.
  • Develop and enforce security engineering standards, policies, and procedures aligned with applicable federal cybersecurity frameworks and compliance requirements.
  • Mentor and provide technical direction to security engineers and other team members while ensuring successful execution of project objectives.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Education: Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related
  • 15+ years of relevant experience in cybersecurity engineering, application security, cloud security, information assurance, or related technical disciplines, including leadership on complex enterprise or federal government programs.
  • Active Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification – Mandatory.
  • Active Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP) certification – Mandatory.
  • Extensive knowledge of application security principles, secure software development practices, vulnerability assessment, risk management, and enterprise security architecture.
  • Demonstrated experience securing cloud environments and implementing cybersecurity controls across enterprise applications, infrastructure, and hybrid cloud architectures.
  • Strong understanding of federal cybersecurity requirements and frameworks, including NIST standards, Risk Management Framework (RMF), FISMA, and applicable security compliance practices.
  • Proven ability to lead technical teams, manage complex cybersecurity initiatives, oversee project resources, and communicate effectively with senior leadership and government stakeholders.
  • Must reside in or be willing to relocate to the Washington, DC, Maryland, or Northern Virginia (DMV) area and be available to work a hybrid onsite/remote schedule.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) certification.
  • Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) certification.
  • Additional recognized cybersecurity or cloud security certifications.
  • Previous experience supporting federal government cybersecurity programs or large-scale enterprise security initiatives.
  • Experience providing technical leadership, managing project financials and staffing, and coordinating with senior-level government clients.

What We Offer

Team members at True Zero enjoy:

  • A competitive salary, paid twice per month, plus an annual performance bonus tied to segment results
  • Best-in-class medical coverage — 100% of medical premiums covered by True Zero
  • Companywide new business incentive programs
  • Contribution incentives (white papers, blog posts, internal webinars, etc.)
  • 3 weeks of PTO to start, plus 11 paid holidays annually
  • 401(k) with 100% company match on the first 4%
  • Monthly reimbursement of cell phone and home internet costs
  • Paternity / Maternity leave

True Zero Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

title: Cybersecurity Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Cybersecurity Engineer based in the United States.

We are seeking an experienced Cybersecurity Engineer to lead the security and compliance of a complex, unclassified IT environment supporting sensitive defense and national security operations. In this hands-on individual contributor role, you will strengthen security controls, assess technical configurations, and maintain compliance with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 requirements. You will take ownership of compliance documentation, technical self-assessments, vulnerability remediation, and audit readiness while helping build and improve an evolving cybersecurity program. Working closely with enterprise IT, cybersecurity operations, and organizational leadership, you will translate regulatory requirements into practical security measures that protect Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI). This opportunity is ideal for a technically strong security professional who enjoys taking initiative, improving processes, and balancing rigorous compliance standards with real-world infrastructure needs. You will play a critical role in maintaining security, accountability, and trust across cloud, hybrid, and enterprise systems.

Accountabilities

  • Cybersecurity Compliance and Governance: Own the security and compliance posture of the unclassified environment, maintaining the System Security Plan (SSP) in alignment with NIST SP 800-171 and CMMC Level 2 requirements.

  • Risk Management and Remediation: Track security findings, vulnerabilities, and compliance gaps; maintain Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms); and coordinate timely remediation with relevant technical teams.

  • Security Assessment Reporting: Generate, maintain, and validate Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) scores, identify control deficiencies, and prepare the environment for independent third-party assessments.

  • Change Management: Follow established change management procedures and Change Control Board (CCB) requirements, ensuring infrastructure modifications are properly reviewed, validated, and tested before production deployment.

  • Internal Assessments and Audit Readiness: Independently plan and conduct comprehensive technical self-assessments to validate control implementation and effectiveness across the unclassified network.

  • External Assessment Coordination: Prepare for Certified Third-Party Assessment Organization (C3PAO) assessments by organizing evidence, interviewing technical staff, documenting controls, and providing accurate technical responses to auditors.

  • Cloud and Hybrid Infrastructure Security: Secure and monitor Google Workspace and Microsoft environments, including Active Directory and Group Policy, ensuring appropriate separation of duties, access management, and secure remote access.

  • CUI Protection Controls: Ensure data loss prevention (DLP), access controls, endpoint security, and mobile device management (MDM) configurations meet applicable requirements for protecting Controlled Unclassified Information.

  • Configuration Monitoring: Monitor infrastructure and security settings for configuration drift against established CUI security baselines and coordinate corrective actions when gaps arise.

  • Vendor and Software Security Assurance: Serve as the primary cybersecurity contact for evaluating new enterprise software and third-party vendors, assessing compliance requirements before tools are introduced into the environment.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Enterprise IT and IT/Cyber Operations to implement security controls, resolve findings, and maintain compliance across the unclassified environment.

  • Program Reporting and Continuous Improvement: Provide leadership with accurate information on security posture, compliance risks, and remediation progress while improving assessment workflows, evidence collection, and compliance processes.

    • Requirements:

    • U.S. citizenship is required, along with authorization to work in the United States, due to requirements associated with access to CUI and ITAR-related data.

    • Five to eight years of professional cybersecurity experience, including at least three years specifically focused on NIST SP 800-171 compliance and implementation.

    • Demonstrated experience configuring and securing Google Workspace in a regulated environment, including security and compliance controls across Drive, Gmail, and endpoint management.

    • Proven ability to independently conduct technical security self-assessments, test control effectiveness, identify deficiencies, and collect defensible evidence for audit purposes.

    • In-depth knowledge of NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 2 assessment guides, and applicable Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) requirements, including clauses 252.204-7012, 252.204-7019, and 252.204-7020.

    • An active DoD 8570/8140 IAM Level II or Level III certification, such as CISSP, CISM, CASP+, or CAP.

    • Strong technical documentation skills and the ability to explain complex security requirements, risks, and remediation plans to non-technical stakeholders and external auditors.

    • Experience working across cloud-based and hybrid IT environments, with a practical understanding of access controls, configuration management, endpoint security, and compliance monitoring.

    • Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple findings, changing priorities, and evolving compliance requirements independently.

    • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, particularly when coordinating remediation efforts across IT, cybersecurity, and business teams.

    • A CMMC Certified Professional (CCP) or Registered Practitioner (RP) credential is preferred.

    • Google Professional Cloud Security Engineer or Professional Google Workspace Administrator certification is an advantage.

    • An active Secret or Top Secret security clearance is a plus but is not required for this role.

    • Experience as a formal Security Control Assessor (SCA) or Qualified Security Assessor (QSA) is preferred.

    • Familiarity with endpoint detection and response (EDR), security information and event management (SIEM), and incident-response tools is beneficial.

      • Benefits:

      • Annual base salary: $145,000–$163,000 USD.

      • Performance-based compensation: Additional performance bonus opportunities.

      • Equity: Equity compensation as part of the overall rewards package.

      • Healthcare coverage: Medical, dental, and vision benefits.

      • Retirement savings: 401(k) plan.

      • Paid time off: PTO to support personal time and work-life balance.

      • Remote flexibility: Remote position with responsibility for securing and monitoring the organization's unclassified environment.

      • Technical ownership: Opportunity to lead hands-on compliance implementation, security assessments, and remediation initiatives.

      • Professional impact: Help strengthen cybersecurity practices supporting sensitive defense and national security operations.

      • Program development: Build and improve compliance processes, assessment practices, and security evidence workflows as the environment evolves.

      • Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with IT, cybersecurity operations, leadership, and external assessors to strengthen organizational security and compliance.

title: Floating ELC Center Director
description:
SUMMARY OF POSITION: This position supports the work of the YMCA, a leading nonprofit committed to strengthening community through youth development, healthy living and social responsibility. Under the general direction of the Executive Director of Early Learning this position ensures the successful operation of assigned sites to include program quality, program promotion, budget monitoring, personnel supervision and community relations. This position will be responsible for training, monitoring and supporting Director’s with new employee orientation and other early childhood priorities as identified through monitoring of classrooms, teacher-child interactions, licensing reports and by Director’s and Administrative staff. This position will also be responsible for filling in at centers in the absence of Director’s for any timeframe at all locations as needed.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:


Leadership

  • Lead assigned center and programs and take responsibility for the successful operation of a child development center, including observing, coaching, and supervising lead teachers, teachers, aides and support staff as identified based on the need of the Early Learning department.

Parent Experience

  • Lead and ensure a high-quality parent experience through program quality, planning and communication when serving in the capacity of an Early Learning Center Director.

Operations

  • When serving in the capacity of a Center Director, Coach and supervise lead teachers, teachers, and aides in areas including, but not limited to:
  • planning and implementation of the program.
  • providing a high-quality, developmentally appropriate curriculum aligned to the state of Tennessee or State of Mississippi early childhood education standards.
  • maintain student portfolios and development plans to include developmental milestones and kindergarten transition plans.
  • maintaining stimulating and orderly program spaces.
  • purchasing appropriate supplies, equipment, and materials, following YMCA purchasing guidelines and procedures.
  • maintaining program enrollment at appropriate levels.
  • conducting program tours and periodic open house/registration events.
  • maintaining accurate and complete records for licensing & safety.
  • planning and conducting a comprehensive family engagement plan (i.e. Parent Advisory Group, picnics, holidays, and parent/child activities).

Growth

  • Under the supervision of the Executive Director of Early Learning, takes an active and supportive role in program planning, program promotion and publicity to meet assigned enrollment goals.
  • Assist with planning and leading professional development and new hire orientation for Lead Teachers, Assistants, Directors and Assistant Directors. Develop both individualized and group training as needed.

Relationship Building

  • Develops and maintains relationships with education staff and Directors. When serving in capacity of Center Director, develop and maintain relationships with state childcare licensing agencies, school administration, community partners and parent groups.

Communication

  • Responds to the needs of Center Director’s, Teaching staff and agencies, parent and community inquiries and complaints in a timely manner, seeking guidance from supervisor(s) and peer directors as needed.
  • Model superior communication and leadership to any level of staff and customers served.

Continuous Improvement

  • Evaluate sites in areas including, but not limited to, proper implementation of curriculum and lesson planning, program quality control, health and safety, teacher-child interactions and recruitment and retention of program participants.

Licensing

  • Assure Education staff and Director’s receives training and in compliance with state and local regulations during training and monitoring. This includes establishing emergency & safety procedures that meet or exceed all safety and licensing standards and that these procedures are followed.

Financial Management

  • When serving in capacity of Center Director, must meet revenue and expense goals for the center.
  • Work with assigned facility directors and maintenance teams to ensure facilities are in good repair, all safety guidelines are met, and repairs are made in a timely manner.

Philanthropy

  • Supports the Executive Director and Center Directors by providing leadership and support to the annual fundraising campaign at centers, as well as supporting overall campaign goals for Centralized Childcare.

YMCA Partnership

  • Attends and participates in assigned staff meetings and special events to provide a collaborative and cohesive approach to the YMCA’s vision and mission.
  • Assume other duties and responsibilities as assigned to meet the changing needs of the program and/or center.


YMCA LEADERSHIP COMPETENCIES:


Mission Advancement: Champions the YMCA’s cause and mission. Builds effective systems for volunteer development and secures resources to advance philanthropic impact.


Collaboration: Works effectively with people of different backgrounds, abilities, opinions, and perceptions. Builds rapport and relates well to others. Seeks first to understand the other person’s point of view and remains calm in challenging situations. Listens for understanding and meaning; speaks and writes effectively. Takes initiative to assist in developing others.


Operational Effectiveness: Makes sound judgments, and transfers learning from one situation to another. Embraces new approaches and discovers ideas to create a better member experience. Establishes goals, clarifies tasks, plans of work, and actively participates in meetings. Follows budgeting policies and procedures and reports for all financial irregularities immediately. Strives to meet or exceed goals and deliver a high-value experience for members.


Personal Growth: Embraces learning, adaptability, and innovation. Anticipates challenges and models resilience and professional growth.

Behavioral Characteristics: Welcoming, Nurturing, Determined, Hopeful, and Genuine.


QUALIFICATIONS, KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:


Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in a directly related field or an equivalent combination of directly related experience, training, and/or education.
  • Five or more years of childcare experience preferred. Comparable experience in other organizations may be considered.
  • Meets minimum qualifications for childcare director as outlined in the Tennessee Department of Human Services or Mississippi Department of Health standards for childcare and completes these requirements within 30 days of hire.
  • Knowledge of childcare licensing requirements for Tennessee or Mississippi Department of Health for childcare and YMCA standards or ability to learn all standards within 60 days of hire.
  • Knowledge of early childhood development practices, developmental milestones, and educational needs for infants through pre-kindergarten.

WORK SCHEDULE:

The full-time work schedule for this position is generally Monday through Friday, 8:00am-6:00pm, though evenings and weekends work may be required. Flexible work schedule required. Work schedules may vary per the needs of the specific ELC site.

The hours of operation for the Hernando ELC are 6:30 am - 6:00 pm (subject to change).


WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • Climbing, sitting, standing, pushing, walking, kneeling, and stooping
  • Some Exposure to the outdoor elements
  • Exposure to electrical/mechanical mechanisms
  • Exposure to some chemical elements
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds

title: Building Inspector
description:
General Description

The purpose of this job within the organization is to inspect buildings and structures for code compliance, the safety and integrity of the renovation of existing structures within the City of Charleston.

This job works under general supervision, independently developing work methods and sequences.

Duties and Responsibilities

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this job. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the job as necessary.

Essential Functions:

Strives to be efficient and effective at balancing and meeting the common needs and reasonable expectations of core constituents.

Contributes towards the department's mission by continuously striving to meet expectations, strategic goals and objectives.

Performs all phases of inspections on new structures and the renovations of existing structures.

Inspects structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations.

Conducts plumbing and HVAC inspections.

Conducts electrical inspections and plan reviews as needed.

Issues permits and conducts city-wide checks to insure permits are obtained.

Answers telephone and responds to walk-in questions and code compliance complaints.

Monitors installation of plumbing, wiring, equipment, or appliances to ensure that installation is performed properly and is in compliance with applicable regulations.

Measures dimensions and verifies level, alignment, or elevation of structures or fixtures to ensure compliance to building plans and codes.

Responds to emergency structure issues and concerns by being a part of the department's on call rotation.

Performs related work as assigned.

Responsibilities, Requirements and Impacts

Data Responsibility:

Data Responsibility refers to information, knowledge, and conceptions obtained by observation, investigation, interpretation, visualization, and mental creation. Data are intangible and include numbers, words, symbols, ideas, concepts, and oral verbalizations.

Gathers, organizes, analyzes, examines or evaluates data or information and may prescribe action based on these data or information.

People Responsibility:

People include co-workers, workers in other areas or agencies and the general public.

Provides information, guidance or assistance to people that directly facilitates task accomplishment; may give instructions or assignments to helpers or assistants.

Asset Responsibility:

Assets responsibility refers to the responsibility for achieving economies or preventing loss within the organization.

Requires minimum responsibility for only small quantities of low cost items or supplies where opportunities for achieving economies or preventing loss are negligible.

Mathematical Requirements:

Mathematics requires the use of symbols, numbers and formulas to solve mathematical problems.

Uses addition and subtraction, multiplication and division and/or calculates ratios, rates and percents.

Communications Requirements:

Communications involves the ability to read, write, and speak.

Reads technical instructions, procedures manuals and charts to solve practical problems, such as assembly instruction for tools, routine office equipment operating instructions, and methods and procedures in drawing and layout work; composes routine reports and specialized reports, forms, and business letters, with proper format; speaks compound sentences using normal grammar and word form.

Judgment Requirements:

Judgment requirements refer to the frequency and complexity of judgments and decisions given the stability of the work environments, the nature and type of guidance, and the breadth of impact of the judgments and decisions.

Responsible for long range goals, planning and methodologies. Decision-making is focus of the job, affecting entire organization and surrounding population; works in an unstable environment with frequent and significant changes in conditions.

Complexity of Work:

Complexity addresses the analysis, initiative, ingenuity, concentration and creativity, required by the job and the presence of any unusual pressures present in the job.

Performs skilled work involving rules/systems with almost constant problem solving; requires normal attention with short periods of concentration for accurate results and occasional exposure to unusual pressure.

Impact of Errors:

Impact of errors refers to consequences such as damage to equipment and property, loss of data, exposure of the organization to legal liability, and injury or death for individuals.

The impact of errors is moderately serious - affects work unit and may affect other units or citizens.

Physical Demands:

Physical demands refer to the requirements for physical exertion and coordination of limb and body movement.

Performs light to medium work that involves walking or standing virtually all of the time and also involves exerting between 20 and 50 pounds of force on a regular and recurring basis or considerable skill, adeptness and speed in the use of the fingers, hands or limbs in tasks involving close tolerances or limits of accuracy.

Equipment Usage:

Equipment usage involves responsibility for materials, machines, tools, equipment, work aids, and products.

Handles or uses tools, equipment or work aids involving some latitude for judgment regarding attainment of a standard or in selecting appropriate items.

Unavoidable Hazards:

Unavoidable hazards refer to the job conditions that may lead to injury or health hazards even though precautions have been taken.

Involves routine and frequent exposure to traffic; moving machinery.

Safety of Others:

Safety of others refers to the level of responsibility for the safety of others, either inherent in the job or to ensure the safety of the general public. (Does not include safety of subordinates).

Requires responsibility for the safety and health of others and for occasional enforcement of the laws and standards of public health and safety.

Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:

Requires High School graduation or GED equivalent.

Requires some experience in construction and building inspection or closely related experience.

Special Certifications and Licenses:

Must obtain within two (2) years of the hire date and maintain ICC certifications: Residential Building Inspector B1, Residential Mechanical Inspector M1, and Residential Plumbing Inspector P1.

Must obtain within four (4) years of the hire date and maintain ICC certifications: Residential Electrical Inspector E1, Commercial Building Inspector B2, Commercial Electrical Inspector E2, Commercial Mechanical Inspector M2, and Commercial Plumbing Inspector P2.

Driver's License

Core Competencies:

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  1. Accountability - takes responsibility for own actions.
  2. Adaptability - responds positively to change.
  3. Communications - listens, speaks and/or writes in a clear, concise and respectful manner.
  4. Customer Service - provides courteous, accessible and quality assistance to internal and external customers.
  5. Initiative - takes proactive action to complete work or resolve issues
  6. Judgment & Decision Making - evaluates issues and makes sound factual decisions.
  7. Professional Development - seeks opportunities to enhance technical skills and job knowledge.
  8. Teamwork & Cooperation - collaborates with others to fulfill the City's vision and achieve departmental goals and strategic objectives.

Additional Qualifications:

  1. Must have the ability to provide documentation verifying legal work status.
  2. Ability to read and speak the English language proficiently in order to communicate and interact with others; to understand and interpret safety instructions; and to respond to internal and external inquiries.
  3. Ability to understand and comply with City and departmental guidelines, policies, procedures and expectations.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work that may be performed by an employee. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory or list of all of the duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. Supervisors/Managers and/or Department Heads may also assign additional or other lawful duties as may be necessary and/or required. The City reserves the right to modify or change this job description at any time, for any lawful reason, with or without notice. This job description is not, and should not be construed or implied to be a contract, promise or guarantee of continued employment.

Americans with Disabilities Act Compliance

The City of Charleston, WV is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The ADA requires the City to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified persons with disabilities.

Prospective and current employees are encouraged to discuss ADA accommodations with management.

title: Sr. Manager IT Applications
description:
Senior Manager, IT Applications

Reports To: Director, Information Technology Department: Information Technology Location: Stow, Ohio FLSA Status: Exempt

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, IT Applications is a strategic technology leader responsible for the overall direction, support, enhancement, development, security, and optimization of the organization's business application portfolio. This role leads the teams responsible for application development, business systems analysis, reporting, and application security while ensuring technology solutions align with organizational goals and deliver measurable business value.

The Senior Manager, IT Applications serves as the primary IT leader for enterprise business applications, including ERP (JD Edwards), Manufacturing Execution Systems (Greycon), reporting platforms (Power BI), and other critical business systems. This individual is responsible for driving continuous improvement initiatives, supporting business transformation projects, and ensuring the application landscape evolves to meet the changing needs of the organization.

Direct Reports

The following functions and leaders report directly to this position:

  • Manager, ERP Development & Technology
  • Manager, Business Systems Analysis
  • Reporting and Business Intelligence Function
  • Application Security Function

Key Responsibilities

Application Strategy & Leadership

  • Develop and execute the strategic roadmap for enterprise business applications.
  • Establish application governance processes, standards, and best practices.
  • Align application investments and initiatives with business objectives.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to business leadership on technology opportunities and application capabilities.
  • Lead the evaluation, selection, implementation, and optimization of business applications.

ERP, Manufacturing Systems, and Business Applications

  • Provide leadership for the support, development, and continuous improvement of JD Edwards (JDE).
  • Oversee Manufacturing Execution Systems and related manufacturing technology platforms.
  • Ensure reliable operation and support of all enterprise business applications.
  • Drive the adoption of new technologies and solutions that improve business efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Establish long-term plans for application modernization and lifecycle management.

Development & Technical Leadership

  • Lead application development teams responsible for ERP enhancements, integrations, reporting solutions, and custom applications.
  • Ensure effective software development, testing, deployment, and support methodologies.
  • Oversee application architecture decisions and integration strategies.
  • Promote automation and innovation across the application portfolio.

Business Relationship Management

  • Partner with leaders across Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, Customer Service, Human Resources, and other business functions.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable technology solutions.
  • Prioritize initiatives and resources based on organizational objectives.
  • Ensure high levels of user satisfaction and business engagement.

Project & Portfolio Management

  • Lead strategic application projects from concept through deployment.
  • Manage application-related project portfolios, budgets, resources, and timelines.
  • Ensure successful delivery of ERP enhancements, system implementations, upgrades, and business transformation initiatives.
  • Drive continuous improvement efforts across all supported platforms.

Reporting, Analytics, and Data Management

  • Provide oversight for reporting and business intelligence solutions.
  • Ensure reporting capabilities support operational and strategic decision-making.
  • Promote data quality, governance, and consistency across business systems.
  • Support data-driven decision making through effective analytics solutions.

Security, Compliance, and Risk Management

  • Oversee application security standards and practices.
  • Ensure appropriate controls, access management, segregation of duties, and audit compliance.
  • Partner with infrastructure and cybersecurity teams to manage risks affecting business applications.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies and external regulatory requirements.

Team Development

  • Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing applications organization.
  • Establish performance expectations and career development opportunities.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, customer service, accountability, and continuous learning.
  • Ensure the team possesses the skills necessary to support evolving business requirements and emerging technologies.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Information Systems, or related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of progressive IT experience supporting enterprise applications.
  • Minimum 3 years of leadership experience managing technical teams.
  • Experience leading ERP, application development, and business analysis functions.
  • Experience managing cross-functional technology initiatives and projects.
  • Strong understanding of application lifecycle management, systems integration, and business process optimization.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting JD Edwards EnterpriseOne.
  • Experience supporting Manufacturing Execution Systems.
  • Experience with reporting and business intelligence platforms.
  • Experience with application governance, security, and compliance programs.
  • Project management experience and formal project management training or certification.

Competencies

  • Strategic Leadership
  • Business Partnership
  • People Development
  • Change Management
  • Continuous Improvement
  • Customer Focus
  • Technology Innovation
  • Financial and Project Management
  • Communication and Influencing Skills
  • Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills

Working Conditions

  • Primarily office-based position located in Stow, Ohio.
  • 0 to 20% travel to manufacturing and business sites as required.
  • Ability to work effectively in both independent and team-oriented environments.

Success Measures

Success in this role will be demonstrated by:

  • High availability and performance of business applications.
  • Successful delivery of application projects and enhancements.
  • Continuous improvement of JD Edwards, MES, and related business systems.
  • Strong business stakeholder satisfaction.
  • Effective management of application security and compliance requirements.
  • Development of a high-performing applications organization capable of supporting current operations while enabling future business growth.

This position plays a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization's ERP ecosystem, manufacturing systems, and broader application portfolio provide a stable, secure, and continuously improving technology foundation that supports operational excellence and business growth.

title: TCAC Systems Administrator II - Goodfellow AFB, TX
description:
Predicate Logic is looking for a motivated TCAC Systems Administrator II to join our team at Goodfellow Air Force Base, TX.

Founded in 1992, Predicate Logic is a woman-owned, employee-owned, high technology engineering service company. Predicate Logic's employees routinely receive many accolades and awards from its customers. The corporate headquarters is in San Diego, California. Predicate Logic also has offices in Chesapeake, Virginia, specializing in communications engineering, training, and Cybersecurity, and in Charleston, South Carolina, supporting the Navy and Marine Corps programs through Naval Information Warfare Center Charleston.


SECURITY CLEARANCE:

  • Applicant must hold an active Department of War (DoW) personnel security clearance.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Establish, maintain, and Assist personnel in troubleshooting and repair of serial and IP-based communications systems and networks.
  • Assist government personnel in maintaining strict configuration control of current architectures.
  • Participate in assigned Computer and Communications Systems Engineering Reviews and provide technical representation at meetings as required.
  • Test, maintain, and monitor computer programs and systems, including coordinating the installation of computer programs and systems.
  • Assess the usefulness of pre-developed application packages and adapt them to a user environment.
  • Coordinate and link the computer systems within an organization to increase compatibility so that information can be shared.
  • Develop, document, and revise system design procedures, test procedures, and quality standards.
  • Provide network and system administration of the assigned Computer and Communications Systems.
  • Ensure the identification of required security-related issues are properly alerted upon by configuring and establishing monitoring, correlation, and alerting solutions.
  • Conduct vulnerability and exploitation scans to determine vulnerabilities and mitigations.
  • Execute automated vulnerability scans using DoD-approved software (Tenable, Nessus, and SCAP).
  • Ensure systems are following applicable Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs).
  • Develop and maintain Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) and prepare exemption waivers and justification documents.
  • Make recommendations for system changes to the environment that can help in the removal of vulnerabilities and reduce the risk of exploitation.
  • Serve as Lead on cyber tasks and ISSO for TCAC and TSCS Systems Security Plans (SSPs) (Cyber and Acquisitions Security).
  • Handle NSA Risk Management Framework (RMF) coordination for NSANet and JWICS for TCAC.

EXPERIENCE:

  • Twenty (20+) plus years of professional experience in systems administration.

EDUCATION:

  • Bachelor's of Science degree Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or Information Systems. Completion of the Marine Cryptologic Computer Administration Program.
  • Must be Cyber Security Work Force (CSWF) certified for Information Assurance Technician Level III (IAT-III) and Information Assurance Manager (IAM) Level I. Require CISSP or higher certifications.
  • In scope Counterintelligence Polygraph required.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled

Predicate Logic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About the team

The Release Team owns the safe, continuous delivery of ClickHouse Cloud, a managed database platform running tens of thousands of ClickHouse clusters. About the role

This role is an equal split between operational execution and software development. You are responsible for the operational side: coordinating and running upgrades, dealing with edge cases that don't fit the happy path, and keeping tens of thousands of clusters healthy in production. At the same time, you are building and constantly improving the systems that make the next rollout safer and more automated than the last. If you find satisfaction in both writing the playbook and executing it, including the messy parts, this role is for you.

What you'll do

  • Plan and execute rolling upgrades across tens of thousands of ClickHouse clusters, ensuring safety, correctness, and minimal customer impact

  • Own the full release pipeline: from pre-upgrade validation and staged rollouts to post-upgrade monitoring and incident response

  • Investigate and resolve production issues as part of a regular on-call rotation, including snowflake clusters and edge cases that automation can't yet handle

  • Build and improve the internal tooling and automation that makes large-scale database operations reliable and repeatable

  • Work closely with the core database and cloud infrastructure teams to identify operational pain points and turn them into solved problems

  • Support and educate other engineering teams using our internal tools

About you

  • 5+ years of experience operating stateful distributed systems in production, such as databases, message queues, or storage systems

  • Hands-on experience running upgrades or maintenance operations on live production data stores, at scale

  • Strong production debugging skills; you are comfortable digging into unfamiliar systems under pressure

  • Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and Kubernetes

Perks

title: Principal Data & AI Engineer- Media
description:
Principal Data & AI Engineer- Audience & Measurement

  • senior technical leadership role
  • Surry Hills location with hybrid working (3 days in the office)
  • Help establish the Centre of Excellence for audience capability and media measurement.

About Cartology, Audience Capabilities, and the Data & AI COE

Cartology is the Retail Media Business within Woolworths Group, connecting brands with customers through data-led experiences. Retail media runs on data: audiences planned before a campaign, measured during it, and proven after it, across our own channels and the open web.

We are investing in new audience capabilities: how audiences are created, governed, and activated across channels. Woolworths Group data platforms underpin the work, and the engineering bar is high: audiences that reach their channels in hours, with commercial guardrails engineered into the platform rather than bolted on as manual review.

Alongside the audience work, we are evolving measurement: post-campaign measurement and reporting with and without audience overlay, for on-network and off-network advertising, drawing on platform reporting, ad logs, and data clean rooms.

You join at the start. Initially you are part of the audience capability project team; as the capability maturing you embed in the core Data & Audience team as a founding member of our Data & AI engineering Centre of Excellence (COE) for audience and media measurement. The COE shapes delivery of our audience capabilities from a Data & Audience perspective and drives our data & AI platform evolution: a governed semantic layer, conversational analytics, and AI-ready data for the next phase of growth.

What You’ll Do

As Principal Data & AI Engineer within Cartology’s Data & Audience team, you set the technical direction for audience and measurement engineering across Woolworths Group data platforms. In this senior technical leadership role, you guide architecture, standards, and AI SDLC practices without direct reports, partnering with Product and Engineering managers to stand up the Data & AI Centre of Excellence. You architect end-to-end data foundations from fast, governed audience activation to post-campaign measurement ensuring every technical decision balances high engineering standards with commercial accuracy and clear revenue impact.

  • Set Technical Direction: Lead the architecture and engineering strategy for Cartology’s audience and measurement data platforms.
  • Establish Engineering Standards: Define robust AI SDLC practices and technical benchmarks across Woolworths Group data systems.
  • Lead Without Direct Reports: Drive technical excellence and team direction through direct architectural leadership and mentorship.
  • Found the Data & AI COE: Help establish the Centre of Excellence for audience capability and media measurement.
  • Partner with Leadership: Collaborate closely with Product and Senior Engineering Managers to shape delivery scope and platform roadmaps.
  • Build End-to-End Solutions: Architect the complete data lifecycle, from rapid audience creation to comprehensive post-campaign reporting.
  • Embed Commercial Guardrails: Ensure governance, privacy, and business logic are engineered directly into the data platform.
  • Drive Business Impact: Align complex technical designs with commercial accuracy, revenue goals, and proven brand value.

What You’ll Bring

We are looking for a commercially fluent, ad-tech native Principal Data & AI Engineer who takes complete ownership of outcomes and interrogated business needs before writing code. You bring deep, hands on experience with ad logs, audience segmentation, platform reporting, and data clean rooms, understanding that accuracy is paramount when brand investments are on the line. As an AI-forward technical leader, you set the standard for how engineering teams build with AI while easily translating complex measurement logic for business stakeholders. Above all, you measure your personal success by the quality, reliability, and business impact of the platforms your fellow engineers ship.

  • Proven Platform Architecture: 8+ years in data engineering, with proven experience designing large scale data platforms in BigQuery, Snowflake, or Redshift.
  • Core Technical Expertise: Mastery of SQL, Python, dbt, and Airflow, with a strong track record of building scalable data foundations.
  • Ad-Tech Domain Knowledge: Deep experience with ad logs, audience segmentation, platform reporting, and campaign measurement within retail media, publishers, or agencies.
  • Technical Leadership: Skilled in guiding senior engineers, conducting design reviews, and raising engineering standards without needing direct reports.
  • AI & SDLC Enablement: Hands-on experience driving AI-assisted engineering practices, governance guardrails, and AI-ready data infrastructure.
  • Commercial Acumen & Communication: Ability to translate complex technical designs into clear business outcomes for product and commercial stakeholders.
  • Audience & Measurement Ecosystems (Desirable): Familiarity with data clean rooms, warehouse-native activation tools (Hightouch, Census, RudderStack), or platforms like Meta, LiveRamp, and DV360.
  • Advanced Analytics & COE Setup (Desirable): Exposure to semantic layers (LookML, Cube, dbt metrics), closed-loop measurement, incrementality, or helping build a Centre of Excellence from scratch.

What You’ll Experience

  • Develop your career in an organisation that gives you the time and space to think creatively and strategically
  • Feel supported and empowered by your leaders
  • A truly unique opportunity to be involved in creating, shaping and leading the new retail media industry.
  • A global business with endless career possibilities around every corner and across every discipline.
  • Team discounts across our range of Woolworths Group brands you know and love and a robust rewards program that celebrates and incentivises purpose-driven work.

Endless Possibilities With Woolworths Group

We’re a proud part of the Woolworths Group (200,000+ bright minds, passionate hearts and unique perspectives working together connected by a shared Purpose) ‘to create better experiences together for a better tomorrow.’

Here you’ll be supported and empowered to explore new ideas, make brave commitments and innovate better ways to meet the food and everyday needs of more than 24 million customers every week. Backed by a culture of genuine care, a flexible approach to work and the support to grow your career and make a meaningful impact, the possibilities for what we can achieve together are endless.

Everyone Belongs At Woolworths Group

Diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging are key to realising our purpose of better together for a better tomorrow. We recognise the value our team’s diversity brings to our business, customers, and communities and that teams with diverse experiences and backgrounds enrich our group and are better able to innovate and solve problems. As one of the largest employers in Australia and New Zealand, we aim to create a truly inclusive workplace where everyone feels that they belong, can be their best selves, and reach their full potential.

- Extracting actionable insights: inspect execution traces and benchmark outputs to isolate systemic failures, delivering high-conviction system design updates that directly enhance output fidelity.
- Scaling agent simulation environments: expand continuous multi-agent testing capabilities to unlock higher throughput for concurrent entity evaluation.
- Driving complete execution loops: lead problem definition, data pipeline construction, automated benchmarking, and technical writeups with total autonomy and minimal administrative overhead.

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov

Are you passionate about performing experimental research in the field of materials science and mechanical behavior of materials? Are you collaboration-focused and want to join a diverse team that solves significant issues facing our nation and the world? You could be the postdoctoral appointee that we are looking for to work in the area of reliable microdevices and electronic packaging for harsh environments! This is an exciting opportunity to join a highly productive and collaborative network of scientists.

The primary project involves the development of materials and novel microelectronic packaging solutions that can survive harsh environments, including temperatures up to 200C and repetitive shock/impact loading. Some important elements include:

  • Understand existing microelectronic packaging solutions that may offer a viable solution or provide a baseline from which to innovate
  • Invent, design, and develop new concepts for microelectronic packaging
  • Coordinate the manufacture of candidate packaging solutions
  • Take advantage of Sandia's in-house manufacturing capabilities including the Center for Advanced Manufacturing Innovation (CAMINO) and the Microsystems Engineering, Science, and Applications (MESA) complex; while also considering external manufacturing resources to achieve product goals
  • Perform or coordinate the testing of candidate packaging solution in relevant environments
  • Coordinate your research with a large product development team
  • Communicate your progress internally at team meetings and externally at research conferences
  • Publish high-quality technical research articles related to your research outcomes

Complementing that primary project goal, you will also participate in a research team advancing the state of the art in the domain of mechanical behavior of materials. Active research in this domain includes:

  • Micro- and nanomechanical testing methods including nanoindentation, micropillar compression, MEMS-based thin film testing, microtensile methods, and conventional load frame-based mechanical testing
  • Advanced characterization methods including: Electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, chemical spectroscopies, electron backscatter diffraction, and x-ray diffraction.
  • In-situ material testing at the micro- and nano-scale
  • Development and implementation of high-throughput testing methods
  • Implementation of autonomous self-driving lab capabilities
  • Collaboration with materials modeling and machine learning specialists

There are also opportunities open to new research pathways as well as to engage with complementary research efforts and interact with a broad spectrum of scientists internal and external to the laboratory.

Due to the nature of the work, the selected applicant must be able to work onsite. Relocation will be provided for those that qualify.

Qualifications We Require

  • PhD in a physical science or engineering discipline (e.g., Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, or related field) must have been conferred within five years prior to employment.
  • Documented experience in both oral presentation settings and in published communication
  • Familiarity with microelectronic packaging strategies.
  • Experience working on an engineering or scientific research team

Qualifications We Desire

We realize that no one will have all the background we desire, so any subset of these skills could make you a candidate for the project, especially if you want to grow in these areas through your own skill development and through collaborations:

  • Experience developing microelectronic packaging solutions
  • Experience with harsh environment testing, including elevated temperatures and/or shock/impact testing
  • Familiarity with product design, including CAD software such as SolidWorks
  • Experience in coordinating the fabrication and testing of materials or product coupons using state-of-the-art manufacturing techniques
  • Experience with mechanical testing of materials (e.g., conventional load frame-based mechanical testing, nanoindentation, micropillar compression, thin film testing, or related techniques)
  • Experience with materials characterization techniques (e.g. scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, x-ray diffraction, and/or other characterization techniques)
  • Familiarity with machine learning and data science methodologies
  • Experience with in situ electron microscopy experiments (such as nanomechanical testing, heating, environmental exposure, etc.)
  • Experience with autonomous experimentation, Bayesian optimization, active learning, or other AI/ML-driven experimental workflows
  • Proficiency with programming for instrument control, data analysis, and/or workflow automation using Python or similar software
  • Familiarity with additive manufacturing processes and the characterization of additively manufactured materials
  • Familiarity with thin film deposition, processing, and microstructural characterization
  • Experience in using electron microscopy for diffraction analysis and defect analysis
  • Familiarity with constitutive modeling, finite element analysis, or molecular dynamics as applied to mechanical behavior
  • Capacity for conception, design, control, and execution of experiments
  • Ability to work as an independent researcher with a high level of scientific judgment, as well as to collaborate with other researchers in a diverse team
  • Experience with MEMS-based mechanical testing, microtensile methods, or other custom small-scale testing platforms

About Our Team

Our team spans across several departments, offering a broad collaborative environment. Some of the topics our team is known for include:

  • Scientific discovery and peer-reviewed publications on nanotechnology, material science, microsystems, metallurgy, mechanical engineering, and related fields
  • Solutions for research and development problems involving mechanical properties of materials
  • Relationships and dependencies among materials structures, composition, properties, performance, reliability, and service environments
  • Diagnostics and modeling that enable deep scientific investigations of material behavior and prevention of failure
  • Pioneering approaches to autonomous experimentation and AI-accelerated materials discovery

This department supports the Center for Integrated Nanotechnology (CINT). CINT is a Department of Energy/Office of Science Nanoscale Science Research Center operating as a national user facility devoted to establishing the scientific principles that govern the design, performance, and integration of nanoscale materials. Through its core facility in Albuquerque and gateway facility in Los Alamos, CINT provides users from academia, industry, and government labs open access to the tools and expertise needed to explore the continuum from scientific discovery to the integration of nanostructures into the micro- and macro world. CINT is an equal partnership between Sandia National Laboratories and Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

Security Clearance

This position does not currently require a Department of Energy (DOE) security clearance.

Sandia will conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Furthermore, employees in New Mexico need to pass a U.S. Air Force background screen for access to Kirtland Air Force Base. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause access to be denied or terminated, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment. Under federal law, citizens and agents of the People's Republic of China, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of North Korea, and the Russian Federation are generally prohibited from accessing Sandia National Laboratories. Accordingly, such individuals will not be considered for employment unless they are also a citizen of the United States.

If hired without a clearance and it subsequently becomes necessary to obtain and maintain one for the position, or you bid on positions that require a clearance, a pre-processing background review may be conducted prior to a required federal background investigation. Applicants for a DOE security clearance need to be U.S. citizens. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Members of the workforce (MOWs) hired at Sandia who require uncleared access for greater than 179 days during their employment, are required to go through the Uncleared Personal Identity Verification (UPIV) process. Access includes physical and/or cyber (logical) access, as well as remote access to any NNSA information technology (IT) systems. UPIV requirements are not applicable to individuals who require a DOE personnel security clearance for the performance of their SNL employment or to foreign nationals. The UPIV process will include the completion of a USAccess Enrollment, SF-85 (Questionnaire for Non-Sensitive Positions) and OF-306 (Declaration of for Federal Employment). An unfavorable UPIV determination will result in immediate retrieval of the SNL issued badge, removal of cyber (logical) access and/or removal from SNL subcontract. All MOWs may appeal the unfavorable UPIV determination to DOE/NNSA immediately. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the MOW may try to go through the UPIV process one year after the decision date.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in France.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.
