title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Cross-Functional Programs
description:
Who we are:

At Rover, pets and their people are at the heart of everything we do. We connect pet parents with trusted pet care across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Australia.

Headquartered in Seattle and Barcelona, we’re a values driven, fast-growing tech company focused on building safe and personalized experiences tailored to the needs of each unique pet. We’re investing in AI as a business accelerator and provide every team member access to AI tools in service of creating better experiences for our community.

We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. At Rover we’re committed to creating an accessible, inclusive, and welcoming community, which starts with our employees.

Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.


Who We're Looking For
Some programs at Rover don't belong to any one team. They pull in product, engineering, data, operations, and the business all at once, and they're the ones that matter most: the platform bet that changes how three orgs build, the flagship feature that can't ship until four teams build against the same plan, the problem everyone agrees is important and nobody can quite scope.

Those programs need someone who owns them outright. You'll join Rover's Technical Program Management team, a small and growing function that sits at the center of how engineering delivers complex, cross-functional work. TPMs here own how programs get executed, drive alignment across organizational boundaries, and bring structured thinking to the hardest problems on the roadmap, all in service of better experiences for the pet parents and sitters who depend on our platform every day.

Your scope is defined by difficulty rather than by domain. Some programs land with you because of their complexity, ambiguity, and visibility, not because of which part of the product they touch. Others you'll find yourself: you'll see the program Rover needs before anyone has named it, and make the case for it. You'll go deep enough in each domain to be genuinely useful, then do it again somewhere else. You'll often carry more than one of these at once, and your work will shape how engineering sets its priorities and OKRs, not just how a single program delivers.

Problems arrive without shape, and your first job is to give them one: a problem statement the room can commit to, a scope with an explicit boundary, named owners and decision rights, and a definition of success set before the build starts. Your second is the technical judgment to be a true peer to engineering: reading a dependency chain, evaluating trade-offs without needing full translation, knowing when to slow down and build the durable thing versus speed up and take on debt deliberately, and spotting where we're walking through a one-way door. You won't just run a playbook. You'll help write it, turning each program into repeatable patterns, and helping the TPMs around you get sharper too.

Most of it comes down to judgment. The role is a steady run of calls with no obviously right answer: when to force a decision and when to let a team keep exploring, when to escalate and when escalating costs more than the delay it saves, when good enough now beats correct later. What matters isn't whether you follow a process, it's whether those instincts are calibrated and you can explain them afterward.

That extends to how you use AI. We're looking for someone who's gone past automating the obvious, like status reports and risk tracking, and is thinking about where these tools change the work more fundamentally: untangling dependencies across a messy program, catching risk earlier in the signal, opening up new ways for distributed teams to collaborate. What matters isn't how many tools you've tried. It's your point of view on where they create real leverage.

This is a role for someone who moves easily across teams and domains, and brings order to complexity without adding bureaucracy.

This is a hybrid position that has the minimum expectation to work out of our Downtown Seattle Office two days per week on Mondays and Thursdays. For this reason, candidates must be based in the Greater Seattle Area or willing to relocate.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Identify the programs Rover needs before they're assigned: spot the cross-org problem no team owns, build the case for it, and stand it up.
  • Take programs from shapeless to executable: converge stakeholders on what problem is actually being solved, set the scope and what's explicitly out of it, establish who owns which decisions, and define what success will be measured by.
  • Own the execution strategy from there, across one or more concurrent programs: turning competing priorities into a coherent plan with owners and sequencing, and making the calls that determine how the work comes together across Rover.
  • Drive decisions rather than track them. Frame the trade-off, make a recommendation, get the right people in the room, and identify the decision maker when the path forward isn't obvious, then land the decision and hold it.
  • Be the point of alignment across organizational boundaries: keep priorities cohesive, surface where they conflict, and get teams to a shared path forward without waiting for an escalation to force it.
  • Be a true peer to engineering on the technical dimension of the program, covering architecture implications, dependency chains, data integrity, and rollout and cutover planning. Pressure-test timelines and sequencing before they slip.
  • Define and report the KPIs that tell teams whether a program is healthy, so risk surfaces early and progress is easy to communicate with confidence. Drive mitigation of department-level risks rather than only escalating them, and connect program KPIs to engineering's OKRs and department strategy.
  • Be the source of truth for program health. Build and maintain the artifacts that keep a program legible — charters, plans, dependency maps, risk registers, decision logs — and communicate crisply in both registers: the detail engineering needs and the summary a leadership audience can act on.
  • Own launch and delivery readiness, making sure everyone from engineering leads to executive sponsors has what they need to move forward. Treat launch as a checkpoint rather than a finish line: the measurement that tells us whether the program delivered should outlast go-live.
  • Push AI tools further in how programs run: automating the reporting and tracking that doesn't need a human, building the workflows and frameworks that help teams across the program move faster, and evaluating and driving adoption of tools that raise efficiency across the department.
  • Ramp fast in unfamiliar domains: build the working relationships, learn enough of the system to ask the right questions, and earn credibility quickly when the teams are new to you.
  • Be the connective tissue across our Seattle and Barcelona teams, and shape Rover's TPM practice so each program runs better than the last: mentor TPMs, help lead hiring for the function, set patterns others adopt, and know when to introduce new department-level process (and when not to).

Your Qualifications

  • 11+ years driving complex, cross-functional technical programs.
  • A track record of owning several high-complexity, ambiguous programs at once, end to end, across domains, including ones new to you. Some you identified and stood up yourself; for others, your first deliverable was the scope.
  • A way of working through ambiguous situations rather than a tolerance for them: orienting quickly on incomplete or conflicting information, separating what's genuinely unknown from what simply hasn't been asked, and breaking a shapeless problem into parts people can start on before the full picture exists.
  • High agency in driving decisions rather than documenting them, and stellar alignment across organizational lines up to senior leadership, including shaping department priorities, strategy, and OKRs. You can hold a room of partners with competing incentives, know when to make the call and when to find who owns it, and leave with a shared plan.
  • Judgment under uncertainty, and the ability to explain it: when to force a decision and when to wait, when to escalate and when to absorb the risk yourself, when to hold the line on scope and when to let it move. You can point to calls you got right and calls you'd make differently now.
  • The technical acumen to be a true peer to engineering: reading a dependency chain, evaluating trade-offs without needing full translation, debating technical approaches, and finding where the real sequencing risk lives, where architectural patterns need to evolve, or where we're choosing one-way doors.
  • Strong core program management craft: standing up a plan and a status process, running a decision-making cadence, using metrics to surface risk early, show progress, and tell whether a program delivered after it shipped, and identifying what's missing in planning and execution before it costs the program. You're as comfortable speaking technically as non-technically, and can bridge between the two, including across globally distributed teams where decisions can't wait for everyone to be awake.
  • A history of making the people and practice around you better: mentoring TPMs or peers, interviewing and hiring, and building processes others adopt.
    A habit of pushing AI tools further in your work: automating repetitive tasks like status reporting or risk tracking, building custom workflows, or creating frameworks that help teams move faster.
    • You won't check every box on this list, and that's okay. If most of it sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

Nice to Have

  • Depth in more than one technical domain, for example platform and infrastructure alongside consumer product, payments, or data.
  • Experience at a marketplace, consumer tech, or SaaS company.

Benefits of Working at Rover.com

  • Competitive compensation
  • 401k match
  • Long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout
  • Flexible PTO
  • Competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Commuter benefits
  • Bring your dog to work (and unlimited puppy time)
  • Pet benefits, including $1000 toward adopting your first dog or cat
  • Stocked fridges, coffee, soda, and lots of treats (for humans and dogs) and free catered lunches monthly
  • Regular team activities performed in-person and virtually

Compensation

  • In the greater Seattle area the first-year salary range is $182,290 - 227,863. Additionally, Rover offers benefits to full-time employees.
  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.
At Rover, we’re driven by seeing our people succeed and grow, while doing our jobs better than ever before. We believe the best business outcomes come from a diverse set of perspectives and we’re committed to promoting an inclusive, inventive, and fun environment with amazing employees. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.
Rover is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, military or veteran status, sex, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital or partnership status, genetic predisposition, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws.
We are committed to work with you to look for reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

title: Software Engineer, Integrations (US + Calgary)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Software Engineer, Integrations (US + Calgary) based in the United States.

As a Software Engineer, Integrations, you will build and scale the data integration infrastructure that enables organizations to connect their systems and manage critical employee information reliably. You will design, develop, and optimize APIs, connectors, and automated workflows that power seamless data ingestion across enterprise platforms. Working across backend services, workflow orchestration, and customer-facing applications, you will help ensure data flows remain secure, accurate, and performant at scale. You will tackle complex integration challenges involving HRIS, payroll, ATS, and other business systems while improving error handling and troubleshooting experiences. In close collaboration with engineering, implementation, and customer success teams, you will turn real-world customer needs into scalable product capabilities. This remote-first opportunity offers meaningful technical ownership, cross-functional collaboration, and the chance to shape the future of enterprise data integration.

Accountabilities:

  • Design, develop, maintain, and optimize scalable integration platforms that enable secure and reliable data exchange across enterprise systems.
  • Build and manage native integrations, connectors, APIs, and automated workflows connecting HRIS, ATS, payroll, CRM, ERP, and other third-party applications.
  • Develop robust API integrations that account for authentication, pagination, rate limits, schema changes, partial failures, and other real-world challenges.
  • Improve data ingestion pipelines and workflow orchestration to support large customer datasets, optimize refresh times, and maintain reliability as data volumes grow.
  • Work across distributed systems and services, including Go-based APIs, Temporal workflows, Python transformation engines, and customer-facing frontend applications.
  • Design and implement effective error-handling, monitoring, retry, and recovery mechanisms that make integration failures easier to diagnose and resolve.
  • Improve customer-facing integration experiences by making data mappings, ingestion results, synchronization status, and error messages transparent and actionable.
  • Collaborate with Forward Deployed Engineering, Implementation, Customer Success, Product, and other engineering teams to understand customer requirements and expand platform capabilities.
  • Establish and maintain integration standards, technical documentation, reusable development patterns, and governance practices that support long-term scalability and maintainability.
  • Ensure sensitive employee and compensation data is handled securely, with appropriate attention to privacy, compliance, and data protection.
  • Investigate complex cross-system issues, trace data discrepancies through pipelines, and implement sustainable solutions that reduce recurring problems.
  • Contribute to technical decision-making and the long-term evolution of the integration platform while continuously improving development processes and product quality.

Requirements:

  • At least four years of experience building and shipping production software, with strong backend engineering fundamentals. Experience with Python and/or Go is preferred.
  • Hands-on experience developing and maintaining integrations with third-party APIs, including REST and SOAP services, webhooks, OAuth, API-key authentication, pagination, rate limiting, and upstream schema changes.
  • Experience designing or maintaining data pipelines and workflow orchestration, including scheduling, sequencing, retries, monitoring, and failure recovery across systems.
  • Strong SQL skills and the ability to understand data models, transformations, validation rules, and data quality challenges.
  • Familiarity with HRIS, ATS, CRM, or ERP platforms and their underlying data models, ideally through experience supporting enterprise implementations or customer onboarding.
  • Strong documentation skills and a commitment to making technical decisions, integration behavior, and troubleshooting procedures clear to other team members.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including Customer Success and Implementation teams.
  • A customer-focused engineering mindset, with an appreciation for the usability, reliability, and transparency of the products and systems you build.
  • A strong understanding of security, privacy, and compliance principles when handling sensitive employee or compensation information.
  • Comfort navigating unfamiliar technical environments, analyzing third-party documentation, tracing data issues across pipelines, and resolving ambiguous problems independently.
  • A collaborative and adaptable approach, demonstrating humility, curiosity, accountability, empathy, and a willingness to learn and grow.
  • The ability to build and maintain strong working relationships in a remote environment through proactive communication and intentional collaboration.
  • Preferred qualifications: Experience with frontend technologies such as TypeScript and React, integration platform as a service (iPaaS) tools such as Workato, Boomi, MuleSoft, Tray.io, or Celigo, and workflow orchestration engines such as Temporal or Airflow.
  • Additional advantages: Experience with large-scale file-based ingestion using SFTP, CSV, or flat-file pipelines, including data validation and error handling.
  • For candidates based in Calgary, the ability to work legally in Alberta without requiring current or future visa sponsorship is required.

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation: Annual target salary of $140,000–$160,000 USD for US-based employees, depending on experience, expertise, and other relevant factors.
  • Equity participation: Access to an equity program that allows eligible employees to share in the organization's long-term success.
  • Flexible time off: Flexible paid time off for US-based employees, with an emphasis on rest, personal well-being, and sustainable work habits.
  • Additional leave: Paid sick and safe time, compassionate leave, and voting leave.
  • Healthcare coverage: Additional private medical coverage, subject to applicable eligibility and plan terms.
  • Remote-first work environment: Work remotely within the designated eligible locations, with the role designed to support distributed collaboration.
  • Professional development: Opportunities to expand your expertise in APIs, data engineering, distributed systems, workflow orchestration, and enterprise integration technologies.
  • Technical ownership: The opportunity to influence integration architecture, establish engineering standards, and shape the evolution of a core data platform.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with engineering, product, implementation, and customer success teams to solve meaningful customer challenges.
  • Career progression: A structured initial development path, progressing from onboarding and smaller integration tasks to independently managing integrations, designing advanced architectures, and leading cross-functional initiatives.
  • Inclusive team culture: Join a collaborative environment that values curiosity, candor, community, continuous learning, and diverse perspectives.

Expected interview process:

  • Initial 30-minute phone conversation with a member of the Talent team.
  • 45–60-minute interview with the hiring manager.
  • 60-minute technical assessment involving pair programming.
  • 30-minute meeting with a Product team member.
  • Final 30-minute interview with an engineering leader.

description:
Job Title: Tool and Die Maker
Starting Pay Rate: $35.00/hour (Increases to $35.05/hour after 3 months and $36.000/hour after 6 months)
Schedule: Sunday-Thursday 11:00pm-7:00am, with mandatory overtime as needed
Reports To: Tool and Die Manager
Job Summary:We are seeking a skilled and motivated Tool and Die Maker to join our team. This role involves the maintenance, repair, and troubleshooting of stamping dies, and related equipment. The ideal candidate will demonstrate technical expertise, strong problem-solving skills, and a commitment to safety and quality.
Responsibilities:

Perform preventive maintenance and repair of stamping dies, and other support equipment.
Train apprentices in a four-year program, progressively delegating duties and responsibilities.
Read and interpret technical prints and use precision measuring tools.
Machine details using manual mills, lathes, surface grinders, drill presses, and saws.
Apply basic knowledge of 2 and 3-axis CNC mills.
Perform welding (TIG, MIG, ARC) and basic heat-treating processes, and rebuild nitrogen springs.
Understand die setups on presses, including tandem line and blanking operations.
Troubleshoot and repair stamping during production breakdowns.
Work in small or uncomfortable positions, including overhead reaching, during die repair inside presses.
Operates over head industrial cranes and forklifts

Ability to work an 8-hour shift with occasional overtime, including weekends. Shift includes two 10-minute breaks and a 20-minute meal break (paid). Employees get paid the entire time they are clocked in and do not clock out for breaks, if taken on campus!

Qualifications:

High school diploma or equivalent.
Tool Makers must provide their own tools
Proven experience in tool and die making, with a strong understanding of stamping dies and equipment.
Proficiency with manual machining tools and a basic understanding of CNC operations.
Welding skills (TIG, MIG, ARC) and knowledge of heat treating and nitrogen spring rebuilding.
Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to work under pressure during production breakdowns.
Crane operator and forklift certifications (or ability to obtain them).

Physical Demands:

Occasionally lift heavy items (up to 50 pounds), though most lifting involves less than 10 pounds.

Regularly required to stand, walk, use hands, reach above head and below shoulder level, and communicate effectively.
Exposure to moving mechanical parts, wet/humid conditions, fumes, airborne particles, and loud environments.
Occasional exposure to toxic or caustic chemicals and vibration.
Ability to work in a non- climate-controlled environment.

Work Environment:

The work environment is representative of conditions typical for a manufacturing facility. Guardian West is not a climate-controlled facility. Safety precautions must always be followed to reduce exposure to hazards.

Why Join Us?We offer a competitive pay rate, opportunities for skill development, and a dynamic work environment where your expertise as a Tool and Die Maker will directly contribute to the success of the team.

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in Finland.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                    • Additional qualifications considered an advantage

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Community credentials or roles such as CNCF Ambassador, AWS Community Builder, or Microsoft MVP.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

                      • Cloud certifications from providers such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.

                        • Benefits:

                        • Competitive fixed fee per course, agreed upfront based on course length and topic complexity, with higher compensation for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

                        • Paid freelance project that can be completed alongside an existing job, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement.

                        • A typical initial project duration of approximately three months, with a mutually agreed delivery plan.

                        • Potential to progress to a full-time role or take on additional course projects based on mutual fit.

                        • Fully remote working arrangements with flexible hours.

                        • Opportunity to collaborate with a global technical education team and reach a community of more than one million engineers.

                        • Dedicated production support for video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and course publishing, allowing you to focus on teaching and technical content.

                        • Opportunity to share your expertise in AI, DevOps, cloud, and Kubernetes through practical, hands-on education.

title: Senior Environmental Compliance Specialist
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Environmental Compliance Specialist based in the United States.

Take a leadership role in delivering environmental compliance for major energy, transmission, and infrastructure projects across the western United States. You will oversee construction-phase compliance programs, guide field inspection teams, and help ensure project activities meet environmental permits, regulatory requirements, and resource protection commitments. With a primary focus on a major transmission upgrade in southwestern Nevada, you will collaborate with contractors, developers, government agencies, and multidisciplinary environmental specialists. Your expertise will help protect sensitive ecosystems, including desert tortoise habitats, while supporting responsible infrastructure development. This role combines field leadership, regulatory coordination, client engagement, and project management in a dynamic consulting environment. It is an excellent opportunity for an experienced environmental professional who enjoys solving complex challenges, mentoring others, and contributing to sustainable project delivery.

Accountabilities

  • Lead environmental compliance programs for complex energy, transmission, utility, transportation, water, and infrastructure projects.

  • Serve as the senior field compliance lead for a major transmission upgrade project in southwestern Nevada, overseeing construction activities and environmental performance.

  • Supervise and coordinate environmental compliance inspectors, providing field guidance and ensuring consistent implementation of project requirements.

  • Monitor construction activities for compliance with environmental permits, mitigation measures, right-of-way conditions, and other environmental commitments.

  • Oversee implementation of biological resource protection measures, including those designed to protect desert tortoises and other sensitive species.

  • Coordinate with the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), authorized officers, developers, contractors, construction managers, and environmental teams.

  • Oversee compliance programs covering biological and cultural resources, stormwater management, erosion control, air quality, noise, restoration, and related environmental considerations.

  • Evaluate contractor performance, identify potential compliance issues, document field observations, and coordinate corrective actions.

  • Manage environmental compliance reports, audits, agency submissions, field records, and regulatory documentation.

  • Lead client discussions, construction coordination meetings, and regulatory consultations to resolve issues and maintain project alignment.

  • Support project managers, compliance specialists, and technical staff through mentoring, knowledge sharing, and practical guidance.

  • Contribute to project planning, proposal preparation, scopes of work, budget development, and business development initiatives.

  • Support additional environmental compliance assignments as needed across California, Nevada, and Arizona.

  • Maintain a strong commitment to safety, environmental stewardship, regulatory compliance, and high-quality project delivery.

    • Requirements:

    • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Ecology, Natural Resources, Environmental Planning, Archaeology, Anthropology, or a related discipline.

    • At least 10 years of experience in environmental compliance, permitting, regulatory oversight, and project management, preferably on major infrastructure, energy, transmission, utility, transportation, or water projects.

    • Demonstrated experience leading construction-phase environmental compliance programs and overseeing field personnel or compliance inspection teams.

    • Working knowledge of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Endangered Species Act, Clean Water Act, and other relevant environmental regulations.

    • Experience coordinating with the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) and other federal, state, and local regulatory agencies.

    • Ability to interpret permits, mitigation requirements, environmental commitments, and regulatory conditions and translate them into practical construction-phase procedures.

    • Strong project management, organizational, documentation, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify compliance risks and drive corrective actions.

    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with clients, contractors, agency representatives, and multidisciplinary teams.

    • Experience in client relationship management, proposal development, scope preparation, or business development.

    • Ability and willingness to travel regularly throughout California, Nevada, and Arizona, including field assignments lasting one to two weeks at a time.

    • Ability to work primarily onsite at project areas when required, with flexibility for a remote or hybrid arrangement depending on location and project needs.

    • Strong leadership and mentoring capabilities, with the judgment and professionalism to manage competing priorities in complex field environments.

    • A proactive, detail-oriented approach to environmental stewardship, safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.

      • Benefits:

      • Annual salary range: $80,000–$105,000 USD, as published for California pay transparency. Actual compensation may vary based on experience, education, skills, and work location.

      • Employee ownership, offering the opportunity to participate in the organization's long-term success.

      • Professional development opportunities to support continued learning and career growth.

      • Mentoring and leadership development opportunities.

      • Collaborative, multidisciplinary working environment focused on meaningful environmental solutions.

      • Opportunities to contribute to significant energy and infrastructure projects across the western United States.

      • Potential for remote or hybrid work arrangements, depending on location and project requirements.

      • Exposure to a variety of environmental compliance, permitting, restoration, and resource protection initiatives.

      • A workplace culture that values diversity, inclusion, mutual respect, and the contributions of different perspectives.

title: Manager, CyberSecurity Risk Management
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Manager, CyberSecurity Risk Management based in the United States.

In this role, you will help drive the execution and continuous improvement of an enterprise cybersecurity risk management program within a fast-paced technology environment. You will coordinate risk assessments, oversee remediation activities, and ensure cybersecurity risks are clearly documented, prioritized, and communicated to leadership. Working across Security, Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, Procurement, and Finance, you will help translate technical findings into actionable business insights. You will contribute to risk governance, compliance alignment, and data-driven reporting while supporting scalable processes and automation initiatives. The role combines hands-on program management with technical risk expertise and cross-functional collaboration. It offers the opportunity to strengthen organizational resilience while helping teams make informed, risk-based decisions in an evolving cloud and AI landscape.

Accountabilities

  • Cybersecurity Risk Program Management: Support day-to-day execution of the cybersecurity risk management program, coordinating assessments, remediation initiatives, timelines, dependencies, and deliverables across multiple teams.
  • Risk Assessment and Analysis: Conduct and support enterprise, technical, cloud, application, and third-party risk assessments. Evaluate inherent and residual risks, gather supporting evidence, validate security controls, and translate technical findings into clear business-impact statements.
  • Risk Register and Remediation Tracking: Maintain accurate risk registers, including ownership, status, target dates, treatment decisions, and mitigation plans. Follow up regularly with risk owners, monitor progress, resolve or escalate blockers, and drive remediation activities through closure.
  • Risk Governance and Reporting: Support risk committee meetings, risk acceptance processes, exception reviews, and escalation procedures. Prepare leadership updates, dashboards, and reports that communicate cybersecurity risk exposure, remediation progress, and emerging concerns.
  • Metrics and Risk Quantification: Collect and analyze key performance indicators (KPIs) and key risk indicators (KRIs), identify trends, and contribute to risk quantification efforts that help prioritize initiatives according to business and financial impact.
  • Compliance and Framework Alignment: Help map risk management activities to applicable regulatory obligations and industry frameworks, including ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, while monitoring emerging requirements such as DORA, NIS2, and the EU AI Act.
  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Collaborate with Security, Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, Procurement, and Finance to coordinate risk initiatives, align stakeholders, track decisions, and ensure timely delivery of remediation commitments.
  • Process Improvement and Automation: Support the implementation and adoption of governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) tools, standardized workflows, and automation solutions. Help pilot AI-enabled use cases, including risk intake triage, evidence mapping, and automated status summaries, with appropriate human oversight and governance.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify gaps in existing risk management processes and recommend improvements to assessment consistency, reporting accuracy, operational efficiency, and overall program effectiveness.

Requirements

  • Professional Experience: At least 8 years of experience in cybersecurity risk management or governance, risk, and compliance (GRC), including a minimum of 3 years in program or project management.
  • Program Management Expertise: Demonstrated ability to plan and coordinate cross-functional initiatives, manage dependencies and timelines, estimate effort, monitor deliverables, communicate status, and ensure accountability for results.
  • Cybersecurity Risk Management: Experience supporting or scaling a cybersecurity risk management program, preferably within a technology, SaaS, or cloud-based organization operating in a fast-paced environment.
  • Risk Methodologies and Frameworks: Working knowledge of risk management methodologies such as NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF), NIST SP 800-30, NIST SP 800-37, ISO 27005, and COBIT, along with security frameworks including ISO 27001/27002, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, CIS Controls, PCI DSS, and HIPAA.
  • Technical Security Knowledge: Sufficient understanding of cloud security, identity management, network security, and application security to engage effectively with engineering teams, assess technical risks, and follow remediation plans.
  • GRC Tools and Reporting: Hands-on experience with project management and reporting tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Tableau, with the ability to maintain risk documentation and communicate progress through structured reporting.
  • Analytical and Communication Skills: Strong analytical thinking, problem-solving, organization, and attention to detail, combined with excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to translate complex technical risks into business-relevant insights.
  • Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to influence stakeholders, build consensus, and coordinate initiatives across teams without relying on direct reporting authority.
  • Education: A bachelor's degree in Security, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

Benefits

  • Competitive Base Salary:
  • United States — San Francisco Bay Area, Washington, D.C. metro area, New York City, and Seattle: $181,600–$272,400 per year.
  • Other U.S. locations and remote positions: $163,400–$245,200 per year.
  • Additional Compensation: Eligibility for performance-based bonuses and equity, subject to the applicable compensation plan.
  • Remote Flexibility: Remote work opportunities within the United States.
  • Professional Growth: Opportunities to develop expertise in cybersecurity risk management, cloud security, regulatory compliance, and AI-enabled risk operations.
  • Collaborative Environment: Work with multidisciplinary teams across security, engineering, product, and business functions to strengthen enterprise security and resilience.
  • Meaningful Impact: Contribute to the protection of critical data, systems, and cloud environments while helping the organization manage evolving cybersecurity threats.
  • Inclusive Culture: Join an environment committed to equal opportunity, inclusion, professional development, and providing reasonable accommodations throughout employment and the application process.

title: Sr. Manager/Associate Director, Regulatory Writer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Sr. Manager/Associate Director, Regulatory Writer based in the United States.

We are seeking an experienced regulatory writing professional to lead the development and delivery of high-quality scientific and regulatory documentation across global clinical development programs. In this remote role, you will oversee document strategy, author complex regulatory submissions, and coordinate cross-functional contributors to support programs from initial clinical development through marketing applications and lifecycle management. You will partner with experts across Regulatory Affairs, Clinical Development, Biometrics, Safety, Nonclinical, and Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) to ensure scientific accuracy and regulatory compliance. As the primary writing lead for major submissions and health authority interactions, you will establish best practices, strengthen document quality, and maintain submission readiness. You will also mentor writers, manage external vendors, and improve processes that support efficient, consistent document delivery. This is an opportunity to influence global development strategies and contribute to advancing innovative therapies for patients with significant unmet medical needs.

Accountabilities:

  • Lead the planning, authoring, coordination, and delivery of regulatory documents supporting global development programs, health authority interactions, and marketing applications.

  • Develop strategic document plans aligned with regulatory milestones, submission timelines, and broader clinical development objectives.

  • Serve as the lead author for complex regulatory documents, including clinical protocols and amendments, Investigator’s Brochures (IBs), Clinical Study Reports (CSRs), briefing packages, Investigational New Drug (IND) applications, Clinical Trial Applications (CTAs), and health authority responses.

  • Prepare and coordinate additional regulatory deliverables, including Orphan Drug Designation applications, Pediatric Investigation Plans (PIPs), Pediatric Study Plans (PSPs), annual reports, and development updates.

  • Integrate scientific and clinical information across regulatory, clinical, nonclinical, safety, and CMC functions to ensure consistency, accuracy, and clarity throughout submission documentation.

  • Lead cross-functional document planning, review meetings, and content discussions, aligning subject matter experts and resolving issues that could affect quality or timelines.

  • Collaborate closely with Regulatory Affairs leadership to support global regulatory strategies, submission planning, and interactions with health authorities.

  • Represent Regulatory Writing in project teams and governance meetings, communicating document status, risks, and recommendations to relevant stakeholders.

  • Establish and maintain writing standards, templates, style guides, and document development procedures that promote consistency and inspection readiness.

  • Identify opportunities to improve writing workflows, review cycles, submission preparation, and overall operational efficiency.

  • Manage external medical writing vendors and contract writers, as needed, ensuring deliverables meet established quality standards and timelines.

  • Mentor junior writers and contribute to the development of organizational regulatory writing capabilities.

  • Coordinate document finalization and publishing activities for major submissions, ensuring compliance with applicable regulatory expectations.

  • Ensure regulatory documents align with relevant ICH guidelines, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and applicable FDA, EMA, PMDA, and other international requirements.

  • Support preparation for regulatory meetings and agency interactions through clear, scientifically rigorous documentation.

    • Requirements:

    • Bachelor's degree in life sciences or a related scientific discipline.

    • At least 10 years of medical writing or regulatory writing experience within biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or contract research organization (CRO) environments.

    • Demonstrated experience serving as lead writer for major regulatory documents and submissions.

    • Extensive hands-on experience authoring and coordinating clinical protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, Clinical Study Reports, regulatory briefing documents, IND and CTA submissions, and responses to health authority questions.

    • Strong knowledge of ICH guidelines, Good Clinical Practice, FDA and EMA requirements, and international regulatory standards.

    • Proven ability to independently manage multiple complex writing projects simultaneously while maintaining scientific quality, regulatory compliance, and delivery timelines.

    • Experience leading cross-functional teams through document planning, development, review, and finalization.

    • Excellent scientific writing, editing, analytical, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail and consistency.

    • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to facilitate technical discussions, resolve content disagreements, and align multidisciplinary teams.

    • Ability to establish effective writing processes, manage competing priorities, and exercise sound judgment in a dynamic development environment.

      • Preferred Qualifications:

      • Advanced degree in a scientific discipline, such as a PhD, PharmD, MD, or MS.

      • Certification from the American Medical Writers Association (AMWA).

      • Experience supporting Biologics License Applications (BLAs), Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs), or New Drug Applications (NDAs).

      • Experience in rare disease and pediatric drug development programs.

      • Experience supporting biologics development.

      • Experience managing external medical writing vendors, consultants, and contract writers.

You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. SUMMARY


Under regular supervision, Communications Officer II is responsible for communicating with and dispatching public safety personnel. Incumbents respond to the emergency and distress calls; dispatch public safety personnel/officers respond to inquiries by the public and other public safety agencies; interact with city, county, state, and federal public safety personnel; and maintain records of all dispatches. Assists in the on-the-job training of Communication Offer I employees, advise in daily activities, and act in the role of Team Lead in the absence of the Supervisor.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


THE ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS INCLUDE, BUT ARE NOT LIMITED TO, THE FOLLOWING DUTIES. ADDITIONAL ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS MAY BE IDENTIFIED BY THE CITY AND LISTED AS SUCH IN THE INCUMBENT’S PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL ELEMENTS. VARIOUS TASKS MAY BE ASSIGNED UNDER EACH ESSENTIAL FUNCTION. THOSE THAT ARE LISTED UNDER THE EXAMPLES OF WORK ARE NOT ALL INCLUSIVE; THEY ARE EXAMPLES ONLY AND MAY BE AMEDED OR ADDED TO AS NEEDED BY THE CITY.


EXAMPLES OF WORK


Examples of work performance in this classification include, but are not limited to, the following tasks. These tasks may be amended, or other tasks may be assigned as necessary.

  • Answer multiple incoming emergency 911 calls.
  • Answer multiple incoming calls to the police department on non-emergency lines and reroute calls to other personnel as needed.
  • Recognize TTY calls, emergency, and non-emergency, and effectively communicate with the caller.
  • Understand and respond quickly and accurately to written and/oral directions, instructions, inquiries, and requests.
  • Quickly evaluate and prioritize the urgency of calls.
  • Must utilize their training and maintain communications with caller while remaining calm, resolve situations, prioritize, and make decisions in multiple, highly stressful, and potentially deteriorating situations.
  • Question callers requesting dispatch to determine location of incident, nature of call, description of any suspects or suspect vehicles, appropriate personnel needed for the type of incident described, and phone number and name of caller.
  • Utilize special techniques to handle erratic and hostile callers when necessary.
  • Relay departmental SOP pre-arrival instructions to the caller
  • Connect emergency callers to other agencies or coordinate with other agencies when the incident does not involve our jurisdiction or other agencies/jurisdictions are involved in the incident.
  • Identifies the need to notify additional specialized resources such as Poison Control,
  • American Medical Response, etc.
  • Operates the phone system safely and reports any malfunction immediately to supervisor.


Radio Operator


  • Monitor radio traffic on patrol (police) frequencies, rescue (fire) frequencies, and county- wide police and fire frequencies.
  • Promptly respond to incoming incidents from radio traffic.
  • Dispatch appropriate personnel to emergency incidents inside and as required by mutual aid agreements, outside the city.
  • Maintain a clear, monotone, professional tone over all radio frequencies.
  • Monitor and respond to radio traffic during incident and act based upon information given by field personnel.
  • Advise officers and fire personnel of any safety issues of locations based upon previous call history.
  • Announces all points bulletins and other messages over the radio.
  • Conducts periodic welfare checks of field personnel during incidents to determine status.
  • Recognizes situational need to notify specific persons or agencies in emergency.
  • Operate radio equipment safely and report any malfunctions immediately to supervisor.

CAD (Computer-Aided Dispatch) Operator


  • Log information received from callers into the Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) system to streamline dispatch.
  • Verify CAD accuracy of street addresses, response pattern advised by CAD system, and beat location of described incidents for appropriate dispatch.
  • If CAD is unable to a validate location, Communications Officer must have a knowledge of jurisdiction including beat boundaries.
  • If CAD is unable to give proper unit assignment, the Communication Officer must assign the appropriate number and type of units to respond to the incident.
  • Add, update, or remove location alerts at various locations in the city based on need, call history, aggressive nature of residents, and other reasons as instructed by field personnel.
  • Review call histories at incident locations to improve officer safety and response efficiency.
  • Review suspects or caller information in arrest/report records for violent history, active warrants, or other information as needed by field personnel.
  • Maintain accurate logs of important information during emergency and non-emergency incidents.

NCIC (National Crime Information Computer) Operator


  • Query vehicle registration and/or driver’s license/person information for field personnel on traffic stops or other incidents; query III/criminal history information on persons; query wanted status of vehicles, persons, or property as requested by field personnel.
  • Advise patrol officers of required information for entry of persons or property as missing, wanted, or stolen, respectively, on the NCIC database.
  • Enter persons or property as missing, wanted, or stolen, respectively, on the NCIC database.
  • Respond to hit requests sent by other agencies on entered persons or property.
  • Coordinate patrol, investigations, and the administration to locate and recover persons or property as needed.
  • Always maintain security of the NCIC computer.
  • Maintain integrity of NCIC files entered or handled by the operator and any other persons who are allowed access to the files.
  • Maintain records for all III/criminal history requests by officers and investigators.


Deputy Court Clerk

  • Witness and sign uniform traffic citations as sworn by police officers.
  • Witness and sign affidavits as sword by police officers and/or complainants.
  • Receive cash bonds/fines after hours and issue proper receipts to the public.
  • Maintain security and accuracy of the cash drawer and any received moneys for bonds or fines paid.
  • Receive written bonds from bonds persons and send releases to holding facilities/jails as needed.
  • As requested by field personnel, contact judges to assign bonds for arrestees, and when applicable, arrange for housing of juvenile arrestees in the appropriate holding facility.
  • When requested, update bond information for inmates in holding facilities and advise those holding facilities of the new information.
  • Coordinate officers, investigators, and administrators to fulfill the requests of holding facilities in which we have housed an arrestee.

Other Duties


  • Contact off-duty personnel when directed by patrol supervisors for response to after- hours incidents.
  • Receive and dispatch after-hours calls for public works and the street department.
  • Keep records of library conference room activity and release the keys to persons renting the space.
  • Assist field personnel with searches or management of arrestees while in the police department as needed.
  • Advise supervisor(s) of any unsafe, illegal, or other harmful activity in the workplace which might compromise the police department or the safety of the public.
  • Must be flexible and adaptable with the ability to multitask during any incident.
  • Participate in scheduled training to maintain certification for state regulations.
  • Keep the integrity and confidentiality of all persons and/or information received.
  • Ability to work any shift, holidays, and weekends. Subject to on-call status.


OTHER REQUIREMENTS:

Have and maintain a valid Mississippi drivers’ license.

Have and present an honorable discharge from military service if applicable.

Have and present a High School diploma or GED.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

No supervisory responsibilities.

The above essential duties and responsibilities are representative of the major obligations of the position. Specific duties and responsibilities may vary based upon departmental needs. Other duties may be assigned to the above consistent with the knowledge, skills, and abilities required for the job. Not all the duties may be assigned to a position.


The City of Brandon, MS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, the city will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourages both prospective and current employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

title: National News Boats Reporter
description:
USATODAY Network is seeking a consumer-focused Boats Reporter to lead coverage for our new national Boats hub. This journalist will create compelling, useful and audience-driven content for people who are considering a boat purchase, enjoy life on the water or are deeply engaged with boats and boating culture.
We’re looking for a boating enthusiast with strong reporting instincts, multimedia storytelling skills and a deep understanding of how to serve three key audience segments:

Boat shoppers and buyers researching models, features, prices and purchasing decisions
Recreationists looking for accessible, practical and inspiring ways to enjoy boating and life on the water
Boating enthusiasts who closely follow new products, innovations, destinations, events and boating culture

This role supports USAT Networks' strategic goal of growing engaged audiences through high-quality, platform-optimized consumer coverage. The reporter will become a leading voice of the Boats hub, producing authoritative journalism while helping establish its identity, audience and programming across multiple platforms.
The reporter will work closely with editors, visual journalists and reporters across the USA TODAY Network to deliver timely, relevant and distinctive coverage. Video will be central to the role. The successful candidate must be comfortable appearing on camera, developing original video concepts and producing content from idea through publication.
This is a full-time, benefits-eligible position. The role is remote, though candidates may also be based in a USAT local market.
Responsibilities:

Report and write useful, engaging stories for boat shoppers, recreationists and enthusiasts
Develop authoritative buying guidance, product comparisons, explainers and other service journalism that helps consumers make informed decisions
Cover boating news, trends, innovations, destinations, events and culture
Generate original video concepts that complement the hub’s journalism and expand its reach
Report, shoot and produce platform-appropriate video, including on-camera segments, demonstrations, interviews and field reporting
Translate reporting into compelling visual stories for YouTube, social platforms and other video destinations
Pitch timely ideas based on news, seasonal interest, consumer demand, search behavior and audience data
Balance quick-turn coverage with enterprise reporting, distinctive features and recurring franchises
Create content optimized for search, social media, newsletters, video and other audience channels
Build and maintain relationships with boat manufacturers, dealers, industry experts, recreational organizations, boat owners and other relevant sources
Collaborate with journalists across the USA TODAY Network to identify local expertise, expand coverage and maximize reach
Help establish the hub’s editorial voice, coverage priorities and publishing rhythm
Monitor performance metrics and use the results to refine topics, formats, packaging and distribution

What you’ll need to thrive

A genuine passion for boats, boating and life on the water
Strong reporting, writing and news judgment
The ability to make boating approachable to newcomers without losing credibility with experienced enthusiasts
Confidence developing stories around consumer questions and real-world audience needs
Strong video instincts and comfort working both behind and in front of the camera
The ability to identify which ideas are best told through articles, videos, social content or a combination of formats
Familiarity with SEO, social media best practices and audience analytics
Clear, concise writing that avoids unnecessary jargon
An energetic and creative approach to building a new editorial product
The ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across a distributed newsroom
Sound judgment when reporting in marinas, on boats and around the water

Requirements

Proven experience in journalism, digital media, video production or a related content field
Excellent reporting, writing, communication and organizational skills
Demonstrated experience creating original video content
Experience shooting and producing video in field environments
Comfort appearing on camera and conducting on-camera interviews
Ability to manage multiple stories and formats in a fast-paced environment
Understanding of audience strategy and digital publishing
Employment is contingent on passing a post-offer, pre-employment background check

Preferred qualifications

Experience covering boats, outdoor recreation, travel, consumer products or a related subject
Demonstrated knowledge of boats and boating culture
Experience with video editing and YouTube programming
Experience producing product reviews, demonstrations or comparison content
Familiarity with consumer buying journeys, affiliate-supported content or commerce journalism
Knowledge of newsletter strategy and performance metrics
Experience using audience data to identify and develop coverage opportunities

How success will be measured

Growth in engaged audience across shoppers, recreationists and enthusiasts
Development of a consistent and recognizable voice for the Boats hub
Performance of original video across relevant platforms
Search, social and direct audience growth
Growth in repeat visitation and audience loyalty
Timeliness, usefulness and distinctiveness of coverage
Development of successful recurring topics, formats and franchises
Effective collaboration with journalists across the USA TODAY Network
Use of performance insights to improve coverage and distribution

Application instructions
We’re eager to learn more about you and how you would build an ambitious, consumer-focused Boats hub. When applying, please upload a single PDF document that includes:

Your resume
A cover letter explaining your approach to serving boat shoppers, recreationists and enthusiasts
Links to three to six examples of your reporting, video or other digital work
A brief description of one story or video franchise you would launch for the Boats hub

It is important that these items be assembled into a single document and uploaded in PDF format. Completing these steps will ensure that your application receives the highest consideration.

title: Hybrid Data Platform Engineer | Snowflake & CI/CD
description:

$120,000 - $130,000 a year

Contract, Full time

Hybrid

10d ago , from Victorian Managed Insurance Authority (VMIA)

Victorian Managed Insurance Authority (VMIA)

Work Type – Full Time, Fixed-term contract until 30th June 2027

Key highlights

Hybrid work environment – Enjoy a mix of office and flexible work arrangements, fostering connection and strengthening networks. The majority of your working week will be in our collaborative office environment.

About the role

VMIA is the Victorian Government’s insurer and risk adviser, covering the people, places and projects that help Victorians thrive.

As our Data Platform Engineer, you’ll help build and maintain the infrastructure that supports VMIA’s data and digital initiatives. You’ll write clean, maintainable code, develop clear documentation and support the deployment of secure, reliable data infrastructure.

Working within the Data and Analytics team in the Business Performance Division, you’ll gain hands-on experience in software engineering, data governance and enterprise data platforms, with guidance from experienced data professionals.

Key responsibilities

Help build and maintain Snowflake databases, schemas, warehouses, tables and stored procedures using Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Pulumi or Terraform.

Write Python and SQL to support deployment scripts, stored procedures and data ingestion pipelines.

Assist with consistent, repeatable deployments across development, test and production environments.

Contribute to platform configurations using YAML and JSON.

Implement and maintain role-based access controls, including role hierarchies, permissions and access policies, under senior guidance.

Support infrastructure configuration to improve platform scalability, security and cost control.

Write and maintain automated tests and help support and troubleshoot continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines.

Use Git and GitHub to contribute through branching, code reviews and pull requests.

Maintain clear documentation, identify and escalate risks or issues, and follow relevant policies and controls.

What we are looking for

You’re curious about how systems work and keen to build your career in data platform engineering. You bring an analytical approach, attention to detail and a willingness to learn.

You’ll have:

Exposure to relational databases and SQL through study, projects, internships or personal learning.

Exposure to Python, including data structures, scripting and structured data formats such as JSON and YAML.

Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down unclear or complex problems into manageable questions.

Strong written communication skills, particularly when documenting technical work.

Practical experience through internships, projects or work in software engineering, software development, data engineering or data modelling.

Familiarity with software engineering practices such as automated testing, code reviews and CI/CD.

Familiarity with version control tools such as Git, and collaboration tools such as Jira and Confluence.

An understanding of APIs and common data formats, including JSON, CSV and XML.

A collaborative approach, openness to feedback and commitment to continuous improvement.

At VMIA, we believe diversity drives innovation. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and empowered to contribute their unique perspectives.

Flex work: Hybrid working to support your best performance.

VMIA encourages applications from candidates of all backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, individuals with disabilities, culturally diverse communities, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

We invite you to submit your CV and a cover letter. Use these to introduce yourself, highlight your fit for the role, and share why you are excited about joining VMIA. For any questions about the role or application process, please contact us at***************@vmia.vic.gov.au.

If you have any accessibility needs during the recruitment process, please let us know at***************@vmia.vic.gov.au.

title: Senior Cloud Security Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Cloud Security Engineer based in the United States.

We are seeking an experienced cloud security professional to strengthen the security, resilience, and compliance of modern cloud-based healthcare platforms. In this role, you will lead the design and continuous improvement of secure AWS environments while protecting sensitive patient information and supporting advanced AI-driven technologies. You will establish security architectures, implement Zero Trust principles, and integrate automated controls across cloud infrastructure and software delivery pipelines. Working closely with engineering, data science, compliance, and enterprise technology teams, you will address emerging risks associated with machine learning, generative AI, and autonomous AI systems. You will also drive threat detection, incident response, and regulatory readiness while mentoring colleagues and promoting security best practices. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact at the intersection of healthcare innovation, cloud engineering, and next-generation AI security in a remote-friendly environment.

Accountabilities

  • Design secure cloud architectures: Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of secure AWS environments, ensuring infrastructure and applications meet organizational security standards.

  • Establish security guardrails: Develop and enforce cloud security policies and standards covering identity and access management (IAM), network segmentation, encryption, logging, and other critical controls.

  • Implement Zero Trust principles: Apply Zero Trust architecture across cloud-native systems, user endpoints, identity workflows, and access management processes.

  • Secure cloud workloads: Protect containerized and serverless environments, including Kubernetes, Docker, Amazon ECS, and AWS Lambda, and assess existing implementations to prioritize remediation of security weaknesses.

  • Strengthen workforce security: Improve endpoint security, identity lifecycle management, privileged access management (PAM), and secure virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) supporting access to protected health information (PHI).

  • Secure AI and machine learning systems: Define security controls for AI/ML and generative AI applications, addressing threats such as prompt injection, model poisoning, data leakage, and adversarial attacks.

  • Protect autonomous AI workflows: Develop security approaches for agentic AI systems, including autonomous workflows and decision-making agents, and collaborate with data science teams to embed security throughout the model development lifecycle through MLSecOps practices.

  • Support regulatory compliance and risk management: Partner with governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) teams to maintain alignment with HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, and other applicable requirements.

  • Conduct security assessments: Perform threat modeling and risk assessments across cloud infrastructure and AI systems, document findings, and support audits and compliance initiatives.

  • Improve detection and incident response: Implement and optimize security monitoring and detection capabilities using SIEM, cloud security posture management (CSPM), and cloud workload protection platforms (CWPP). Develop automated remediation workflows and support incident response for cloud security events.

  • Integrate security into development: Apply static application security testing (SAST), dynamic application security testing (DAST), and software composition analysis (SCA), including appropriate use of AI-assisted coding tools.

  • Automate security controls: Integrate security scanning, policy enforcement, and compliance checks into CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code workflows using tools such as Terraform and CloudFormation.

  • Promote DevSecOps practices: Work closely with engineering teams to embed security early in the software development lifecycle and reduce vulnerabilities before deployment.

  • Mentor and influence teams: Guide engineers and security analysts, share technical expertise, and encourage consistent adoption of security best practices across the organization.

  • Monitor emerging threats: Stay informed about evolving cloud, cybersecurity, and AI-related risks, translating new developments into practical security improvements.

  • Collaborate across functions: Partner with product, engineering, people operations, enterprise systems, data science, and external stakeholders to support business objectives and security priorities.

    • Requirements:

    • Education: Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. A master's degree in a relevant discipline is desirable.

    • Professional experience: At least five years of experience in cloud security or cybersecurity engineering, with hands-on responsibility for designing, implementing, and improving security controls.

    • AWS expertise: Strong practical experience securing AWS services and applying cloud security principles across identity management, networking, encryption, logging, and infrastructure protection.

    • Cloud-native security: Solid understanding of containerized environments, including Kubernetes and Docker, as well as serverless architectures and cloud-native application security.

    • Regulated environments: Strong knowledge of security and compliance requirements in regulated industries, particularly HIPAA, HITRUST, and SOC 2.

    • Zero Trust architecture: Experience implementing Zero Trust principles across cloud infrastructure, endpoints, identity, and access controls.

    • AI security knowledge: Experience identifying and mitigating security risks associated with AI technologies, including machine learning, generative AI, and emerging autonomous AI systems.

    • DevSecOps and automation: Demonstrated ability to automate security controls and integrate security testing into CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code workflows.

    • Programming and scripting: Proficiency in at least one programming or scripting language, with familiarity with Python, Java, Node.js, or C#.

    • Application security testing: Hands-on experience with SAST, DAST, and SCA tools, along with an understanding of how AI-assisted coding tools affect software security.

    • Security monitoring and response: Knowledge of cloud security monitoring, threat detection, vulnerability remediation, and incident response processes.

    • Security certifications: CISSP, CCSP, AWS security certifications, or comparable credentials are highly desirable.

    • Technical leadership: Ability to guide and influence engineers, security analysts, and other technical professionals without necessarily having direct managerial authority.

    • Communication and collaboration: Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex security issues and collaborate effectively across technical and business teams.

    • Problem-solving and adaptability: Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, prioritization, motivation, and the ability to respond effectively to evolving security challenges.

    • Travel availability: Willingness to travel occasionally to the organization's Tennessee offices for training.

    • Work authorization: Must already be authorized to work in the United States on a full-time, permanent basis without requiring current or future visa sponsorship.

    • Pre-employment screening: Successful completion of a background check is required due to access to sensitive information, including proprietary data and protected health information.

      • Benefits:

      • Medical, dental, and vision insurance to support employee health and well-being.

      • 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching to help employees plan for the future.

      • Flexible paid time off to support work-life balance.

      • Paid parental leave for eligible employees.

      • Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options to help manage eligible healthcare expenses.

      • Educational reimbursement program to support continued learning and professional development.

      • Employer-paid Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental health services.

      • Remote work opportunity within the United States, with occasional travel to Tennessee for training.

      • Meaningful technical impact: The opportunity to strengthen security for AI-enabled healthcare technology and help protect sensitive patient data.

      • Professional growth: Exposure to cloud security architecture, emerging AI threats, regulated healthcare environments, and cross-functional technical leadership.

The associate is responsible for following established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), cleaning schedules, safety requirements, and applicable pharmacy standards.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform routine cleaning and sanitization of the non-sterile compounding laboratory and designated support areas according to established SOPs and cleaning schedules.
  • Perform daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and other scheduled cleaning activities as required.
  • Perform scheduled deep cleaning of the non-sterile compounding laboratory.
  • Clean floors, walls, doors, work surfaces, shelving, carts, sinks, and other designated laboratory surfaces.
  • Wash, rinse, sanitize, dry, and appropriately store reusable compounding utensils, glassware, containers, and equipment according to established procedures.
  • Maintain laboratory dishwashing and cleaning areas in a clean, organized, and sanitary condition.
  • Clean designated compounding equipment and external equipment surfaces according to established procedures.
  • Use approved cleaning agents, detergents, sanitizers, and other cleaning materials according to established procedures, including required dilution and contact times when applicable.
  • Follow established cleaning techniques and procedures designed to minimize contamination and cross-contamination.
  • Maintain cleaning tools and supplies in designated locations and ensure cleaning materials are properly stored and labeled.
