  • Collect, segregate, and dispose of laboratory waste according to established procedures.
  • Complete cleaning logs and other required documentation accurately and at the time the activity is performed.
  • Immediately report spills, residues, damaged surfaces, pest activity, water intrusion, equipment issues, or other conditions that could affect the cleanliness or suitability of the compounding environment.
  • Follow applicable procedures for the cleanup of spills involving pharmaceutical ingredients or compounded preparations.
  • Wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) and comply with laboratory entry, safety, hygiene, and personnel requirements.
  • Follow applicable Safety Data Sheets (SDS), chemical-handling requirements, and workplace safety procedures.
  • Coordinate cleaning activities with compounding personnel to minimize disruption to production activities.
  • Support laboratory cleaning activities following maintenance, repairs, spills, or other events requiring additional cleaning.
  • Report missed cleaning activities, cleaning deficiencies, or other deviations promptly to the supervisor.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe working environment.
  • Complete required training and competency assessments before independently performing assigned duties.
  • Perform other cleaning, sanitation, organization, and laboratory-support duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to follow written cleaning procedures, SOPs, safety instructions, and established cleaning schedules.
  • Ability to maintain accurate and complete cleaning records.
  • Ability to consistently follow contamination and cross-contamination prevention practices.
  • Ability to safely use cleaning chemicals and cleaning equipment.
  • Ability to identify and promptly report abnormal or potentially unsafe conditions.
  • Ability to manage multiple cleaning responsibilities in a fast-paced pharmacy environment.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision after completion of required training.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • Dependable, punctual, and able to complete assigned cleaning activities within established timeframes.

title: Mid level Agentic AI Engineer
description:
About the Role

You will design, build, and operate production-grade multi-agent systems for commercial and federal customers. The work spans the LangChain ecosystem, reliable agent loops, advanced retrieval architectures, and ontologies that ground agent reasoning.

You will also connect agents to enterprise tools and to each other through MCP and A2A. This role suits an engineer who thinks in systems: how agents reason, retrieve, act, recover from failure, and get evaluated and observed in production.

Key Responsibilities

Agent development and orchestration

  • Build single- and multi-agent applications with LangChain and LangGraph, including stateful graphs, supervisor/worker and hierarchical patterns, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
  • Engineer robust agentic loops (plan, act, observe, reflect) with clear termination conditions, retry and self-correction logic, guardrails, and cost and latency budgets.
  • Apply loop engineering to tune iteration depth, tool-call strategy, memory handling, and state persistence so agents behave predictably.
  • Use LangSmith for tracing, debugging, prompt and dataset management, and automated evaluation; maintain regression suites for agent behavior.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

  • Build and optimize Agentic RAG (agent-driven query planning and iterative retrieval), Adaptive RAG (routing by query complexity), Corrective and Self-RAG, GraphRAG (knowledge-graph retrieval and reasoning), and Cache-Augmented Generation with semantic caching.
  • Design chunking, embedding, hybrid search, re-ranking, and query-rewriting strategies.
  • Measure retrieval quality with faithfulness, context precision and recall, and answer relevance.

Ontologies, context, and skills

  • Develop domain ontologies and knowledge graphs (OWL/RDF or property-graph models) that ground agent reasoning and power GraphRAG.
  • Practice context engineering: decide how instructions, memory, retrieved knowledge, and tool results are assembled in the context window.
  • Build reusable agent skills and tool libraries with clear interfaces, documentation, and versioning.

Interoperability protocols

  • Build and integrate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and clients that expose enterprise data, APIs, and tools to agents securely.
  • Implement Agent-to-Agent (A2A) patterns for agent discovery, capability negotiation, task delegation, and cross-vendor communication.

Engineering and delivery

  • Write production-quality Python (TypeScript optional) with tests, CI/CD, and secure coding practices.
  • Take agents from prototype to production with product, data, and platform teams.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions, code reviews, and internal standards for agentic systems.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 10 years of software engineering, with at least 4 years building LLM-powered applications.
  • Hands-on production experience with LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith.
  • Demonstrated experience designing agentic loops, tool calling, memory, and multi-agent orchestration.
  • Practical experience implementing several RAG variants (Agentic, Adaptive, GraphRAG, Cache RAG/CAG) and evaluating their quality.
  • Experience designing ontologies or knowledge graphs and applying them to retrieval or reasoning.
  • Strong context engineering and prompt design for complex agent workflows.
  • Experience building or integrating MCP servers and clients, and working knowledge of the A2A protocol.
  • Proficiency in Python, REST/gRPC APIs, and asynchronous programming.
  • Solid grasp of LLM failure modes (hallucination, prompt injection, context limits) and their mitigations.

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in United Kingdom.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                    • Additional qualifications considered an advantage

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Community credentials or roles such as CNCF Ambassador, AWS Community Builder, or Microsoft MVP.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

                      • Cloud certifications from providers such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.

                        • Benefits:

                        • Competitive fixed fee per course, agreed upfront based on course length and topic complexity, with higher compensation for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

                        • Paid freelance project that can be completed alongside an existing job, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement.

                        • A typical initial project duration of approximately three months, with a mutually agreed delivery plan.

                        • Potential to progress to a full-time role or take on additional course projects based on mutual fit.

                        • Fully remote working arrangements with flexible hours.

                        • Opportunity to collaborate with a global technical education team and reach a community of more than one million engineers.

                        • Dedicated production support for video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and course publishing, allowing you to focus on teaching and technical content.

                        • Opportunity to share your expertise in AI, DevOps, cloud, and Kubernetes through practical, hands-on education.

title: Collections Fellow - Grant Funded
company: Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
description:
ABOUT PAFA

Founded in 1805, the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts (PAFA) is America's first museum and school of fine arts. Located in center city Philadelphia, PAFA is intimate in scale with a strong sense of community. PAFA offers a certificate in studio art. PAFA's museum has an outstanding collection of American art, and the museum actively collects and exhibits art, including work in new media. Additionally, PAFA is home to the Brodsky Center, a print and papermaking center focused on the creation of innovative editions by contemporary artists.

PAFA is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to an environment that welcomes and encourages recruiting and retaining qualified candidates from diverse groups. PAFA provides equal opportunity to applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability, or status as a veteran.

POSITION: Collections Fellow

PAFA is accepting applications for a Collections Fellow, a part-time temporary, grant funded position designed for early-career museum professionals, recent college graduates, and current graduate students interested in gaining experience in collections care, management, and refinement. Working closely with PAFA curators, registrars, and collections managers, the Collections Fellow will receive training in Axiell, a collections management database used widely by museums and will develop areas of personal interest within the fields of collections research, care, maintenance, and refinement. There will be opportunities for the Collections Fellow to participate in a wide range of activities in the day-to-day operations of a museum and to meet with other fellows supported in the same grant funded cohort at different local cultural organizations. The Collections Fellow will report to PAFA's Director of Archives, Library, Collections.

  • This is a part-time temporary position. The position is not eligible for PAFA employee benefits.
  • The fellow will work 20 hours per week from January 2027 through December 2027.
  • Compensation is $20 per hour/ $400 per week.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities and opportunities include but are not limited to the following:

PAFA Permanent Collection – 75%

  • Provide research and administrative support to PAFA's museum team for ongoing collections assessment, care, and refinement.
  • Prepare condition reports, review catalogued works of art, conduct research and verify provenance information, exhibition histories, and bibliographic references, as well as document critical opinions found in literature.
  • Prepare and edit reports, presentations and other supporting materials.
  • Assist in scheduling collections meetings with the PAFA project team and act as liaison with other PAFA departments.
  • Other duties pertaining to PAFA collections as assigned.

John Rhoden Collection – 25%

  • Provide research and administrative support to PAFA's museum team for the distribution of sculpture from the John Rhoden Collection.
  • Assist in the preparation and mailing of collection informational packets, checklists, and other materials as required.
  • Maintain the sculpture inventory and distribution information in PAFA's collection management database.
  • Finalize the distribution timeline of sculptures by John Rhoden to other museums by coordinating checklists, travel, and organizing correspondence with curators and registrars.
  • Prepare and edit correspondence, reports and presentations.
  • Assist with travel arrangements for visiting museum colleagues and the preparation and submission of expense reports.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree required, master's degree in art history or related field preferred
  • Museum, gallery, or other related experience preferred
  • Basic computer skills, including the use of Microsoft Office Suite required
  • Scholarly research databases, collection management databases and photo editing software skills preferred
  • Excellent interpersonal, written communication and research skills
  • Excellent organizational skills: ability to multi-task and meet deadlines
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Ability to work collaboratively as well as independently

APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS

The Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts accepts digital applications only. A complete application should include the following:

  • Resume
  • Cover Letter

When submitting your application online, please save your documents as Microsoft Word (.doc, .docx) or PDF (.pdf) files. To help us process your applications as efficiently as possible, please save your files with the following filename format:

  • LastName_FirstName_Resume
  • LastName_FirstName_CoverLetter

title: DevOps Engineer / Mid- Senior level
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a DevOps Engineer / Mid–Senior Level based in the United States.

We are seeking an experienced DevOps Engineer to lead enterprise-wide source control, release engineering, and CI/CD platform standardization in a mission-critical technology environment. In this role, you will shape the strategy for secure, scalable, and auditable software delivery while consolidating fragmented Git platforms into a unified enterprise foundation. You will design and maintain automated build, test, security, and deployment workflows, alongside shared platform services for container registries, object storage, and secrets management. Working closely with engineering, cybersecurity, IT, and platform teams, you will establish best practices that improve reliability, consistency, and developer productivity. This is a hands-on technical leadership opportunity for someone who combines deep platform expertise with strong governance and automation skills. The position is fully remote and supports technology initiatives where security, operational excellence, and mission impact are paramount.

Accountabilities:

  • Define and own the enterprise source control strategy, including platform architecture, governance standards, technical direction, and long-term roadmaps.

  • Lead large-scale Git platform consolidation and repository migration initiatives, standardizing fragmented and legacy environments on approved enterprise platforms.

  • Administer GitHub Enterprise Cloud and Server, GitLab SaaS and self-hosted environments, repository structures, access permissions, branch protection, and code review workflows.

  • Integrate source control platforms with identity and access management systems, including Okta, Active Directory, single sign-on (SSO), and SCIM-based user provisioning and deprovisioning.

  • Design, build, maintain, and optimize CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Azure DevOps Pipelines, and other relevant automation tools.

  • Develop reusable pipeline templates and shared workflow libraries that enable standardized, automated builds, testing, security scanning, and deployments across development, staging, and production environments.

  • Deploy and operate enterprise-wide container registry services, such as Harbor, to manage, scan, and distribute container images while consolidating team-specific solutions.

  • Establish and maintain shared S3-compatible object storage services, such as MinIO, for build artifacts, test data, and engineering files.

  • Own centralized secrets management platforms, such as HashiCorp Vault or equivalent solutions, providing secure and consistent secrets handling across pipelines, applications, and infrastructure automation.

  • Define and enforce access controls, retention policies, backups, disaster recovery procedures, and operational standards for shared platform services.

  • Develop and maintain infrastructure-as-code using Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, and related tools; create automation using Python, PowerShell, and Bash.

  • Support Docker-based workflows and Kubernetes-enabled build and deployment pipelines.

  • Partner with cybersecurity and compliance teams to implement audit logging, access reviews, compliance reporting, and security controls across source control and delivery platforms.

  • Integrate static and dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST) and dependency scanning into CI/CD workflows.

  • Monitor platform health, pipeline performance, infrastructure reliability, security events, and compute costs; implement proactive alerting and self-healing mechanisms where appropriate.

  • Collaborate with engineering, data, IT, and platform teams to translate business and technical needs into scalable developer tooling solutions.

  • Maintain technical documentation, platform standards, operational runbooks, and pipeline guidance; serve as a technical escalation point for Git and CI/CD issues.

  • Participate in architecture reviews, sprint-based delivery, cross-functional planning, and roadmap development, with occasional after-hours support for maintenance, migrations, and incident response.

    • Requirements:

    • Hold and maintain an active Secret security clearance upon hire.

    • Be a U.S. Person, defined for applicable export-control purposes as a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or protected individual under relevant U.S. law, and be eligible to obtain any required export authorizations.

    • Have a bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

    • Bring approximately 10–12 years of experience in DevOps, platform engineering, site reliability engineering, or a closely related discipline.

    • Demonstrate hands-on enterprise-scale administration experience with both GitLab and GitHub, including platform configuration, repository management, access controls, and governance.

    • Have substantial experience designing, implementing, and operating CI/CD pipelines across multiple teams, environments, and software delivery workflows.

title: Treatment Coordinator
description:
Treatment Coordinator

ORVAC - Northwest Arkansas

Full-Time, In-Person · Monday–Thursday,7:00am–5:30pm · Base Salary + Performance Incentives

About Us

Ozark Regional Vein & Artery Center (ORVAC) - named 2025 Best of Northwest Arkansas: Vein Center - along with our affiliated clinics Renew Aesthetics (Best Weight Loss Clinic) and The Edge Men's Health (Best Men's Clinic), is a growing, award-winning group of practices built around personalized, root-cause healthcare. We're looking for a reliable, detail-oriented Treatment Coordinator to help our patients move confidently from a treatment recommendation to scheduled care.

The Role

As our Treatment Coordinator, you'll pick up where the consultation leaves off. Once a patient has come in for their appointment and a provider has recommended treatment, you're the person who takes it from there -

walking them through their insurance benefits where applicable, answering questions about cost and coverage, and getting their treatment appointment on the calendar. You'll be a calm, knowledgeable guide at a pivotal moment in a patient's care, helping them feel confident about moving forward.

What This Role Does

This is a back-end, patient-facing role focused on turning a treatment recommendation into a scheduled, committed patient. You'll work closely with our clinical teams and Client Concierge staff to make sure nothing falls through the cracks between consultation and care.

  • Explain insurance benefits to patients where applicable, breaking down coverage, out-of-pocket costs, and payment options in clear, understandable terms.
  • Present treatment plans and pricing with confidence, helping patients understand their options and next steps.
  • Schedule treatment appointments promptly after a recommendation is made, keeping patients moving forward in their care.
  • Follow up with patients who haven't yet scheduled, helping them take the next step and re-engaging those who've paused.

What You'll Do

  • Meet with patients following their consultation to review the provider's recommended treatment plan.
  • Verify and explain insurance benefits where applicable, providing clear breakdowns of coverage, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs.
  • Present pricing, packages, and financing options clearly and confidently, answering questions and addressing concerns.
  • Schedule treatment appointments and coordinate logistics across providers and locations.
  • Maintain accurate records of treatment plans, conversations, and follow-ups in our CRM/EMR systems.
  • Conduct proactive follow-up with patients who have not yet scheduled their recommended treatment.
  • Re-engage patients who have delayed or paused care, helping them get back on track.
  • Collaborate closely with providers and Client Concierge staff to ensure a seamless handoff from consultation to treatment.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, especially when discussing cost and coverage.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication.
  • A warm, professional presence that puts patients at ease when talking about money or insurance.
  • High emotional intelligence and empathy.
  • Attention to detail and a process-oriented mindset - nothing falls through the cracks.
  • A confident, empathetic approach to helping patients say yes to care, without being pushy.
  • Comfort learning practice management, CRM, and insurance verification tools.
  • Experience with medical billing, insurance verification, patient financial counseling, or healthcare sales is a plus.
  • Interest in holistic or functional medicine principles is a plus.
  • Bi-lingual in Spanish is highly preferred.

Schedule & Compensation

  • Full-time, in-person role supporting multiple clinic locations in Northwest Arkansas
  • Monday–Thursday, 7:00am–5:30pm (some flexibility may be needed based on business needs)
  • Base Pay $18+ DOE, plus performance incentives tied to increased conversion rates
  • 401(k)
  • Health, dental, vision, and other great benefits
  • Paid time off

Why Join Us

  • Be part of an award-winning, growing group of clinics
  • Work in a collaborative, supportive environment with real access to leadership
  • Room to grow - we invest in our high performers

Ready to join our team? We'd love to hear from you - apply today!

title: Information System Security Officer (ISSO) – Intermediate
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Information System Security Officer (ISSO) – Intermediate based in the United States.

As an Intermediate Information System Security Officer, you will help safeguard cloud-based and classified information systems by managing security compliance, risk assessments, and authorization activities. You will play a key role in maintaining secure operational environments aligned with federal cybersecurity standards, including NIST SP 800-53, FedRAMP, and the Risk Management Framework (RMF). Working alongside senior security professionals, engineering teams, and external assessors, you will support system authorization, continuous monitoring, and vulnerability remediation. You will contribute to integrating security controls into cloud infrastructure and DevSecOps practices while ensuring that evolving regulatory requirements are met. Through effective risk management, detailed documentation, and cross-functional collaboration, you will help protect sensitive information and support mission-critical operations. This fully remote opportunity offers the chance to contribute to complex cybersecurity initiatives within a collaborative, security-focused environment.

Accountabilities:

  • Support the information assurance program for assigned information systems, programs, and security enclaves, ensuring compliance with applicable federal cybersecurity policies and standards.
  • Develop, review, implement, and maintain information system security policies, procedures, standards, and methodologies in alignment with organizational and regulatory requirements.
  • Prepare and maintain Risk Management Framework (RMF) documentation, including System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Plans (SAPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), Risk Assessment Reports, System Requirements Traceability Matrices (SRTMs), FedRAMP appendices, and continuous monitoring strategies.
  • Support system authorization and reauthorization activities across RMF Steps 1–6, helping obtain and maintain Authorization to Operate (ATO) approvals for assigned systems.
  • Monitor and maintain the operational security posture of cloud-based and classified systems, working under the guidance of senior ISSOs and the Information System Security Manager (ISSM).
  • Conduct vulnerability assessments, analyze security risks, evaluate control effectiveness, and recommend remediation actions to support authorization and ongoing compliance.
  • Coordinate with Third-Party Assessment Organizations (3PAOs), federal agencies, commercial customers, and internal stakeholders during security assessments, audits, and authorization reviews.
  • Support continuous monitoring activities by tracking vulnerabilities, documenting findings, updating POA&Ms, and ensuring timely remediation and reporting.
  • Assist with security incident response, collaborating with incident response teams to investigate events and ensure compliance with relevant security controls.
  • Partner with cloud engineering and cross-functional technical teams to implement, validate, and maintain security controls across cloud environments and DevSecOps workflows.
  • Review significant change requests, assess their potential security impact, and document required updates to system security controls and authorization artifacts.
  • Evaluate security solutions to determine their suitability for processing classified or sensitive information and verify alignment with applicable cybersecurity requirements.
  • Engage with customers, technical teams, and cybersecurity stakeholders to define security objectives, resolve compliance issues, and maintain alignment with evolving federal security requirements.

Requirements:

  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance.
  • At least five years of professional cybersecurity experience, including a minimum of two years working as an Information System Security Officer in a cloud, federal government, Department of Defense (DoD), or Intelligence Community environment.
  • Working knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5, FedRAMP Moderate and High baselines, and federal cybersecurity compliance frameworks.
  • Practical experience with the Risk Management Framework, including system authorization processes, authorization maintenance, and preparation of SSPs, POA&Ms, risk assessments, and related security documentation.
  • Experience reviewing and developing security policies, coordinating with 3PAOs, and engaging with commercial customers and federal agencies on security compliance matters.
  • Familiarity with continuous monitoring, vulnerability assessment processes, security control validation, remediation tracking, and authorization documentation updates.
  • Understanding of cloud security principles and the implementation of security controls in cloud-based environments.
  • Experience supporting FedRAMP, DoD, or Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) authorization and ATO processes is highly desirable.
  • CompTIA Security+ certification or an equivalent DoD 8570/8140 baseline certification is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical documentation skills, with the ability to assess risks and translate findings into practical remediation recommendations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to coordinate effectively with technical teams, customers, external assessors, and senior security stakeholders.
  • Sound risk-based decision-making, attention to detail, and a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Ability to balance technical security requirements with operational needs and mission objectives.
  • Self-directed and organized, with the ability to manage competing priorities and collaborate effectively across distributed teams.
  • Ability to work fully remotely from within the United States.
  • Applicants must be able to meet the position's citizenship and clearance requirements. Employment authorization or immigration sponsorship is not available for this role.

Benefits:

  • Competitive annual salary: Proposed compensation range of $93,700–$156,200 USD, depending on geographic location, relevant experience, education, certifications, specialized skills, and applicable federal contract labor categories.
  • Healthcare coverage: Access to health insurance options as part of a comprehensive employee benefits package.
  • Paid leave: Paid time off to support personal needs, rest, and work-life balance.
  • Retirement benefits: Access to retirement savings benefits.
  • Professional development: Learning and development opportunities designed to strengthen technical expertise and support career growth.
  • Remote work flexibility: Fully remote work arrangement for eligible candidates located in the United States.
  • Mission-driven work: The opportunity to contribute to national security, federal cybersecurity compliance, and the protection of sensitive information systems.
  • Technical growth: Hands-on experience with federal security frameworks, cloud security, continuous monitoring, vulnerability management, and authorization processes.
  • Collaborative environment: Work alongside experienced cybersecurity professionals, engineering teams, external assessors, and government stakeholders.
  • Inclusive workplace: An equal opportunity employment environment that welcomes qualified applicants, including veterans and individuals with disabilities.

title: AI Engineer, Public Sector
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Engineer, Public Sector based in the United States.

Join an innovative AI engineering team developing advanced artificial intelligence solutions for US government agencies and mission-critical public sector applications. In this role, you will design, build, and deploy generative and predictive AI capabilities that address complex operational challenges and support high-impact government missions. You will work with large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic workflows, and predictive machine learning to transform emerging AI technologies into practical, secure, and scalable solutions. Balancing rapid proof-of-concept development with long-term production readiness, you will help turn ambitious ideas into reliable applications. Working closely with government customers, subject matter experts, and cross-functional teams, you will translate technical concepts into measurable outcomes. This opportunity combines hands-on engineering, applied research, and customer collaboration in a fast-growing environment focused on trustworthy, explainable, and responsible AI.

Accountabilities:

  • Design and deploy AI solutions: Develop, implement, and deploy AI-powered applications that address the needs of US government customers and support mission-critical use cases.
  • Build generative and predictive AI capabilities: Create solutions combining large language models, predictive machine learning, and intelligent workflows to solve complex customer problems.
  • Develop rapid prototypes: Build proof-of-concept applications to validate technical approaches, demonstrate value, and accelerate customer adoption while designing solutions that can evolve into scalable, maintainable systems.
  • Implement agentic workflows: Explore and develop AI agents, LLM fine-tuning approaches, structured outputs, multimodal capabilities, and advanced orchestration patterns.
  • Build user-facing applications: Design and develop interfaces and applications that enable customers to interact effectively with AI-powered tools, using frameworks such as Flask or Streamlit.
  • Integrate AI technologies: Connect AI models and applications with APIs, databases, retrieval systems, and existing customer infrastructure to deliver end-to-end solutions.
  • Collaborate with customers and experts: Engage directly with government stakeholders and subject matter experts to understand requirements, communicate technical concepts clearly, and translate operational challenges into practical AI solutions.
  • Support solution discovery and pre-sales: Contribute technical expertise to pre-sales activities, demonstrations, and solution design, identifying how AI capabilities can meet customer requirements.
  • Conduct applied research and development: Investigate emerging generative AI techniques, agentic capabilities, and predictive modeling approaches to expand the possibilities of AI applications in government environments.
  • Promote trustworthy AI practices: Contribute to the development of secure, transparent, explainable, and reliable AI solutions suitable for sensitive and regulated use cases.

Requirements:

  • Professional experience: At least three years of professional experience in AI/ML, software engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Education: A bachelor's degree or equivalent undergraduate qualification in a technical discipline, supported by a strong foundation in applied artificial intelligence and machine learning.
  • Programming expertise: Strong Python programming skills and the ability to develop practical, maintainable AI applications. Experience with Java and HTML is an advantage.
  • Generative AI knowledge: Familiarity with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, AI agents, structured outputs, multimodal large language models, and embedding models.
  • AI frameworks: Experience with or knowledge of frameworks and libraries such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Hugging Face Transformers.
  • Predictive machine learning: Experience developing, training, or deploying predictive AI models, ideally within government or other mission-critical environments.
  • Application development: Ability to build functional AI prototypes and user interfaces using tools such as Flask, Streamlit, or comparable UI development frameworks.
  • APIs and integrations: Familiarity with common APIs and development frameworks, including OpenAI APIs, GraphQL, and FastAPI.
  • Data and retrieval technologies: Understanding of databases, vector search, and RAG infrastructure, with exposure to technologies such as Pinecone, FAISS, OpenSearch, and Neo4j.
  • Government sector experience: Experience working with or supporting the US Department of Defense, the US Intelligence Community, or federal civilian agencies is desirable.
  • Customer-facing communication: Ability to explain complex AI/ML concepts in clear, accessible language and connect technical capabilities to practical customer needs and operational outcomes.
  • Problem-solving and adaptability: Strong analytical skills, creativity, and the ability to move between rapid experimentation and the development of robust, reusable solutions.
  • Security clearance: Must be eligible to obtain a US Top Secret security clearance. An active Top Secret clearance is preferred.
  • US employment and export-control eligibility: Applicants must meet applicable US government export-control requirements. This generally requires US citizenship, lawful permanent residence, qualifying protected-individual status, or eligibility to obtain the necessary government authorizations.

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary: Annual base salary ranging from $185,000 to $225,000 USD, depending on qualifications, experience, location, applicable government contract labor categories, education, and certifications.
  • Additional compensation: Potential eligibility for annual bonuses, equity awards in the form of restricted stock units (RSUs), and other incentive compensation, depending on the role and applicable compensation arrangements.
  • Equity ownership: The opportunity to participate in the organization's long-term growth through equity awards.
  • Flexible paid time off: Unlimited paid time off and 14 paid company holidays to support rest, personal commitments, and work-life balance.
  • Flexible working arrangements: Remote work options, flexible working hours, and hybrid opportunities, with offices in Reston, Virginia, and Austin, Texas. Specific arrangements may depend on customer and role requirements.
  • Retirement savings: A 401(k) plan with employer matching to help support long-term financial goals.
  • Comprehensive healthcare: Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance coverage beginning on the first day of employment, with options to support employees and their families.
  • Paid parental leave: Paid leave to support employees welcoming a child through birth, adoption, or foster placement.
  • Meaningful mission: The opportunity to develop advanced AI technologies that address complex challenges and contribute to important US government and public sector initiatives.
  • Innovative technical environment: Work with modern AI frameworks, emerging generative AI technologies, predictive models, and agentic systems.
  • Collaborative culture: Join a team of skilled professionals committed to customer success, technical innovation, security, transparency, and responsible AI development.
  • Professional growth: Opportunities to expand expertise in applied AI, government-focused solutions, customer engagement, and the deployment of mission-critical systems.

title: ASSOC ENGINEER-PRODUCTION (CAB SHOP)
description:
JOB SUMMARY:

Assists in performing the coordination and integration of different departments to ensure that the aircraft or components are on schedule, mitigate risks in a timely manner, and the aircraft/components meets the Dassault quality and safety level. The goal is to accomplish the production process in the smoothest, most judicious and most economical way.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS):

Assists in assessing the risk induced by new tasks/reworks on the aircraft progress, defining action plans to negate those risks and proposing risk reduction plans for future improvement.

Participates in daily technical action plans and follow up with assembly team managers concerning assignment of tasks, operations and discrepancies to be performed on the aircraft/components according to the schedule and expected quality level.

Conduct daily monitoring of critical issues (to include but not limited to shortages, technical events and schedule with actions necessary to keep the line moving). Reports to the Business Unit Manager about critical issues with input regarding recommendations and actions to resolve them.

Coordinates with other departments as required ensuring materials, parts, documentation, engineering data, and other items are delivered to the aircraft or shop on time.

Participates in ways to identify and propose action plans to improve the process or product in regards to cost, schedule, quality, etc.).

Support aircraft/component transfers, projects, and new processes.

Basic ability to conduct root cause analysis and define a corrective action plan.

Utilize support teams to maintain the aircraft/component production process and to improve the schedule.

NON-PRINCIPAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (NON-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS):

Other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor’s Degree in Aviation Engineering, Business or related field. Completed, relevant education from an accredited college or university may be substituted with years of relevant work experience. 1 year of education = 2 years of experience.

Knowledge of engineering practices and challenges related to the management of the production process

Ability to research, analyze and recommend efficient production processes through production engineering concepts regarding work-study, ergonomics, operation research, root cause analysis, manufacturing management, materials management, production planning etc.

Ability to read, understand and communicate (both verbally and in writing) technical information contained in aircraft maintenance manuals, wiring diagrams, and engineering drawings.

Analytical and critical-thinking skills

Ability to troubleshoot problems by determining and following detailed action plans

Proficient in Microsoft Office to include Project and SharePoint skills

Must be able to function throughout the total facility, including up and down stairs and in and out of aircraft with or without reasonable accommodation.

ADDITIONAL DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Fluent in French

Aeronautical experience

FAA Airframe and Power plant licenses

Leadership experience

Formal training in Lean/Continuous improvement

Formal training in project management

Knowledge of Visual Basic

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Typical office and manufacturing environments. Must be able to work for long periods at a computer terminal. Cannot be sensitive to manufacturing environment and noise. Travel by surface and air to include international as required.

This position is designated as a safety-sensitive position because it includes as part of the essential job duties operating equipment and tools on a routine basis. Additionally, the duties of this position concern the service and completion of aircraft, and overall airworthiness of the aircraft. This position is one in which a lapse of attention could result in injury, illness, or death. For the safety of this employee and others, the employee must be able to work in a constant state of alertness and concentrate for long periods of time while performing safety activities.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The compensation for this position typically falls between $58,543.00 and $78,193.00 per year. This position is not eligible for overtime under FLSA guidelines. Note, the final compensation offered to a successful candidate will depend on several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and years of relevant experience, Falcon-specific experience, relevant education/certifications, geographic location, and shift.

Our total compensation package also offers comprehensive healthcare coverage (Medical/Prescription, Dental, Vision), HSA and FSA options, 401k Plan with Company Match, Life Insurance, Disability Benefits, Supplemental Insurance, Group Legal, Paid Time Off, Tuition Reimbursement, Employee Discounts and much more.

We are committed to finding the best, brightest and most dedicated individuals in the aviation industry. Our employees are the key to our success. Soar with us.

title: Senior Cyber Security Analyst
description:
About Y TREE

We are a rapidly growing WealthTech business that is re-defining how individuals and families connect and engage with their money. We provide our clients with control over their personal finances, enhancing their ability to achieve their financial and life aspirations. We are harnessing sophisticated portfolio analytics, innovative behavioural psychology and cutting-edge UX/UI to create a revolutionary experience and transformational outcomes for our users. The business was founded in 2017 by three successful entrepreneurs and business-builders with d iverse experiences and skill-sets in Technology, Corporate Advice and Investment Management and is backed by some of Europe’s leading investors.

Team Overview & The Role

The role will be part of the Technology team and will report into the CTO. This role will work closely with multiple Technology disciplines and other internal and external teams to establish a strong set of cyber controls for the Y TREE business.

This is a hands-on role with a wide range of responsibilities including monitoring, detection, response and remediation of security risks, threats and vulnerabilities. The ultimate goal is to holistically improve Y TREE’s security posture to meet the demands of its clients and its regulators. This is a great opportunity for the right individual to make their mark and support the growth of a scale-up organisation.

Core Responsibilities

  • Security Posture Improvement: Act as a hands-on Security Analyst, closely interacting with multiple technology disciplines to collectively improve the security posture of Y TREE’s technologies.

  • SOC Collaboration & Incident Response: Collaborate with an externally-managed SOC; act as the escalation point for Y TREE, triage and prioritise issues, manage the issue lifecycle, and lead incident response.

  • Vulnerability Management: Carry out security scanning; detect and manage vulnerabilities to resolution and reduce operational risks using commercial (CrowdStrike) and open-source technologies (Trivy) in AWS-hosted applications and infrastructure.

  • Monitoring & Mitigations: Manage security monitoring and alerts to understand attack vectors and introduce mitigations.

  • Automation & LLMs: Use tools and automation (including LLMs) to carry out common security operations tasks.

  • Routine Security Testing: Introduce and embed tools to enhance Y TREE’s internal capabilities for routine security testing activities, and monitor/enhance security on CI/CD pipelines (SAST, DAST and SCA testing).

  • Risk & Remediation Tracking: Maintain a register of security risks and remediations; work closely with Technology, Risk, and Compliance teams to track and close issues.

  • Certifications & Policies: Support Y TREE’s efforts in maintaining current cyber security certifications and achieving higher accreditations, while maintaining/enhancing policies, documentation, and reporting on cyber metrics.

  • Advocacy & Awareness: Elevate cyber security awareness across the organisation and champion best practices.

  • External Audits: Collaborate with external cyber security consultants for external reviews, audits and assessments.

What You Bring

  • Security Frameworks & Regulation: Experience with security-focused frameworks (e.g., CIS, NIST, ISO) and a track record of applying security controls in an FCA-regulated environment, with an understanding of key regulatory guidelines (e.g., GDPR, DORA).

  • Threat Detection & Cloud Security: Experience with intrusion detection, prevention, and management (e.g., SIEM) alongside vulnerability management on cloud systems and applications (ideally AWS and Kubernetes).

  • Incident & Penetration Expertise: Experience leading incident response and management, with familiarity in pen testing of applications and infrastructure.

  • Application Security: Familiarity with OWASP principles, web application security, security practices on native mobile apps (iOS and Android), and security-by-design principles.

  • Tooling & Threat Landscape: Familiarity with project management tools (Confluence, Jira, ServiceNow) and a good understanding of the threat landscape and risks from emerging technologies (like AI).

  • Leadership & Growth: Comfortable taking the lead when required, eager to learn, and passionate about technology with a drive for continuous professional development.

  • Mindset & Collaboration: An organised, meticulous, independent, and critical thinker who is an effective collaborator, open to feedback, and capable of identifying issues and building logical steps to overcome them.

  • Communication Skills: Excellent written and verbal English skills, able to clearly articulate thoughts and ideas during interpersonal communication within our community.

Bonus Points

  • Experience working in a Fintech or WealthTech domain.

Location & Ways of Working

  • Hybrid Model: London-based with a hybrid working policy requiring 2 days per week in our London office.

What We Offer (Benefits)

  • Health & Wellbeing: Private healthcare plan through Vitality (including 50% off premium gym memberships and an exclusive rewards programme) and support for your mental health through our employee assistance programme.

  • True Time Off: 25 days of annual leave per year where we expect you to turn your phone off and switch off; we never ask you to book leave for a doctor's appointment or to see your children's school plays.

  • Financial Future: 3% employer pension contribution as standard, with generous additional employer contributions if you choose to make contributions via salary sacrifice.

  • Environment: A welcoming, dog-friendly London office with appropriate spaces for varying needs, including breakout spaces and silent booths, alongside regular, well-balanced team socials.

  • Extra Perks: A range of family-friendly policies, support towards professional qualifications, electric car schemes, and more!

title: Memory Care Director
description:
About The Ivy of McKinney

The Ivy of McKinney provides assisted living, memory care, and respite care. We are part of Surpass Senior Living, and our mission is simple: we keep families connected. Named Best of McKinney in 2025, our community pairs personalized care with first-class accommodations, amenities, and programming that keeps residents active and thriving.

Our Memory Care neighborhood runs New Traditions, our proprietary, evidence-based dementia care program built around the whole person rather than the diagnosis. It brings families into the care process at every step, and it includes Timeless Table, our signature dining experience that serves the recipes residents grew up with. A Certified Dementia Practitioner developed the program, and every caregiver, nurse, and Resident Care Partner on our team trains in Alzheimer's and dementia care.

About the Role

You will lead the daily life of our Memory Care neighborhood. You build the program calendar, coach the caregivers who deliver it, and keep families close to the people they love. You report to the Health & Wellness Director and supervise the Memory Care department staff.

What You'll Do

  • Plan a monthly program calendar through our Whole-Person Wellness model, with engagement across physical, intellectual, social, emotional, vocational, and spiritual needs, then publish the monthly newsletter and calendar plus weekly and daily schedules.
  • Train, schedule, and coach caregivers to lead assigned programs and adapt activities so every resident can take part successfully.
  • Maintain a safe secured environment through resident checks, door alarm awareness, and wander and elopement vigilance.
  • Coordinate person-centered responses to behavioral expressions in line with New Traditions and the memory care clinical manual.
  • Assess each resident's life history and preferences, keep the Discovery Book current, and help set service plans.
  • Build and supervise outing plans, including at least one Memory Care outing each month, and review them quarterly.
  • Partner with families on communication and dementia-specific care decisions, host in-house events with our marketing team, and use LifeLoop to keep families connected between visits.
  • Manage program expenses within the monthly budget, including correct coding of Memory Care costs.
  • Serve on the Manager on Duty rotation and take part in EOS, including weekly Level 10 meetings, quarterly Rocks, and role Scorecard metrics.

What You'll Bring

  • Two years of experience in a social or recreational program serving older adults living with dementia within the past five years, at least one of them full time in an activity program in a health care or assisted living setting.
  • Two years working with people living with dementia, including leading groups, building social interaction, and assisting with activities of daily living.
  • Experience assessing resident needs and developing approaches that ease discomfort and improve daily well-being.
  • Licensed LVN/LPN
  • Direct management experience in dementia care.
  • Eligibility under state regulatory requirements for the position.
  • Preferred: a degree in social work, psychology, gerontology, therapeutic recreation, or nursing.

Who Thrives Here

You bring the energy to get a room of residents and staff involved. You stay calm and patient when the day shifts. You train well side by side, stay open to new methods, and hold a genuine commitment to the well-being of seniors living with dementia.

Schedule

Tuesday through Saturday

title: Grants Manager
description:
Position: Grants Manager

Reports to: Finance Director

Emergency Classification: Essential

FLSA Classification: Exempt

Pay Grade: 113

The Town of Fort Myers Beach is seeking an organized, detail-driven Grants Manager to administer the Town's portfolio of federal, state, and county grant-funded projects. Under the direction of the Finance Director, this role manages grants across the full lifecycle, from identifying funding opportunities through implementation, reimbursement, and closeout, and partners with department directors to keep capital, resilience, and disaster recovery projects compliant and funded. The ideal candidate brings working knowledge of the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), HUD CDBG and CDBG-DR, and FEMA programs, along with the project management skills to keep multiple awards on schedule and audit-ready.

If you enjoy turning complex regulations into clear, workable processes and want to help secure the funding that rebuilds and strengthens our island, we encourage you to apply.

The Town of FMB Offers a Competitive Benefits Package!

  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive health insurance with low deductibles and annual maximums. The Town covers 100% of employee premiums and 50% of dependent premiums. Benefits include employer-paid life insurance, short- and long-term disability coverage, gym membership reimbursement and more.
  • Work/Life Balance: Employees accrue paid leave monthly, plus sick leave and a birthday benefit annually. The Town observes 14 paid holidays and offers a supportive, team-oriented environment.
  • Retirement Planning: Immediate vesting in a 401(a)/457(b) pension plan with generous employer contributions.

And More! Join a team that values your well-being, growth, and future.

Position Summary

Under the general direction of the Finance Director, the Grants Project Manager plans, coordinates, administers, and oversees municipal projects funded in whole or in part through federal, state, county, and other grant sources across the full grant lifecycle, from identification of funding opportunities and award acceptance through implementation, reimbursement, closeout, and post-closeout compliance. Projects may include capital improvements, infrastructure, facility renovations, resilience and hazard mitigation initiatives, disaster recovery, and community development activities administered under programs such as the Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), CDBG-Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) programs, other U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) programs, and state and county funding sources such as the Lee County Tourist Development Council (TDC).

This position is responsible for coordinating project scope, schedules, budgets, procurement, contracts, consultants, and contractors; ensuring consistent and timely reporting to the Finance Director, Grants Accountant, and funding agencies; and administering grant compliance requirements, including the federal Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), from project inception through closeout and reimbursement.

The Grants Project Manager works in partnership with the Town's department directors, who serve as the project managers for grant-funded projects within their departments. Department directors are responsible for the technical delivery of their projects (design, construction, and operations); the Grants Project Manager is responsible for ensuring those projects are administered in compliance with grant requirements and that the documentation, reporting, and reimbursement needed to secure and retain funding are completed.

The ideal candidate will have experience managing public-sector or grant-funded projects and a working knowledge of federal grant requirements, HUD regulations, environmental review, procurement, labor standards, income eligibility, civil rights compliance, and project closeout requirements. Experience researching funding opportunities and supporting grant applications is a plus.

Responsibilities and Reporting During an Emergency Situation

If assigned, employees in this classification will be required to report and carry out duties as directed immediately before, during, and after a severe weather event or other emergency, and for the duration of the emergency. Depending on the nature of the emergency, this may require irregular schedules and extended hours, including around the clock for several days on short notice.

EXAMPLES OF ESSENTIAL DUTIES

Funding Identification and Pre-Award

  • Researches and monitors federal, state, county, corporate, and private foundation funding opportunities, including Notices of Funding Opportunity (NOFOs), that align with Town capital, resilience, and recovery priorities; disseminates opportunities to departments and evaluates eligibility, match requirements, and administrative capacity before the Town commits to pursue an award.
  • Assists in preparing grant applications, including narratives, project budgets, cost estimates, and supporting documentation; coordinates with departments and Town-procured grant consultants on complex or technical applications.
  • Prepares or assists with Town Council agenda items, resolutions, ordinances, budget amendments, and agreements required to apply for, accept, appropriate, and execute grant awards.

Project Implementation and Contract Management

  • Serves as the primary grants liaison to department directors acting as project managers for grant-funded projects; meets regularly with each to review scope, schedule, budget, and compliance status, and coordinates all implementation aspects of assigned grants with Town Administration, Finance, funding agencies, and other Town staff involved in grant administration.
  • Prepares compliant scopes of work, timelines, schedules of deliverables, and budgets for written agreements based on grant applications, award terms, and regulations; monitors these throughout program execution.
  • Prepares and maintains detailed workplans for each agreement with key deadlines and requirements; meets regularly with department directors and assigned partners to ensure program objectives are met; provides technical assistance during program execution.
  • Coordinates with the Town's procurement function to ensure solicitations, contracts, and purchases for grant-funded work comply with 2 CFR 200.317–200.327, funding-agency requirements, and Town purchasing policy, including required federal contract provisions.
  • Works with contractors and consultants to ensure contract terms, project timelines, and grant reporting deadlines are met; conducts field visits to verify that work performed is accurate, eligible, and progressing on established deadlines.
  • Provides contract oversight, including review of pay applications, invoices, change orders, and compliance with contract terms.
  • Monitors award terms, conditions, budgets, and periods of performance; identifies the need for scope changes, budget modifications, or time extensions in coordination with department directors and prepares amendment and extension requests to funding agencies.

Compliance, Monitoring, and Financial Coordination

  • Administers federal cross-cutting requirements applicable to assigned awards, which may include environmental review (NEPA/24 CFR Part 58), Davis-Bacon and Related Acts, Section 3, Build America, Buy America (BABA), the Uniform Relocation Act, fair housing and civil rights requirements, and duplication-of-benefits requirements for disaster funds.
  • Acts as project lead in monitoring subrecipients and partners, ensuring all elements of program compliance are met, and overseeing completion of monitoring-related corrective action plans.
  • Establishes and maintains compliant master grant files and a Town-wide grant tracking system (award amounts, status, deadlines, expenditures, and reporting dates) to support audit, monitoring, budgeting, and statistical reporting.
  • Works closely with the Grants Accountant on common grant requirements to ensure timely, compliant completion, including executive summary development, match requirements, program income or other revenue tracking and usage, and review of expenditures for allowability, allocability, and reasonableness.
  • Coordinates the collection of documentation from departments to support drawdowns and reimbursement requests; prepares and submits complete reimbursement packages to the Finance Director and/or Grants Accountant for approval and submittal.
  • Assists with year-end grant reconciliation, preparation of the Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards and State Financial Assistance (SEFA/SESFA), Single Audit requests, and funding-agency monitoring visits.
  • Develops and recommends grant administration policies, procedures, checklists, and internal controls that promote compliance and consistency across Town departments; maintains a resource library of funding sources, templates, and past applications.

Reporting and Closeout

  • Submits quarterly and other required progress, financial, and performance reports to funding agencies, the Finance Director, and other stakeholders, ensuring consistent and timely reporting.
  • Oversees the timely and compliant conclusion of grant programs by working closely with subrecipients, developers, vendors, or partners to provide guidance on program completion, review of compliant pay requests, and completion of all deliverables identified in the agreement.
  • Assures each program meets its final objective and participates in compliant grant closeout by reviewing final records, pay requests, regulations, and grant agreement documents; prepares post-closeout compliance plans for partners, such as program income tracking, Section 3, Davis-Bacon, or long-term use and maintenance requirements.
  • Assists with the preparation of HUD planning documents, such as the Consolidated Plan, annual Action Plan, and CDBG-DR Action Plan amendments, or the Town's input into County and State plans, as applicable.

Emergency Management and Disaster Recovery

  • Supports emergency preparedness, disaster recovery, and post-disaster grant administration activities, including FEMA Public Assistance and Hazard Mitigation Grant Program documentation, cost tracking, and coordination with state and federal agencies.

General

  • Provides assistance, advice, support, and guidance to Town departments, applicants, and recipients of grants during the program operation and closeout phases.
  • Reads professional journals, federal and state regulations, notices of funding, and correspondence, and attends conferences and training as needed to stay abreast of industry standards, trends, and regulatory changes.
  • Operates a computer, copier, scanner, telephone, and other standard office and field equipment, including word processing, spreadsheet, database, and grant-management software, to complete essential functions.
  • Builds and maintains effective working relationships with Town departments, funding agencies, contractors, consultants, and the public.
  • Maintains regular and reliable attendance; attends assigned meetings, training, and events, which may include evening Town Council meetings.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

(These essential job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed. The omission of a specific duty does not exclude it from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment for this classification. Employees will be required to perform other job-related duties as required.)

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

None. Provides guidance on grant compliance requirements to department directors and their staff, and functional direction to consultants, contractors, and subrecipients on assigned projects.

REQUIREMENTS:

Education, Certification, and Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Construction Management, or a closely related field required.
  • Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience working with grant agencies and/or implementing federal, state, and local grant programs subject to numerous regulations required, preferably in a governmental environment; experience with HUD Community Development Block Grant (CDBG), CDBG-DR, or FEMA-funded programs strongly preferred.
  • Any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience that provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job may be considered.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Grants Management Specialist (CGMS), Grant Professional Certified (GPC), or HUD-related program certification preferred.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Driver License with any applicable endorsements, or obtain one within thirty (30) days of hire or promotion.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

Knowledge:

  • Federal, state, and local grant administration requirements, including the Uniform Guidance (2 CFR Part 200), cost principles, and Single Audit requirements.
  • HUD CDBG and CDBG-DR regulations, environmental review, procurement standards, labor standards (e.g., Davis-Bacon/Section 3), Build America, Buy America (BABA), income eligibility, and civil rights compliance.
  • FEMA Public Assistance, Hazard Mitigation, and other post-disaster recovery funding programs, as applicable.
  • Funding sources and research methods for federal, state, county, corporate, and foundation grants.
  • Program income, match requirements, and other revenue tracking and usage rules applicable to federal and state grant programs.
  • Consolidated Plan and annual Action Plan preparation and community needs assessment processes.
  • Project management principles and practices, including scope, schedule, budget, and risk management.
  • Public procurement and contract administration procedures, and basic legal principles of contracts and agreements.
  • Governmental budgeting and accounting fundamentals as they relate to grant revenues, expenditures, and reimbursement.
  • Subrecipient and partner monitoring practices, including compliance review and corrective action plan development.
  • Florida public-records law (Chapter 119, F.S.) and documentation and records-retention standards applicable to grant-funded projects.

Skills:

  • Managing multiple concurrent grant agreements, projects, budgets, and deadlines.
  • Preparing and presenting clear, accurate reports, executive summaries, workplans, Council agenda items, and grant documentation.
  • Making accurate arithmetic, financial, and statistical computations and preparing budget analyses.
  • Negotiating and administering agreements with subrecipients, contractors, and consultants.
  • Communicating effectively, orally and in writing, with Town leadership, funding agencies, partners, and the public.
  • Using Microsoft Office (particularly Excel), project management, financial, and grant-tracking software and systems, such as HUD's Integrated Disbursement and Information System (IDIS), Disaster Recovery Grant Reporting (DRGR) system, and FEMA Grants Portal.
  • Monitoring grant partners for compliance and developing corrective action plans.

Abilities:

  • Interpret, apply, and explain complex federal, state, and local grant regulations and municipal policies consistently and accurately, including to staff without grant experience.
  • Exercise sound judgment and independent decision-making in managing project risk, timelines, and budgets.
  • Coordinate effectively across departments and influence outcomes without direct supervisory authority.
  • Organize own work, set priorities, and meet critical deadlines while adapting to competing demands, frequent change, delays, or unexpected events.
  • Review and verify the accuracy of financial and project documentation.
  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with Town staff, funding agencies, contractors, consultants, and the public.
  • Conduct field inspections and site visits in varied conditions.
  • Maintain accurate, organized, and confidential records in accordance with public-records requirements.
  • Work flexible and irregular hours, including during emergency activations or disaster-recovery periods, when required.

Physical Requirements:

  • Frequent sitting, standing, and walking between office and field or project-site environments; frequent use of hands to handle, feel, and operate a keyboard.
  • Ability to walk construction and project sites, including on uneven or unfinished terrain.
  • Regular lifting and carrying of materials, equipment, or documents up to 25 pounds, and occasionally up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to operate a Town or personal vehicle to travel between project sites, meetings, and Town facilities.

Environmental Requirements:

  • Work is performed in both an office setting and outdoor or field environments, including active construction sites, in varied weather conditions.
  • May involve exposure to construction-related hazards, noise, dust, uneven surfaces, and post-disaster field conditions.

Sensory Requirements:

  • Task requires sound perception and discrimination.
  • Task requires visual perception and discrimination.
  • Task requires color and depth perception and discrimination (e.g., reviewing plans and inspecting field work).
  • Task requires oral communications ability.
