title: Intern - Sandia/DOE Science Undergrad Laboratory Intern (SULI) - RD Undergrad Summer
description:
What Your Job Will Be Like

This position requires a separate application to the DOE SULI Program, which has a submission deadline of January 6, 2027, including two online letters of recommendation.

We are hiring several undergraduate students for a 10-week, full-time internship during Summer 2027, through the DOE Science Undergrad Laboratory Intern (SULI) Program. Most projects will necessarily involve on-site work, but in some cases a remote internship may be possible.

As a SULI intern, you will assist Sandia research staff on projects that span a variety of technical areas at Sandia's Livermore site. Depending on the project assignment and qualifications, you will be responsible for:

  • setting up and running lab experiments
  • creating software programs to analyze data
  • developing computational models and algorithms

At Sandia's California campus, SULI interns are placed in a variety of topical areas in association with foundational science and energy research programs. Topics of research may include:

  • biofuel development
  • genomics and biological systems
  • chemical reaction processes
  • molecular dynamics
  • quantum sensing
  • advanced laser diagnostics
  • exascale simulations of reacting flows
  • uncertainty quantification
  • machine learning and stochastic modeling
  • advanced engine combustion
  • advanced materials for hydrogen storage
  • advanced materials for neuromorphic and quantum computing
  • advanced fusion materials

Salary Range

At Sandia, we value the important work done by our interns and its contribution to National Security. Because of this, our interns earn competitive pay rates. Our pay structure is based on earned credit hours, classification, and degree level. Your pay rate will be determined during the hire process and included in your offer package. You can view the Intern Pay Rate chart here.

Qualifications We Require

You bring the confidence and skills to be eligible for the job by meeting these minimum requirements:

  • Currently attending and enrolled full time in the spring term immediately preceding the internship (or scheduled to graduate in the spring) in an accredited undergraduate program
  • Pursuing a science, engineering, or math major
  • Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0
  • Ability to work up to 40 hours per week during the summer
  • U.S. citizens, legal permanent residents, asylees or refugees in the U.S.

Note: If you have not earned a HS diploma or equivalent, please apply to a high school intern position.

Qualifications We Desire

Desired candidates will have skills and interests aligned with science and energy programs at Sandia's Livermore, CA location.

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of three (3) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

About Our Team

Sandia's Livermore, CA location performs a wide range of open research addressing science and energy topics through support from the DOE Office of Science, the DOE¿s applied energy offices, and the internally funded Laboratory Directed Research & Development program.

About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov


*These benefits vary by job classification.

Security Clearance

This position does not currently require a Department of Energy (DOE) security clearance.

Sandia will conduct a pre-employment drug test and background review that includes checks of personal references, credit, law enforcement records, and employment/education verifications. Furthermore, employees in New Mexico need to pass a U.S. Air Force background screen for access to Kirtland Air Force Base. Substance abuse or illegal drug use, falsification of information, criminal activity, serious misconduct or other indicators of untrustworthiness can cause access to be denied or terminated, resulting in the inability to perform the duties assigned and subsequent termination of employment. Under federal law, citizens and agents of the People's Republic of China, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Democratic People's Republic of North Korea, and the Russian Federation are generally prohibited from accessing Sandia National Laboratories. Accordingly, such individuals will not be considered for employment unless they are also a citizen of the United States.

If hired without a clearance and it subsequently becomes necessary to obtain and maintain one for the position, or you bid on positions that require a clearance, a pre-processing background review may be conducted prior to a required federal background investigation. Applicants for a DOE security clearance need to be U.S. citizens. If you hold more than one citizenship (i.e., of the U.S. and another country), your ability to obtain a security clearance may be impacted.

Members of the workforce (MOWs) hired at Sandia who require uncleared access for greater than 179 days during their employment, are required to go through the Uncleared Personal Identity Verification (UPIV) process. Access includes physical and/or cyber (logical) access, as well as remote access to any NNSA information technology (IT) systems. UPIV requirements are not applicable to individuals who require a DOE personnel security clearance for the performance of their SNL employment or to foreign nationals. The UPIV process will include the completion of a USAccess Enrollment, SF-85 (Questionnaire for Non-Sensitive Positions) and OF-306 (Declaration of for Federal Employment). An unfavorable UPIV determination will result in immediate retrieval of the SNL issued badge, removal of cyber (logical) access and/or removal from SNL subcontract. All MOWs may appeal the unfavorable UPIV determination to DOE/NNSA immediately. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the MOW may try to go through the UPIV process one year after the decision date.

EEO

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status and any other protected class under state or federal law.

NNSA Requirements for MedPEDs

If you have a Medical Portable Electronic Device (MedPED), such as a pacemaker, defibrillator, drug-releasing pump, hearing aids, or diagnostic equipment and other equipment for measuring, monitoring, and recording body functions such as heartbeat and brain waves, if employed by Sandia National Laboratories you may be required to comply with NNSA security requirements for MedPEDs.

If you have a MedPED and you are selected for an on-site interview at Sandia National Laboratories, there may be additional steps necessary to ensure compliance with NNSA security requirements prior to the interview date.

title: Foreperson - Charleston, WV
location: Charleston, WV, West Virginia, United States
description:
The Foreperson coordinates crew members, equipment, tools, and supplies in order to complete all jobs according to contract specifications.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

  • Always follow and enforce safe practices and rules
  • Direct crew members and manage equipment each day
  • Assign specific tasks to crew members and supervise performance
  • Plan and execute the assigned work and tasks in a safe and professional manner
  • Organize job assignments so that work is completed as efficiently as possible
  • Notify private property owners of presence on property; obtain permission from property owners to trim or remove trees and/or apply herbicides; discuss issues such as obtaining access, power interruption, work to be done, etc. with customer and/or property owner
  • Ensure crew members wear personal protective equipment (PPE) and follow safe practices on the job
  • Trim and/or remove trees by climbing with the aid of a ladder, safety belt, climbing line, powered trimmer lift truck, or work from the ground using gasoline, air, and hand-powered saws, pruner, etc.; cuts branches or trunk sections and ropes or lowers them to the ground with lines
  • Spray stumps and brush with hand-spraying equipment to prevent further growth
  • Load and unload trucks with logs, stumps, brush, and debris and/or feeds brush into a powered chipper
  • Designate break and lunch time
  • Direct cleanup of the job site and make sure all equipment and supplies are secured on the truck Inspect the work performed to job specifications then notify customer that work has been completed
  • Keep accurate records of time, equipment, and material used
  • Complete daily truck inspection; conduct job briefings as specified by federal law
  • Re-stock needed supplies on truck and perform routine maintenance on equipment or inform General Foreperson of damaged equipment and needed supplies
  • Determine action to take in emergency situations by eliminating hazards to life and property
  • Perform duties for storm work as needed

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Foreperson has no direct reports, but directs crew members to prepare equipment, tools, and supplies necessary for each day’s work.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

Prior experience in electric utility vegetation management, construction, logging, landscaping, mechanical, or military industries preferred

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS

High School diploma or education equivalent preferred

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Must be able to meet and demonstrate qualifications of all positions on a crew
  • Must be able to follow verbal or written directives
  • Must be able to delegate work and take accountability for the performance of a crew
  • Must be able to understand drawings and symbols representing lines, voltages, line equipment, etc.
  • Must be capable of adjusting to field requirements and taking independent action without close supervision
  • Must have and maintain a Driver’s License and be able to safely drive a company vehicle
  • Must be able to work outdoors under varying and sometimes adverse weather conditions
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain first-aid certification and CPR
  • Must have and maintain a Driver’s License if hired for a driving position
  • Must be able to effectively communicate with others
  • Must have endurance necessary to perform duties throughout a standard eight or ten hour day
  • Must be able to operate and service all required tools and equipment
  • Must be able to travel out of town for storm restoration work when needed

title: Sourcing & Contracts Lead, Operations
description:
Fervo Energy develops and operates next generation geothermal assets that deliver reliable, 24/7 carbon free electricity. As Fervo commissions new facilities and expands its operating portfolio, disciplined sourcing and contract management will be essential to safe startup, reliable production, and cost effective plant performance.


The Sourcing and Contracts Lead, Operations will develop and execute procurement strategies for commissioning, operations, and production requirements. The role will lead competitive sourcing, negotiate and establish contracts, manage supplier and contract performance, and help build Fervo's maintenance, repair, and operations category strategy. Working with Operations, Commissioning, Engineering, Maintenance, Finance, Legal, and HSE, this person will protect supply continuity, control commercial risk, and deliver measurable value from demand planning through contract closeout.

title: Senior Expeditor
description:
Fervo Energy is applying first-principles engineering and a manufacturing mindset to geothermal power, an industry that has operated the same way for decades. Rather than deploying one-off energy projects, we are building standardized, repeatable GeoBlocks – units of geothermal power generation – designed to get cheaper, faster, and more reliable with every iteration. By applying advanced drilling technology and engineering rigor to geothermal development, Fervo delivers clean, firm, 24/7 renewable energy at commercial scale. At Fervo, Supply Chain is a highly strategic function that acts as a core driver of our GeoBlock manufacturing process.


The Senior Expeditor owns the schedule-side view of procurement across Fervo’s active project portfolio — building and maintaining the master delivery timeline, tracking critical-path packages from award through fabrication and shipment, and surfacing risk to leadership before it threatens a project milestone.


This is a senior, largely autonomous role that works closely with Engineering, Construction, Logistics, and Field Operations, and represents Supply Chain directly in cross-functional planning discussions. The right person manages a large, complex portfolio of purchase orders and vendor commitments aligned to the integrated project schedule, exercises independent judgment on which packages matter most to cycle time and well cost, and mentors less experienced expeditors and coordinators. Success requires strong schedule ownership, structured status reporting, sound escalation judgment, and the ability to influence engineering, procurement, and field stakeholders without direct authority.

title: Shift Operations Supervisor
description:
Panchero's - NOW HIRING TEAM LEADS

Panchero's Mexican Grill is looking for friendly and enthusiastic people to join the team! You will have the opportunity to be part of a positive and fun culture while enhancing your job skills for further opportunities within our company!

**Flexible schedule**
**Competitive pay**
**Food Discounts**
**Career Advancement Opportunities**
**Fun Workplace Culture**

JOB DUTIES INCLUDE (but not limited to):

· Food Prep & Burrito Building

· Customer Service

· Leadership & Employee Management

· Cash Handling

· Kitchen and Restaurant Sanitation

· Other duties as assigned

EDUCATION AND TRAINING: No educational requirements.

WORKING EXPERIENCE: Leadership experience required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bending, stooping, reaching, twisting, lifting, pushing, pulling and moving items
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. without assistance
  • Requires the ability to move and stand for long periods of time

WHO WE ARE

Pancheros grew from our very first restaurant-a local favorite in the college town of Iowa City back in 1992-to one of the most beloved Mexican Fast casual brands in the country. Scratch-made dough and fresh-pressed flour tortillas are integral to our burritos. Ingredients perfectly mixed into every bite is also a key component of Burritos Better Built, so in 2002 we introduced Bob The Tool® to mix before roll. And of course, our homemade queso, which has earned a fan following for its ooey, gooey, extra cheesy, velvety texture and zip of zesty, mouthwatering flavor perfect for chip-dipping or slathering on your burrito.

WHAT SETS US APART

Delicious starts with a solid foundation.

Our fresh-pressed tortillas are the key to Burritos Better Built. Each one, made from house-made dough every morning and fresh-pressed in front of your eyes until perfectly golden brown. Then tightly wrapped to support all the freshest ingredients of your choice for a burrito that stands up to your wildest cravings.

URRITO. Burritos without the B.S.

When you keep things as fresh as we do, there's simply no need for the B and the S. (Otherwise known as shortcuts like fryers, freezers, packaged tortillas-we'd never!) We take pride in putting in the extra effort to do things the right way-from scratch, by hand-because that's what delivers the flavor that really sets us apart.

All the right stuff in all the right places.

The key to our burritos is mixing every ingredient together in every bite, because no one wants a mouthful of sour cream or rice. We take mixing so seriously, we even created our very own tool to get the job done right: Bob the Tool. Your single-handed assurance that every burrito you order at Pancheros won't just meet your expectations, it'll exceed them.

We take a fresh approach to service, too.

Every time you walk into one of our restaurants, we're on a mission to make your day even better. Carefully preparing your food from scratch, keeping our restaurants in tip top shape, making online ordering, delivery, and catering as smooth as our queso, and providing quick, courteous service that makes every meal an unforgettable one.

Reports to the Assistant Manger on duty.

description:

title: User Terminal Project Coordinator
description:
The User Terminal Project Coordinator supports the Program Manager responsible for internal development activities and technology vendors providing user terminal solutions for Telesat. The role combines program administration with hands-on Jira work management, ensuring that technical work is clearly defined, actively tracked, and driven to completion across internal software development teams and external vendors.

The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a technical development environment and across a multifunctional organization that includes engineering, program management, product management, business development, sales, commercial teams, and external suppliers. Experience supporting Agile software development is strongly preferred.

Main Responsibilities

Create well-structured Jira epics, stories, tasks, bugs, and technical-request tickets with clear problem statements, scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, priorities, owners, and supporting technical context.

Administer and maintain Jira projects and boards, including Kanban boards, workflows, backlogs, filters, dashboards, and reporting views that provide clear visibility into work status, blockers, ownership, and due dates.

Drive Jira work items through completion by coordinating follow-up with internal software developers, engineering teams, program stakeholders, and vendors; identify stalled work, facilitate resolution of blockers, and escalate issues when required.

Facilitate work intake, backlog review, prioritization, and status-tracking activities in collaboration with technical leads and program managers, while ensuring tickets remain current, actionable, and aligned to program priorities.

Establish and maintain action-item registers and Kanban-style action boards; assign owners and target dates, monitor progress, follow up on overdue actions, and confirm closure with appropriate evidence.

Attend program, vendor, and technical meetings; prepare agendas as needed; capture concise minutes, decisions, risks, dependencies, and action items; and distribute and maintain meeting records.

Coordinate project activities across system engineering, user terminal engineering, software development, program management, product management, commercial teams, and external vendors to support compliant delivery on time and on budget.

Ensure required program documentation, decisions, meeting records, and supporting artifacts are organized and archived in accordance with data-management standards.

Support the Program Manager in developing and maintaining project schedules, timelines, milestone plans, status reports, risks, and dependencies across multiple user terminal vendors, integrators, component developers, and internal teams.

Education and Experience Required

Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, business management, or a relevant discipline; experience with communications systems, satellite terminals, or other complex technical products is preferred but not required.

Minimum of 3 years of experience in project coordination, program support, software delivery coordination, or a related role within a STEM or technical development environment.

Demonstrated proficiency with Atlassian Jira and Confluence, including creating and managing tickets, administering boards and backlogs, configuring or working within workflows, building filters and dashboards, and tracking work to completion.

Experience supporting Agile software development practices such as Scrum, Kanban, backlog refinement, sprint or increment planning, stand-ups, reviews, and retrospectives.

Ability to understand technical discussions and translate them into clear, accurate, and actionable Jira tickets, meeting records, status updates, and follow-up actions.

Experience coordinating work across internal technical teams and external technology vendors; experience with third-party design, software, integration, or manufacturing programs is an asset.

Strong working knowledge of project-management and reporting tools such as Oracle Primavera, Microsoft Project

Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with strong attention to detail and disciplined follow-through.

PMP, Certified ScrumMaster, SAFe, or comparable project or Agile certification is an asset.

Decision Making and Working Style

Make day-to-day decisions about task sequencing and follow-up priorities in support of program-management objectives.

Proactively identify incomplete, unclear, blocked, or overdue work and coordinate the appropriate next steps with owners and stakeholders.

Work independently in areas of ambiguity while seeking timely technical or program direction when needed.

Demonstrate self-motivation, persistence, and accountability in driving varied assignments through conclusion.

Work effectively with diverse, geographically distributed teams and communicate technical information in a concise, accurate, and accessible manner.

The successful candidate must be able to work in Canada and obtain clearance under the Canadian Controlled Goods program (CGP).

Your single-handed assurance that every burrito you order at Pancheros won't just meet your expectations, it'll exceed them.

Every time you walk into one of our restaurants, we're on a mission to make your day even better. title: Field / Phone Enumerator Indiana
company: National Association of State Departments of Agriculture
description:
The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture (NASDA) of Arlington, VA is looking to hire a detail-oriented part-time Field Enumerator to perform tasks that support our organization. Are you looking for a job with flexible hours? Would you like to work for an agriculture nonprofit that cares about its community and employees? If so, please read on!

This field enumerator position earns a competitive wage of $17.75/hour, plus mileage with opportunities for a promotion based on hours worked and performance ratings. We also offer exceptional perks, including a flexible schedule, the opportunity to work from home, the ability to work in your community, and knowledge about where your food comes from. If this sounds like the right opportunity in agriculture for you, apply today!

ABOUT NASDA

NASDA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit association that represents the elected and appointed commissioners, secretaries, and directors of the departments of agriculture in all fifty states and four U.S. territories. Founded in 1916, our mission is to grow and enhance American agriculture through policies, partnerships, and public engagement.

Since 1972, NASDA has employed enumerators to collect agricultural data on behalf of the United States Department of Agriculture's (USDA) National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS). In order to achieve our goals, we need employees who are as passionate about agriculture as we are and willing to put in the hard work. To find the right people, we strive to create a positive work environment that our employees can be proud of and want to build their careers with!

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A FIELD ENUMERATOR

In this Field Enumerator position, you play a crucial role in serving our agricultural producers by providing reliable, accurate, and objective statistics and information that farmers, ranchers, and rural communities depend on. You actively interview farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural businesses either in person or on the phone. At times, you travel to designated fields in order to perform crop counts. After gathering all your information, you maintain and deliver detailed and legible records of the interviews, crop counts, mileage, expenditures, and your hours worked.

You conduct your enumerator work from a residence with an operable telephone free from any distractions. By maintaining a personal vehicle, you are always ready to travel in order to perform your field enumerator duties. The job brings something new every day, and you enjoy the flexibility and energetic nature of it!

QUALIFICATIONS FOR A FIELD ENUMERATOR

  • Experience multitasking in an energetic, deadline-oriented work environment
  • Ability to positively represent NASDA and the benefits of enumerators in all survey actions
  • Ability to make crop counts in designated fields
  • Ability to maintain a reliable personal vehicle
  • Ability to conduct interviews in person or by telephone with farm operators and other individuals
  • Knowledge about computers or iPads

Do you have excellent verbal and written communication skills? Are you able to demonstrate good time management in a fast-paced environment? Are you self-motivated? Do you enjoy working as part of a team? Are you organized? Can you maintain a positive and friendly attitude? If so, you might just be perfect for this field service position for our agriculture nonprofit!

WORK SCHEDULE

This part-time field service position works a flexible schedule that may include some evenings, weekends, and holidays. Weather, seasonal farm responsibilities, and community functions may affect work hours.

READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

We understand your time is valuable, so we have a very quick and easy application process. If you feel that you would be right for this Field Enumerator job, please fill out our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application. We look forward to meeting you!

Location: Benton Co and surrounding Counties

NASDA does not discriminate in employment practices or programs on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, disability, political beliefs, or family status.

You will have to pass a background check

title: Senior SAP ABAP Developers (Digital Manufacturing Integration)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior SAP ABAP Developer (Digital Manufacturing Integration) based in the United States.

We are seeking highly experienced Senior SAP ABAP Developers to support a major digital manufacturing integration initiative within a highly regulated aerospace and defense environment. In this remote, contract-to-hire opportunity, you will lead hands-on ABAP development, code remediation, and integration efforts as enterprise systems transition from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA. You will build secure, scalable interfaces connecting core ERP systems with SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence (MII), Manufacturing Execution (ME), and SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP). Your expertise will help optimize real-time shop-floor data exchange, improve system performance, and support modern, clean-core SAP architecture. Working closely with functional consultants and distributed technical teams, you will translate complex requirements into robust technical solutions. This role is particularly suited to a senior SAP specialist with extensive brownfield migration experience, strong technical leadership, and a background in project-based manufacturing.

Accountabilities

  • Develop, enhance, and maintain SAP ABAP solutions across ECC and S/4HANA environments to support digital manufacturing integration and enterprise system modernization.

  • Design, build, and optimize interfaces connecting SAP S/4HANA with SAP MII, SAP ME, and other shop-floor manufacturing systems using OData services, CDS Views, and ABAP Managed Database Procedures (AMDP).

  • Develop APIs, integration flows, and side-by-side extensions on SAP BTP, applying clean-core principles and modern SAP extensibility practices.

  • Create and maintain custom ABAP objects, User Exits, BADIs, and Enhancement Spots across key manufacturing modules, including Production Planning (PP), Quality Management (QM), Materials Management (MM), and Plant Maintenance (PM).

  • Apply modern SAP development frameworks, including the ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model (RAP), where appropriate.

  • Lead hands-on code remediation and optimization activities associated with SAP S/4HANA brownfield migrations, resolving legacy-code issues and supporting migration readiness.

  • Troubleshoot, profile, and tune complex ABAP programs and database queries to ensure reliable, high-performance processing of high-volume, real-time data.

  • Ensure custom code, integrations, applications, and data structures meet applicable aerospace and defense security requirements, including ITAR-related data segregation and secure cloud standards.

  • Collaborate with functional consultants, technical leads, and customer stakeholders to translate specifications into secure, scalable, maintainable solutions.

  • Organize technical work, maintain clear documentation, plan development activities, and take ownership of deliverables while remaining actively involved in coding.

  • Support project-based manufacturing capabilities, including project-level material and cost tracking, work-in-progress visibility, inventory management, and engineer-to-order processes, where applicable.

    • Requirements:

    • Typically 10–15+ years of SAP experience, with approximately 8–12+ years or more of advanced SAP ABAP development experience. The project description references both 8–12+ and 10–15+ years; candidates should be prepared to demonstrate senior-level expertise.

    • Extensive hands-on experience developing and remediating ABAP code in SAP ECC and SAP S/4HANA environments.

    • Mandatory: Experience with at least two to three SAP S/4HANA brownfield migration or implementation projects, including hands-on code remediation.

    • At least one to two substantial projects involving native development in SAP S/4HANA, with three or more years of relevant hands-on experience preferred.

    • Strong practical knowledge of SAP BTP services, such as SAP Integration Suite, Extension Suite, or the BTP ABAP Environment, including side-by-side extensions and decoupled integrations.

    • Deep technical expertise in CDS Views, OData services, AMDP, modern ABAP development, and SAP clean-core principles.

    • Strong understanding of SAP S/4HANA manufacturing data models, database tables, and business logic, particularly across PP, QM, and MM.

    • Demonstrated experience with ABAP performance tuning, complex integration troubleshooting, and high-volume data processing.

    • Strongly preferred: Experience with Project Manufacturing Management and Optimization (PMMO), particularly in project-based manufacturing, aerospace and defense, industrial manufacturing, or engineer-to-order environments.

    • Experience developing integrations with manufacturing execution systems (MES), SAP MII, or SAP ME is an advantage; SCADA-only experience does not meet this specific preference.

    • Familiarity with SAP S/4HANA brownfield migration strategies, SAP Fiori, SAPUI5, and Agile or Scrum delivery methodologies is desirable.

    • SAP BTP or SAP ABAP development certifications are advantageous.

    • Strong analytical skills, exceptional attention to detail, and a disciplined approach to technical documentation and delivery planning.

    • Demonstrated leadership, organization, and stakeholder management skills, including the ability to navigate challenging customer interactions while maintaining a collaborative, solutions-oriented approach.

    • Ability to work independently, lead technical activities, and remain hands-on throughout development and remediation work.

    • U.S. citizenship or relevant regional security clearance may be required due to ITAR regulations and defense contract restrictions.

      • Benefits:

      • Compensation: $70–$90 per hour.

      • Work arrangement: Remote position.

      • Employment type: Contract-to-hire.

      • Initial project duration: Approximately 6–8 months.

      • Technical scope: Work on SAP S/4HANA modernization, digital manufacturing integration, code remediation, and SAP BTP solutions.

      • Industry exposure: Contribute to a complex enterprise technology initiative in the aerospace and defense sector.

      • Professional growth: Apply senior-level SAP expertise to brownfield migrations, manufacturing integration, and modern SAP architecture.

      • Technical leadership: Take ownership of development planning, solution quality, documentation, and stakeholder collaboration.

title: Code Enforcement Official
description:
General Description

The purpose of this class within the organization is to ensure enforcement and compliance of the City of Charleston Zoning Ordinance and the State Building Codes as adopted by the city as they pertain to existing structures and properties within the City of Charleston.

This class works under general supervision, independently developing work methods and sequences.

Duties and Responsibilities

The functions listed below are those that represent the majority of the time spent working in this class. Management may assign additional functions related to the type of work of the class as necessary.

Essential Functions:

Strives to be efficient and effective at balancing and meeting the common needs and reasonable expectations of core constituents.

Contributes towards the department's mission by continuously striving to meet expectations, strategic goals and objectives.

Schedules and completes scheduled residential rental property inspections.

Receives and investigates complaints from various sources for code violations in a timely manner.

Issue warning letter(s), fines, or citation / summons to court if code violations are found.

Testifies in municipal court with appropriate documentation to clearly articulate facts to the Municipal Judge and City Attorney.

Researches and contacts owners of structures via letter, phone or court citation and secures their signature on demolition agreements; listens to complaints of potential for all code violations.

Coordinates title search and asbestos survey request/receipt and reviews; contacts any necessary lien holders regarding potential demolition.

Performs various administrative work; enters and updates data in the Tyler Enterprise Permitting and Licensing Module; creates and maintains files; forwards invoices with appropriate paperwork for payment.

Attends and speaks at community meetings and speaks to groups and other peers on property maintenance, crime and other issues when necessary.

Corresponds with utility companies concerning electric drops.

Investigates un-permitted work.

Performs site checks, takes photos and documents information for Historic Preservation Clearance.

Additional Duties:

Initiates and oversees asbestos removal based on survey results.

Orders demolition and reseeding of lots.

Updates the Property Maintenance Manual with new codes, computer processes, or new legal information such as state regulations.

Creates any in-house publications, pamphlets, flyers, or print materials.

Enters employee time and leave into timekeeping system.

Studies building code; attends seminars to maintain ICC-PM certifications.

Performs related work as assigned.

Responsibilities, Requirements and Impacts

Data Responsibility:

Data Responsibility refers to information, knowledge, and conceptions obtained by observation, investigation, interpretation, visualization, and mental creation. Data are intangible and include numbers, words, symbols, ideas, concepts, and oral verbalizations.

Gathers, organizes, analyzes, examines or evaluates data or information and may prescribe action based on these data or information.

People Responsibility:

People include co-workers, workers in other areas or agencies and the general public.

Provides information, guidance or assistance to people that directly facilitates task accomplishment; may give instructions or assignments to helpers or assistants.

Asset Responsibility:

Assets responsibility refers to the responsibility for achieving economies or preventing loss within the organization.

Requires minimum responsibility for only small quantities of low cost items or supplies where opportunities for achieving economies or preventing loss are negligible.

Mathematical Requirements:

Mathematics requires the use of symbols, numbers and formulas to solve mathematical problems.

Uses addition and subtraction, multiplication and division and/or calculates ratios, rates and percents.

Communications Requirements:

Communications involves the ability to read, write, and speak.

Reads technical instructions, procedures manuals and charts to solve practical problems, such as assembly instruction for tools, routine office equipment operating instructions, and in drawing and layout work; composes routine reports and specialized reports, forms, and business letters, with proper format; speaks compound sentences using normal grammar and word form.

Judgment Requirements:

Judgment requirements refer to the frequency and complexity of judgments and decisions given the stability of the work environments, the nature and type of guidance, and the breadth of impact of the judgments and decisions.

Responsible for long range goals, planning and methodologies. Decision-making is focus of the job, affecting entire organization and surrounding population; works in an unstable environment with frequent and significant changes in conditions.

Complexity of Work:

Complexity addresses the analysis, initiative, ingenuity, concentration and creativity, required by the job and the presence of any unusual pressures present in the job.

Performs skilled work involving rules/systems with almost constant problem solving; requires normal attention with short periods of concentration for accurate results and occasional exposure to unusual pressure.

Impact of Errors:

Impact of errors refers to consequences such as damage to equipment and property, loss of data, exposure of the organization to legal liability, and injury or death for individuals.

The impact of errors is moderately serious - affects work unit and may affect other units or citizens.

Physical Demands:

Physical demands refer to the requirements for physical exertion and coordination of limb and body movement.

Performs light to medium work that involves walking or standing virtually all of the time and also involves exerting between 20 and 50 pounds of force on a regular and recurring basis or considerable skill, adeptness and speed in the use of the fingers, hands or limbs in tasks involving close tolerances or limits of accuracy.

Equipment Usage:

Equipment usage involves responsibility for materials, machines, tools, equipment, work aids, and products.

Handles or uses tools or work aids involving some latitude for judgment regarding attainment of a standard or in selecting appropriate items.

Unavoidable Hazards:

Unavoidable hazards refer to the job conditions that may lead to injury or health hazards even though precautions have been taken.

Involves routine and frequent exposure to traffic; moving machinery.

Safety of Others:

Safety of others refers to the level of responsibility for the safety of others, either inherent in the job or to ensure the safety of the general public. (Does not include safety of subordinates).

Requires some responsibility for safety and health of others and/or for occasional enforcement of the standards of public safety or health.

Minimum Education and Experience Requirements:

Requires High School graduation or GED equivalent.

Requires some experience in demolition inspection or closely related experience.

Special Certifications and Licenses:

Must possess or obtain within one year of hire date ICC Property Maintenance Certification and State of West Virginia Property Maintenance Inspector License.

Valid Driver's License

Core Competencies:

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  1. Accountability - takes responsibility for own actions.
  2. Adaptability - responds positively to change.
  3. Communications - listens, speaks and/or writes in a clear, concise and respectful manner.
  4. Customer Service - provides courteous, accessible and quality assistance to internal and external customers.
  5. Initiative - takes proactive action to complete work or resolve issues
  6. Judgment & Decision Making - evaluates issues and makes sound factual decisions.
  7. Professional Development - seeks opportunities to enhance technical skills and job knowledge.
  8. Teamwork & Cooperation - collaborates with others to fulfill the City's vision and achieve departmental goals and strategic objectives.

Additional Qualifications:

  1. Must have the ability to provide documentation verifying legal work status.
  2. Ability to read and speak the English language proficiently in order to communicate and interact with others; to understand and interpret safety instructions; and to respond to internal and external inquiries.
  3. Ability to understand and comply with City and departmental guidelines, policies, procedures and expectations.

This job description has been designed to indicate the general nature and level of work that may be performed by an employee. It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory or list of all of the duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. Supervisors/Managers and/or Department Heads may also assign additional or other lawful duties as may be necessary and/or required. The City reserves the right to modify or change this job description at any time, for any lawful reason, with or without notice. This job description is not, and should not be construed or implied to be a contract, promise or guarantee of continued employment.

The City of Charleston, WV is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The ADA requires the City to provide reasonable accommodations to qualified persons with disabilities. Prospective and current employees are encouraged to discuss ADA accommodations with management.

  • Experience troubleshooting instrumentation in the field
  • Clear documentation habits and attention to detail
  • Willingness to travel to remote sites in field conditions during campaigns
  • Australian citizenship and eligibility to obtain a security clearance

Highly regarded

  • Experience in test and evaluation, range, flight test, launch, aerospace or defence environments
  • Experience with high-speed or high-channel-count data acquisition
  • Scripting or software skills for data processing and automation
  • Experience with data security, controlled transfer or handling sensitive customer data
  • A current NV1 security clearance

Why join us

  • Ownership of the data that proves every test and launch campaign
  • Work that supports Australia's sovereign space and defence capability
  • A capable, close-knit team

title: Maintenance Tecnichian
description:
Position Summary Bennett Heat Treating & Brazing Co., Inc. is seeking an experienced and self-directed Maintenance Manager to oversee all production-equipment and facility-maintenance activities. Although the title is Maintenance Manager, this is an individual-contributor position with no direct reports. The successful candidate will personally troubleshoot, repair, inspect, and maintain electrical and mechanical systems throughout the facility. A strong Maintenance Technician or Maintenance Supervisor who is ready to assume full ownership of the maintenance function may be considered. This position works frequently with 480V electrical systems, DC voltage, water pumps, vacuum pumps, furnace elements, fans, hydraulics, and other industrial equipment. The Maintenance Manager will also maintain repair records, manage preventive maintenance activities, monitor MRO inventory, assist with quality and safety initiatives, and support corrective actions. The current maintenance workload is approximately 40% preventive maintenance and 60% emergency or corrective repair. A major objective of this position is to improve the established maintenance program and move the facility toward a more preventive and reliability-focused model.
Key Responsibilities Electrical Maintenance and Troubleshooting Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair electrical failures affecting production and facility equipment. Work safely with electrical systems operating at up to 480V AC, as well as DC-voltage systems. Inspect electrical components, wiring, connections, motors, controls, switches, relays, contactors, heating elements, and related equipment. Use appropriate testing equipment to identify electrical faults. Replace defective electrical components according to applicable safety requirements. Identify recurring electrical failures and recommend permanent corrective actions. Report unsafe electrical conditions immediately. Coordinate specialized electrical work with qualified contractors when required. Maintain accurate documentation of electrical repairs and recurring problems. Electrical issues are currently the most common type of maintenance emergency within the facility. Mechanical Maintenance Troubleshoot and repair mechanical systems and production equipment. Maintain water pumps, vacuum pumps, furnace elements, fans, motors, hydraulic equipment, and related components. Inspect equipment for wear, vibration, leaks, overheating, unusual noise, and other signs of mechanical failure. Repair or replace defective bearings, seals, motors, belts, pumps, fans, valves, and mechanical components. Support alignment, adjustment, lubrication, and replacement activities. Evaluate whether equipment should be repaired, rebuilt, or replaced. Reduce repeat failures through root-cause analysis and corrective action. Maintain orderly tools, parts, and maintenance work areas. Vacuum Furnace Maintenance Perform routine and corrective maintenance on vacuum furnaces and related systems. Support the maintenance of vacuum pumps, heating elements, fans, controls, and supporting equipment. Investigate vacuum leaks, heating issues, electrical faults, and equipment-performance concerns. Coordinate furnace downtime and repairs with Operations and Production. Learn facility-specific furnace systems through company-provided on-site training. Maintain accurate records of furnace inspections, repairs, and preventive maintenance activities. Previous vacuum furnace experience is a strong advantage but is not required. The company will provide on-site training to a candidate with strong transferable electrical and mechanical skills. Preventive and Predictive Maintenance Maintain and improve the established preventive maintenance program. Schedule preventive maintenance according to equipment condition, manufacturer recommendations, usage, production priorities, and operational risk. Coordinate maintenance activities with Operations and Quality. Complete inspections, lubrication, adjustments, component replacements, and other scheduled tasks. Track recurring failures and adjust maintenance intervals when appropriate. Apply predictive maintenance methods when practical. Reduce dependence on emergency repairs by identifying issues before equipment failure. Maintain preventive maintenance records and completion logs. Recommend improvements that increase equipment reliability and service life. The facility currently operates at approximately a 40% preventive and 60% reactive maintenance mix. The long-term goal is to move toward a predominantly preventive maintenance model. Production Equipment Repair Respond promptly to production-equipment failures. Determine the cause, scope, and operational impact of equipment problems. Prioritize repairs based on safety, production requirements, quality risks, and equipment criticality. Communicate estimated downtime and repair status to Operations and Production. Complete emergency and corrective repairs safely and efficiently. Test equipment after repairs to confirm safe and reliable operation. Monitor recently repaired equipment for recurring problems. Escalate concerns when specialized vendor or contractor support is required. Facility and Building Maintenance Schedule and complete routine and emergency facility maintenance. Inspect building systems and infrastructure for safety and operational concerns. Coordinate repairs involving utilities, lighting, electrical systems, mechanical systems, plumbing, HVAC, and structural components. Support general maintenance throughout the industrial facility. Coordinate qualified vendors and contractors when specialized services are required. Monitor contractor work for safety, quality, and completion. Maintain documentation related to building repairs and facility-service activities. MRO Inventory and Maintenance Planning Maintain an organized inventory of maintenance, repair, and operations parts. Identify critical spare parts for production equipment. Monitor stock levels and reorder points. Help prevent production delays caused by unavailable replacement parts. Plan repairs by identifying necessary labor, tools, components, materials, and contractor support. Coordinate with purchasing and approved vendors to obtain parts. Evaluate component cost, availability, quality, and lead times. Maintain organized maintenance storage and work areas. Document part usage and replacement history. Quality Management System Support Perform maintenance activities in accordance with machine and Quality Management System requirements. Maintain complete and accurate repair and preventive maintenance records. Work with Quality personnel when equipment performance may affect product quality. Support internal, customer, supplier, and external audits. Assist with corrective action requests related to equipment, facilities, processes, or safety. Participate in root-cause analysis. Implement and document approved corrective actions. Provide maintenance records and supporting documentation during reviews and audits. Safety, Health, and Environmental Support Follow all workplace safety requirements and industrial maintenance procedures. Identify and help resolve health, safety, and environmental concerns. Apply lockout/tagout and hazardous-energy-control procedures. Report unsafe equipment, working conditions, or operating practices. Ensure equipment is properly shut down and secured before maintenance. Coordinate repairs for conditions that create safety or environmental risks. Help ensure contractors follow facility safety requirements. Promote safe work practices throughout the maintenance function. Maintenance Documentation Maintain accurate daily maintenance logs. Document equipment failures, troubleshooting steps, completed repairs, replacement parts, downtime, and follow-up actions. Maintain preventive maintenance schedules and completion records. Track open maintenance requests. Record recurring equipment problems and corrective measures. Provide management with updates regarding equipment condition and maintenance priorities. Maintain records required for quality, safety, and audit purposes. Process Improvement and Training Identify opportunities to improve equipment reliability, workflow, safety, and production efficiency. Recommend solutions for recurring equipment or facility problems. Participate in process-improvement initiatives. Help standardize maintenance procedures and documentation. Train employees on equipment care, basic troubleshooting, operating considerations, and maintenance-related safety when appropriate. Share technical knowledge with Operations, Production, and Quality personnel. Support the development of a preventive maintenance culture.
Required Qualifications Must-Have Qualifications At least four years of industrial, manufacturing, production, or facility-maintenance experience. Hands-on electrical troubleshooting experience. Ability to safely work with or around 480V AC and DC electrical systems. Strong mechanical troubleshooting and repair experience. Experience maintaining pumps, motors, fans, hydraulic systems, or comparable industrial equipment. Knowledge of preventive and corrective maintenance. Ability to diagnose equipment failures independently. Familiarity with maintenance planning and MRO inventory. Strong understanding of industrial safety practices. Willingness to work in an industrial environment. Ability to maintain accurate repair, inspection, and preventive maintenance records. Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills. Self-directed work style with initiative and perseverance. Ability to prioritize multiple maintenance requests. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Ability to work effectively with Operations, Production, Quality, management, contractors, and vendors. Willingness to occasionally support urgent repairs outside regular working hours. Preferred Qualifications Vacuum furnace maintenance experience. Experience with vacuum pumps and furnace heating elements. PLC troubleshooting experience. Hydraulics and pneumatics experience. Welding experience. HVAC maintenance experience. Predictive maintenance experience. Experience supporting a Quality Management System. Experience with corrective action requests and root-cause analysis. Familiarity with computerized maintenance management systems. Lockout/tagout training. Previous maintenance leadership or facility-ownership experience. Technical education, apprenticeship, license, or certification in industrial maintenance, electrical systems, mechanical systems, or a related field.

Mycronic is a global high-tech company whose innovative solutions have been advancing electronics technology for over 50 years. Today we continue to grow and serve customers in an expanding variety of industries. What we do impacts the future of technology, and in turn, the way we live our lives tomorrow.

Overview

We are looking for an experienced Senior Semiconductor Equipment Engineer (Mechanical) to join Mycronic's Global Technologies division working within Surfx Technologies, our Applied Plasma business line. It is an exciting time to join our team!

Surfx Technologies is a fast-growing company that offers atmospheric argon plasmas for the high-volume manufacturing of integrated circuits, semiconductor packages, printed circuit boards, and other microelectronic devices. These automated plasma machines are an excellent choice for surface cleaning, activation, and metal oxide removal. The Surfx Technologies team delivers this atmospheric argon plasma technology for assembled products that are less likely to corrode, delaminate, or come unglued during their lifetime. Our customers include the world's leading semiconductor manufacturers and technology companies.

The Senior Semiconductor Equipment Engineer (Mechanical) is responsible for the design, development, and continuous improvement of automated plasma equipment for the semiconductor industry. This role leads mechanical engineering activities from initial concept and system design through prototyping, testing, validation, and product launch, applying strong expertise in mechatronics to develop high-precision, reliable equipment. The engineer works closely with electrical, controls, software, and process engineering teams to integrate complex systems and ensure equipment meets performance, quality, and reliability requirements. In collaboration with sales, service, and management, this role also supports troubleshooting, addresses technical challenges, and identifies opportunities to enhance equipment functionality, manufacturability, and overall performance.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to team members, contributing to a collaborative engineering environment and the development of innovative equipment solutions

  • 10 years plus of mechanical tool design experience, preferably in the semiconductor industry or working with high precision equipment applications
  • Proficiency in SolidWorks, GD&T, and Microsoft project
  • Knowledge of equipment cleanliness and safety standards (ISO, CE, UL, SEMI, NFPA, etc.)
  • Strong verbal and written communication as well as project management skills
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers; work both independently and effectively within a team
  • Travel domestically and internationally to customer sites, as needed
  • Must be currently authorized to work full-time in the United States; this position does not offer visa sponsorship
  • Prior experience with providing technical guidance and project management mentorship to team members, fostering knowledge sharing, effective planning, cross-functional collaboration

Why Join Us?

At Mycronic, we love what we do, but most importantly who we do it with. Because to us the relationships we have with our customers and each other are the keys to success. Take part in the excitement of working with innovative people and global businesses who are elevating today's standards in modern electronics. Share in the responsibility of bringing great ideas to life within an inclusive culture that not only promotes personal growth and embraces diversity but depends upon it.

title: Senior Data Engineer - USA
description:

Job Overview

We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer based in the US to design, build, and maintain robust data pipelines and scalable infrastructure across our cloud platform. In this role, you will play a key part in enabling Data Products throughout their lifecycle—sourcing data via batch and stream processing, optimizing data architecture, and ensuring data quality. You will collaborate closely with Data Scientists and ML Engineers to automate workflows and deploy resilient data pipelines in production.

  • Work Location / Employment: US-based (Remote / Hybrid) — Must be authorized to work in the United States.

    • Tech Stack & Key Technologies

    • Cloud Platforms: AWS (Redshift, Glue, EMR, MWAA, S3) & GCP (BigQuery, Cloud Storage)

    • Languages & Frameworks: Python, PySpark, SQL (advanced optimization & tuning)

    • Data Engineering & Ops: Batch & Stream Processing, ETL/ELT Pipelines, Data Modeling, Data Warehousing, Orchestration

    • DevOps, Infrastructure & Tools: Docker, Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, UNIX/Linux environments, MLOps best practices

      • Key Responsibilities

      • Pipeline Architecture & Development: Design, build, and deploy scalable, decoupled, and high-performance data pipelines for batch and streaming data ingestion into Data Lakes and Data Warehouses.

      • ETL/ELT Processing: Develop and optimize efficient data pipelines using Python, PySpark, and advanced SQL.

      • Collaboration with ML & Data Science: Partner with Data Scientists and ML Engineers to build resilient pipelines, automate MLOps workflows, and gather model interaction data to support retraining loops.

      • Performance Optimization & Monitoring: Continuously monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize pipeline execution, query performance, and storage resource utilization across cloud platforms.

      • Data Quality & Governance: Implement data quality frameworks and testing controls to ensure data integrity, reliability, and governance across raw and curated datasets.

      • DevOps & Standards: Apply MLOps and DevOps best practices, maintain CI/CD pipelines, use Docker for containerization, and document technical standards and architectures.

        • Qualifications & Requirements

        • Experience: 5+ years of experience in Data Engineering, with a proven track record of designing and running large-scale data systems.

        • Core Languages: Mastery of Python and advanced SQL (query optimization and performance tuning).

        • Cloud & Big Data Tools: Hands-on experience with AWS (Redshift, Glue, EMR, MWAA, S3) or GCP (BigQuery) and modern data processing engines (PySpark).

        • Engineering Ecosystem: Proficiency with UNIX environments, Docker, Git, and CI/CD pipelines.

        • Data & ML Lifecycle: Solid understanding of data structures, batch/streaming processing, and familiarity with MLOps or the ML deployment lifecycle.

        • Communication: Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.

          • Nice to Have

          • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform).

          • Experience building and maintaining scalable REST APIs.

          • Exposure to prompt engineering workflows or generative AI data pipelines.

Why join Coderio?

At Coderio, we value talent regardless of location. We are a remote-first company, passionate about technology, collaborative work, and fair compensation. We offer an inclusive, challenging environment with real opportunities for growth. If you are motivated to build impactful solutions, we’re looking for you.


Apply now.

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

title: Sterile Cleaning Technician
description:
Position Summary

The Sterile Cleanroom Cleaning Technician plays a critical role in maintaining environmental control, contamination prevention, and regulatory compliance of ISO-classified cleanroom suites within a 503A compounding pharmacy environment. This individual is responsible for executing daily and monthly cleaning and disinfection protocols across hazardous and non-hazardous sterile compounding suites, weighing/mixing rooms, gowning areas, and corridors. The role ensures strict adherence to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), United States Pharmacopeia guidelines (USP 797, USP 800), and state regulations to maintain audit readiness and batch safety.


Key Responsibilities & Essential Functions


Daily & Monthly Cleanroom Sanitation Execution

  • Execute daily cleaning and disinfection procedures for Primary Engineering Controls (BSCs, LAFWs, Lyophilizers), ISO 5 zones, pass-throughs, easy surfaces (e.g., carts, benches, chairs, pump stands, crimping stations, viable/non-viable stations), and floors prior to compounding activities.
  • Perform comprehensive monthly cleaning of all ISO-8 or better controlled areas, including ceilings, walls, pass-throughs, equipment, and floors using designated sporicidal solutions, sterile Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA), and automated decontamination systems (TOMI Steamiest Surface Select).
  • Adhere strictly to clean-to-dirty workflows, top-to-bottom surface wiping (ceilings, walls, easy surfaces, floors), and prescribed overlapping stroke patterns. Maintain required contact/dwell times (e.g., 10-minute sporicidal dwell times) for chemical agents.
  • Fully gown and garb in accordance with facility sterile gowning SOPs. Don and remove additional hazardous PPE/gowns and boot covers when servicing Hazardous Drug (HD) suites and weighing/mixing areas to prevent cross-contamination.

Material, Equipment & Solution Management

  • Accurately prepare, label, and use facility-approved cleaning agents (e.g., Peridox RTU®, HYPO-CHLOR®, Sterile 70% IPA, Tomi Solution) according to manufacturer and SOP specifications.
  • Prepare TexQ mops and mop head covers using sterile dry wipes. Ensure stainless steel mop heads are properly handled for daily steam sterilization/autoclaving. Manage area-captive mops and storage carts to ensure strict separation between hazardous, non-hazardous, and corridor zones.

Waste Removal & Pass-Through Transfer

  • Perform structured trash removal across cleanroom suites, hazardous areas, pre-/post-gowning rooms, and weighing/mixing suites. Double-bag hazardous waste.

Documentation & Compliance Support

  • Accurately complete and sign all Daily Cleanroom Cleaning Logs (Hazard, Non-Hazard, Corridor, Weighing/Mixing) and Monthly Cleaning Logs (or corresponding pharmacy software entries) immediately after cleaning cycles.
  • Assist Quality Assurance in keeping cleaning logs and assessment forms fully up-to-date and audit ready. Perform required cleaning procedures following new equipment introductions, facility maintenance, or environmental monitoring re-certifications.
  • Maintain flexibility to adapt to changing operational priorities and complete additional cleaning or quality-related tasks as requested by management.
