title: Senior Information System Security Officer
description:
Senior Information System Security Officer (ISSO) / POA&M Remediation and Compliance Specialist

Position Summary

The Senior Information System Security Officer (ISSO) / POA&M Remediation and Compliance Specialist will provide senior-level cybersecurity, risk management, and compliance support for the Acquisition Systems Branch's PRM2 solution. This position will work closely with the PRM2 ISSO, system owners, technical teams, and other Government stakeholders to ensure the system complies with Department of Homeland Security cybersecurity requirements.

The Senior ISSO will support security assessments, maintain required security documentation, coordinate vulnerability remediation, monitor Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), and support the timely achievement and maintenance of an Interim Authority to Operate (IATO) and Authority to Operate (ATO). The position requires practical experience translating identified security weaknesses into documented, trackable, and verifiable remediation actions.

Key Responsibilities

  1. ISSO and Cybersecurity Compliance Support
  • Provide senior-level cybersecurity and compliance support to the PRM2 ISSO, system owner, and applicable Government stakeholders.
  • Assist with maintaining PRM2 compliance with DHS information technology security requirements.
  • Provide cybersecurity documentation, analysis, and technical support during security assessments, audits, authorization activities, and recurring compliance reviews.
  • Coordinate with application, database, infrastructure, operations, and security personnel to address cybersecurity requirements affecting PRM2.
  • Monitor changes to the PRM2 environment and evaluate their potential impact on the system's security authorization and compliance posture.
  • Support implementation of security best practices throughout the system development and operational lifecycle.
  • Participate in cybersecurity audits and assessments as required.
  1. Authority to Operate and Interim Authority to Operate
  • Support the planning, preparation, coordination, and maintenance of the security documentation required to obtain and maintain an ATO.
  • Support achievement of an IATO when required prior to obtaining the full ATO.
  • Ensure authorization activities and supporting documentation comply with DHS MD 4300A and applicable DHS cybersecurity requirements.
  • Coordinate the collection, review, and organization of security evidence needed to support authorization decisions.
  • Track authorization milestones, open compliance actions, responsible parties, dependencies, and completion dates.
  • Work with technical and program stakeholders to resolve deficiencies that may delay an IATO or ATO decision.
  • Support the maintenance of authorization documentation after approval to ensure the system remains compliant as configurations, technologies, and operating conditions change.
  1. POA&M Management and Remediation
  • Develop, review, maintain, and track POA&M entries associated with security assessments, vulnerability scans, audits, penetration testing, configuration reviews, and other compliance activities.
  • Validate that each POA&M item clearly identifies the security weakness, affected component, risk, corrective action, responsible owner, required resources, milestones, and target completion date.
  • Coordinate with technical teams and system stakeholders to develop practical corrective action plans for identified weaknesses.
  • Monitor remediation progress and identify overdue, delayed, or blocked corrective actions.
  • Facilitate recurring POA&M review meetings with technical owners and Government stakeholders.
  • Review remediation evidence to determine whether corrective actions have been completed and adequately documented.
  • Support requests to close, extend, revise, or otherwise update POA&M items based on documented remediation status.
  • Maintain traceability between findings, POA&M actions, remediation evidence, vulnerability scan results, and applicable security requirements.
  • Escalate material risks, missed milestones, and unresolved findings to the PRM2 ISSO and appropriate program leadership.
  1. Security Documentation
  • Develop and maintain an updated IT Security Plan that describes the approach, methods, controls, and safeguards used to comply with Government and DHS cybersecurity requirements.
  • Create, review, and update security documentation required to support assessments and authorization activities.
  • Ensure security documentation reflects the system's current operating environment, architecture, boundaries, technologies, interfaces, and implemented safeguards.
  • Maintain supporting evidence in an organized and audit-ready manner.
  • Coordinate document reviews, comments, revisions, approvals, and version control with Government and contractor stakeholders.
  • Identify documentation gaps and work with responsible parties to obtain or develop missing information.
  1. Vulnerability Management and Patching
  • Coordinate and provide pertinent vulnerability scans for the PRM2 environment.
  • Review vulnerability scan results to identify findings affecting the operating system, database, application, and other components within the PRM2 authorization boundary.
  • Work with system administrators, database administrators, application teams, and infrastructure personnel to prioritize and execute required remediation and patching.
  • Track vulnerabilities from initial identification through remediation, verification, and closure.
  • Validate remediation through rescanning, technical evidence, or other approved verification methods.
  • Identify vulnerabilities that cannot be remediated within required timeframes and ensure they are appropriately documented and tracked.
  • Provide the PRM2 ISSO with updates concerning patches affecting PRM2 and its authorization boundary, excluding the DEC AWS environment where specified.
  • Communicate patch status, remediation dependencies, known exceptions, and residual risks to Government stakeholders.
  • Support the establishment and maintenance of an ongoing vulnerability management process.
  1. Configuration and Change Management
  • Notify and update the PRM2 ISSO regarding hardware and software configuration changes affecting the PRM2 authorization boundary.
  • Review proposed configuration changes for potential cybersecurity and compliance impacts.
  • Support security impact analyses for changes to operating systems, databases, applications, interfaces, infrastructure, and system components.
  • Ensure approved changes are accurately reflected in security plans, diagrams, inventories, procedures, and authorization documentation.
  • Coordinate with change management and technical teams to verify that security requirements are addressed before changes are implemented.
  • Monitor configuration changes that may introduce new vulnerabilities, alter existing safeguards, or affect the system's authorization status.
  1. Security Assessment and Audit Support
  • Support internal and external security assessments, compliance reviews, authorization reviews, and cybersecurity audits.
  • Coordinate the collection and submission of requested documentation and security evidence.
  • Assist technical and business stakeholders in preparing for assessor interviews, control reviews, and evidence demonstrations.
  • Analyze assessment findings and coordinate corrective actions with responsible technical owners.
  • Maintain an audit-ready repository of security documentation, scan results, remediation evidence, configuration information, and approval records.
  • Track assessment findings through final resolution and documented closure.
  1. Risk Communication and Reporting
  • Prepare recurring cybersecurity status reports for the PRM2 ISSO, program management, and Government stakeholders.
  • Report the status of ATO and IATO activities, POA&M items, vulnerabilities, patches, open findings, configuration changes, and compliance risks.
  • Identify risks that could affect authorization milestones or continued system operations.
  • Present technical cybersecurity issues in clear business and mission terms for leadership decision-making.
  • Recommend risk treatment actions, remediation priorities, and escalation paths based on the severity and operational impact of identified weaknesses.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in cybersecurity, information technology, computer science, information systems, engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Senior-level experience supporting federal information system security, cybersecurity compliance, or security authorization activities.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting ATO and, when applicable, IATO preparation and maintenance.
  • Experience managing POA&M development, remediation tracking, evidence validation, milestone updates, and closure activities.
  • Experience reviewing and coordinating vulnerability scans, patching, remediation, and verification activities.
  • Experience developing and maintaining cybersecurity plans, assessment documentation, and authorization evidence.
  • Knowledge of federal risk management and information security principles.
  • Ability to interpret cybersecurity requirements and translate them into actionable technical, programmatic, and documentation tasks.
  • Experience supporting security assessments, audits, compliance reviews, and authorization activities.
  • Strong written communication, documentation, coordination, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with Government ISSOs, system owners, assessors, program managers, developers, engineers, administrators, and executive stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting DHS information systems and cybersecurity requirements.
  • Working knowledge of DHS MD 4300A.
  • Experience supporting acquisition, procurement, or mission-business systems.
  • Experience with application, operating system, and database security.
  • Experience performing security impact analyses for hardware, software, configuration, and boundary changes.
  • Experience maintaining security documentation and supporting evidence in an audit-ready environment.
  • Relevant cybersecurity certification such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CAP/CGRC, CASP+, or Security+.

Core Competencies

  • Information System Security Officer support
  • POA&M development and remediation
  • ATO and IATO coordination
  • Cybersecurity compliance
  • Vulnerability and patch management
  • Security assessment support
  • Security documentation
  • Risk identification and reporting
  • Configuration and change management
  • Audit evidence management
  • Corrective action tracking
  • Stakeholder coordination
  • Continuous compliance monitoring

Performance Standards and Milestones

Interim Authority to Operate

  • Support achievement of an IATO within six months of contract award, when an IATO is required.
  • Maintain full compliance with applicable security requirements throughout the IATO process.
  • Performance will be evaluated at each applicable milestone.

Authority to Operate

  • Support achievement of an ATO within 12 months of contract award.
  • Maintain compliance with applicable DHS cybersecurity requirements following authorization.
  • Performance will be evaluated at each applicable milestone.

POA&M and Remediation Performance

  • Maintain current, accurate, and adequately documented POA&M records.
  • Track corrective actions against established milestones and target completion dates.
  • Provide timely notification of delayed, blocked, overdue, or high-risk remediation items.
  • Ensure closure recommendations are supported by sufficient remediation and validation evidence.

Security Documentation

  • Maintain the IT Security Plan and associated security documentation in an accurate and current condition.
  • Update applicable documentation when material system, boundary, configuration, hardware, or software changes occur.
  • Maintain security evidence in an organized and audit-ready format.

Vulnerability and Patch Management

  • Provide applicable vulnerability scan information and coordinate necessary remediation and patching.
  • Notify the PRM2 ISSO of relevant patches and configuration changes affecting the PRM2 authorization boundary.
  • Maintain traceability among vulnerabilities, remediation actions, verification evidence, and closure decisions.

title: Lead Counsel, Public Company Governance & Corporate Programs
description:

  • Identify and implement opportunities to use AI and automation to improve the quality, consistency, scalability, and efficiency of governance work.

  • Develop templates, playbooks, workflows, and supporting infrastructure that strengthen governance operations and reduce unnecessary administrative complexity.

  • Partner with the Director of Corporate Legal and relevant internal stakeholders to continuously improve governance practices and support the organization's long-term growth.

    • Requirements:

    • At least 3–4 years of meaningful in-house experience advising a U.S. publicly traded company on corporate governance matters.

    • Deep knowledge of public company governance, including board and committee practices, director independence, governance policies, stock exchange requirements, and related-party frameworks.

    • Demonstrated ability to independently assess complex governance matters and provide practical, well-reasoned legal recommendations.

    • Extensive experience supporting boards of directors and board committees, with the credibility to advise senior stakeholders and communicate effectively in boardroom settings.

    • Significant responsibility for preparing annual proxy statements and managing annual shareholder meeting processes.

    • Proven experience with governance-related investor engagement and proxy advisor interactions, including the ability to collaborate with Investor Relations and senior leadership as a trusted advisor.

    • Experience independently managing complex, recurring governance programs with strong attention to legal judgment, execution, compliance, and records management.

    • A demonstrated commitment to improving processes, strengthening operational discipline, and making recurring legal programs more effective and scalable.

    • A Juris Doctor (JD) degree from an accredited law school and active bar membership in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

    • Strong written and verbal communication, analytical reasoning, stakeholder management, and organizational skills.

    • Preferred: In-house legal experience at a publicly traded technology or SaaS company.

description:

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?

title: Senior Technical Trainer — Machine Learning
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — Machine Learning based in Spain.

We are seeking a hands-on machine learning practitioner with a passion for teaching to design and deliver engaging technical courses for engineers. In this remote freelance role, you will help learners progress from core machine learning concepts to training and evaluating their own models through practical, lab-based learning. You will collaborate with curriculum specialists and production teams to develop clear lessons, hands-on exercises, and real-world demonstrations. The focus is on sharing your technical expertise through compelling scripts, video presentations, and lab walkthroughs rather than managing production tasks. The initial paid course project typically lasts around three months and can be completed alongside existing professional commitments. With flexible hours and a delivery plan agreed in advance, the opportunity may lead to further projects or a full-time position.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop course content: Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, sections, lessons, practical labs, and notebooks that support progressive learning.

  • Create hands-on learning experiences: Write detailed lab specifications for the dedicated lab development team, then test the completed environments to ensure they work as intended.

  • Write engaging educational scripts: Develop short, story-driven video lessons of approximately six minutes each, making machine learning concepts accessible, intuitive, and relevant to engineers.

  • Deliver technical presentations: Narrate scripted lessons confidently in English and record demonstrations and lab-solution walkthroughs that reinforce key concepts.

  • Apply practical machine learning expertise: Build course material grounded in real experience with training, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models.

  • Incorporate editorial feedback: Work through structured reviews, particularly during the initial course section, and refine content to meet established quality and teaching standards.

  • Collaborate remotely: Coordinate with curriculum and production teams through weekly syncs and Slack, maintaining sufficient time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

  • Focus on teaching and technical content: Partner with the production team, which manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

    • Requirements:

    • Hands-on machine learning experience: Demonstrated ability to train, evaluate, and ship models using frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.

    • Strong technical communication skills: Ability to explain machine learning concepts, including the reasoning behind different approaches, clearly to engineers who are new to the field.

    • Excellent English proficiency: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to write natural scripts, deliver clear narration, and communicate confidently on camera.

    • A genuine passion for teaching: Evidence of enjoying knowledge-sharing through online courses, tutorials, technical talks, workshops, mentoring, or other educational activities.

    • Current technical knowledge: An active interest in machine learning developments and a commitment to continuously learning and improving.

    • Presentation confidence: Comfort presenting technical material on camera in a clear, engaging, and accessible way.

    • Openness to feedback: Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology, collaborate with editors, and improve course content through structured feedback.

    • Preferred qualifications:

      • Experience publishing courses on platforms such as Udemy, Pluralsight, or Coursera, or creating educational content on YouTube.

      • Experience writing a technical book or teaching at a university, bootcamp, or similar educational setting.

      • Practical knowledge of fine-tuning, MLOps, or deploying machine learning models in production.

      • Cloud machine learning certifications related to AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or Databricks.

        • Benefits:

        • Competitive project-based compensation: A fixed fee is agreed upfront for each course, based on its length and technical complexity, with competitive rates for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

        • Flexible working arrangements: Work remotely from anywhere in the world, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement and a delivery schedule agreed in advance.

        • Compatible with existing commitments: Complete the initial freelance course project alongside your current job or other professional responsibilities.

        • Defined project scope: The initial course project typically takes around three months, providing a clear timeframe for planning and delivery.

        • Payment upon completion: Receive the agreed course fee when the completed course is delivered.

        • Long-term career potential: Successful collaboration may lead to additional course projects or a full-time opportunity as part of a growing trainer network.

        • Dedicated production support: Focus on instructional content and teaching while the production team handles editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

        • Collaborative remote environment: Work closely with curriculum and production specialists through regular team syncs and Slack communication.

        • Professional visibility: Showcase your technical expertise and teaching ability by developing practical learning experiences for a broad engineering audience.

title: Routing Engineer - Intern
description:
If you haven’t checked out our Realistic Job Preview, take a look before applying:

Acutec is an employee-owned manufacturer of flight-critical components & assemblies for Aerospace & Defense markets, striving to be the most respected supplier and sought after company in the Aerospace industry, earning the respect of our customers, employees and the community. With a library of over 12,000 different components manufactured in both continuous run and single run production, we have parts on almost every plane and helicopter in the sky and on the programs of the future that will advance commercial aerospace, space travel, and defense in the coming decades. Our employees are our greatest asset. We prepare to be lucky, embrace change and continuously improve by investing in employee development and training and giving them the best tools and resources to continually exceed customer expectations. At Acutec, we want to help you continue to learn and grow in your career, and our ASCEND internship program is designed to give you the experience you need to develop your skills and gain valuable experience through hands-on training. Interns have the opportunity to collaborate with teams partnering with premiere Aerospace customers.

We are hiring for our ASCEND program where students can present a capstone project to the CEO/President of the organization at the end of their intern experience. Interns from Acutec have gone on to fulfilling careers both at Acutec and other various Aerospace organizations. Multiple members of Acutec’s management team began working as interns before they graduated from high school or college. An internship with Acutec can be a springboard to success post-graduation!

This intern will work with skilled leaders in the field.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Collaboration – The small team environment at this facility ensures engagement, collaboration, and support. Work with the best of the best: in-house and worldwide experts in tooling, equipment, and software development.

• Community Engagement – we are focused on being engaged with our community and giving back! As a part of our team, you will be able to participate in many community service events and make it a priority to make donations to causes and programs our team members are involved with.

• Interface successfully with assigned teams.

• Assist with the improvement of policies and processes to enhance productivity and eliminate waste.

• Assist with strategic improvement initiatives within the organization to improve key features such as quality, delivery, cost, and safety.

• Assist with day-to-day tasks as well as special projects as assigned

• Completes projects accurately and as assigned, meets deadlines under normal working conditions.

• Establish and maintain a positive relationship with associates. Demonstrate the ability to work with others to achieve company and department objectives.

• Handle multiple tasks, prioritize according to importance, and follow instructions and works well under pressure; see additional work and responsibilities

• Demonstrate the ability to grasp and follow instructions without constant supervision.

• Successfully complete all assigned trainings including Acutec Culture training and Safety training.

Key Roles

• Assist in the creation of Acutec’s new planning tool.

• When necessary, collaborate with manufacturing planning to assist in the creation of routing for new parts.

• Utilize proprietary software to connect our new planning application to our current work instructions application.

• Translate legacy manufacturing routing into dynamic records within the new system.

title: Senior IT Operations Engineer
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior IT Operations Engineer based in the United States.

The Senior IT Operations Engineer will play a key role in building secure, scalable, and automated internal technology systems across a global organization. This hands-on individual contributor position combines IT operations, cloud engineering, identity and access management, systems integration, and AI enablement. You will design and maintain automations that connect business applications, streamline workflows, and reduce manual effort across teams. Working closely with Security, Engineering, People, Support, and go-to-market functions, you will turn operational challenges into reliable technical solutions. You will also help govern emerging AI tools and integrations, ensuring that innovation is balanced with security, privacy, and appropriate access controls. This is an opportunity to take ownership of meaningful projects, influence technical direction, and improve the employee experience within a collaborative, DevOps-oriented environment.

Accountabilities:

  • Design, build, and maintain automation and integrations across AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and enterprise applications using services such as AWS Lambda, API Gateway, REST APIs, webhooks, and integration platforms.

  • Own and improve automation workflows using Okta Workflows, Workato, and related technologies, identifying opportunities to eliminate repetitive tasks and streamline internal processes.

  • Define infrastructure as code using Terraform or similar tools and deploy changes through CI/CD pipelines, maintaining reliable, repeatable, and secure infrastructure.

  • Develop and maintain scripts in Python, Go, Node.js, or other suitable languages to connect systems, resolve workflow issues, and support business-critical processes.

  • Manage integrations across business applications, including connections involving Salesforce, Slack, Jira, identity platforms, and data warehouses.

  • Implement and maintain backup and recovery processes for critical systems, including Jira, GitHub, and automation platforms.

  • Lead the rollout and ongoing administration of enterprise AI tools, including Claude and other approved assistants, connectors, and internal agents.

  • Host and govern Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and related infrastructure, assessing each connector’s access scope, security implications, and suitability before deployment.

  • Administer identity and access management platforms, including Okta and Auth0, with responsibility for authentication, provisioning, access policies, MFA, device trust, SCIM, and joiner-mover-leaver processes.

  • Integrate identity platforms with access governance solutions and support the implementation of appropriate role-based access controls and security practices.

  • Manage security and edge services, including DNS, public key infrastructure (PKI), web application firewalls, rate limiting, certificates, and email authentication protocols such as SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

  • Support customer-facing web infrastructure, including CloudFront-hosted sites, coordinate hosting changes with external web agencies, and collaborate with security teams on technical findings.

  • Administer workplace collaboration and productivity platforms, including Google Workspace, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Slack, and GitLab, while coordinating with owners of other enterprise applications.

  • Resolve Tier 2 and Tier 3 service desk escalations, troubleshoot Windows and macOS devices, manage vendor support cases, and collaborate on device-management and access policies.

  • Maintain clear technical documentation, including runbooks, architecture notes, process guides, handoff materials, and accurate inventories of hardware, software, and IT resources.

  • Manage relationships with IT vendors and contractors, identify operational weaknesses, and continuously improve infrastructure reliability, scalability, security, and maintainability.

  • Serve as a North American point of contact for urgent IT requests, escalations, and production incidents when other members of the global team are unavailable.

  • Exercise independent judgment, lead projects from initial requirements through rollout, and balance planned engineering work with operational support needs.

    • Requirements:

    • At least 7 years of experience in IT operations, DevOps, cloud engineering, identity and access management, or a related technical field, including at least 2 years focused on IT process automation. Equivalent experience may be considered.

    • Hands-on experience administering Okta, including Okta Workflows, and working with Auth0 custom logic such as Actions or rules.

    • Working knowledge of AWS services, including Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront, and IAM, along with GCP environments, projects, IAM, and BigQuery.

    • Experience building and maintaining integrations using Workato or a comparable integration platform as a service (iPaaS).

    • Proficiency in at least one automation or scripting language, such as Python, Go, or Node.js, with practical experience using REST APIs and webhooks.

    • Experience with infrastructure as code, using Terraform, Pulumi, or similar technologies, and with CI/CD pipelines, preferably GitLab.

    • Practical experience with Claude or comparable large language model tools, connectors, and MCP servers, including an understanding of the associated security and access-control considerations.

    • Experience managing Cloudflare services, including DNS, certificates, or Workers, and strong Google Workspace administration skills.

    • Solid understanding of single sign-on technologies, including SAML and OIDC, as well as MFA, SCIM, role-based access control, DNS, and email authentication.

    • Familiarity with mobile device management platforms such as Kandji or Microsoft Intune, along with experience troubleshooting Windows and macOS endpoints.

    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to investigate complex technical issues across interconnected systems.

    • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with a commitment to clear documentation and effective technical handoffs.

    • Sound judgment and discretion when handling confidential information, identity data, security-sensitive systems, and internal business information.

    • Ability to work independently with limited oversight, establish technical direction, prioritize competing demands, and lead projects through successful implementation.

    • A security-first mindset, with the ability to assess access permissions, anticipate risks, and design automation around business needs and employee experience.

    • A generalist mindset and willingness to learn new tools and technologies across identity, cloud infrastructure, security, automation, and enterprise SaaS.

    • Preferred experience with Salesforce Apex or Flow, custom MCP servers, AI agent frameworks, SQL, and data platforms such as BigQuery, Snowflake, or Databricks.

    • Additional experience with Azure or other public cloud platforms, SaaS security and access governance tools, HRIS-driven provisioning, SOC 2 or ISO 27001, and vulnerability management is beneficial.

    • Relevant certifications in AWS, GCP, Okta, or related technical disciplines are an advantage.

    • Authorization to work in the United States without employer-sponsored visa support is required, and candidates should ideally be located in the Eastern United States.

      • Benefits:

      • Base salary: $145,000–$165,000 USD annually.

      • Annual bonus opportunity: 13%–15%, in addition to base compensation.

      • Remote work: Remote position for candidates based in the United States, with a preference for the Eastern Time Zone.

      • Technical ownership: Opportunity to lead projects independently, set technical direction, and influence the design of internal systems and automation.

      • Broad technical exposure: Hands-on work across cloud platforms, identity management, cybersecurity, AI enablement, integrations, and enterprise productivity tools.

      • Collaborative environment: Work with a global IT team and cross-functional partners in Security, Engineering, People, Support, and other business functions.

      • Professional development: Opportunities to expand technical expertise and contribute to emerging AI-enabled workflows and modern IT operations practices.

      • Inclusive culture: A workplace committed to collaboration, innovation, diversity, equality, and ensuring every team member feels heard and valued.

title: Fraud Strategy Specialist - Card Issuance
description:
About Us

At Félix, we are building the indispensable financial companion for Latinos in the US. We combine an AI-powered, conversational-first interface with real-time financial infrastructure to make cross-border money movement as easy as sending a text. Starting with fast, affordable remittances powered by AI and crypto rails, we are expanding into credit, savings, and wallet services to support the complete immigrant financial journey. Our ambition is to deliver a white-glove financial experience with the simplicity of a conversation to a community the traditional financial system has historically overlooked.

We are a hyper-growth Series C company, backed by over $300 million in funding from top-tier global investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, QED, Castle Island, Switch Ventures, HTwenty, Monashees, General Catalyst Customer Value Fund. This isn't just about the numbers; it's a testament to the trust our investors have in our vision and our team. Additionally, Félix was selected as an “Endeavour Entrepreneur” and was a recipient of the CrossTech Fintech Startups Award.

Joining Félix means you will be part of a team building a legacy, a company that will outlive us all. This is a rare opportunity to apply your skills to a deeply meaningful mission—serving a community that has been underserved for too long because we are obsessed with our customers. We get things done with urgency and focus, driven by extreme ownership over our impact. We collaborate without ego, fostering radical transparency and fierce loyalty so we can grow together. Because we aim for insanely great rather than just good enough, we stay insatiably curious—always experimenting, building the future today, and delivering a product that truly makes our users' lives better.

About the Role


You'll join the Fraud Strategy team at Felix — the team responsible for how we detect, decide on, and prevent fraud across every product, payment rail, and country we operate in. We sit at the intersection of Data Science, Product, Operations, and Risk: we turn fraud signals into decisions, design the controls that stop bad actors, and make sure good customers move through with as little friction as possible. As Felix grows into new rails, new products and new markets across Latin America, our job is to let the business say yes to growth without letting fraud scale alongside it.
Felix is building a new card issuance program, and with it, a new fraud surface: we'll own authorization decisioning end-to-end and carry direct exposure to card network fraud and dispute monitoring (Visa/Mastercard-style thresholds). This is a build role — there's no existing card fraud stack to inherit, and our infrastructure partner isn't a fraud team, so the decisioning architecture gets built by this role, from the ground up.
We're looking for a Fraud Strategist to own that build: turn our vendor's area-of- responsibility split into a real decisioning architecture, keep us under network fraud and dispute thresholds from day one, and design the authorization strategy using the full toolkit — step-up authentication, velocity controls, holds, product-level friction — not rules as the default answer. Rules are a last resort here, not the first move.


Responsibilities


  • Own fraud strategy for the card issuance program end-to-end — from pre-launch risk assessment through steady-state monitoring after go-live.
  • Translate our infrastructure partner's area-of-responsibility split into an operating decisioning model. Card issuing infrastructure providers generally aren't fraud teams — authorization decisioning, onboarding fraud, velocity controls, and cross-account detection sit with Felix, and this role turns that into actual controls, not just a documented split.
  • Design and own authorization decisioning for card transactions: approve/decline logic, 3DS/SCA step-up, velocity limits, cross-card/cross-account linkage — biased toward product and action-based controls over static rule sprawl.
  • Own network-level fraud health. Monitor fraud-to-sales and dispute ratios against card network thresholds (Visa's VAMP, Mastercard's excessive chargeback program) and build the early-warning system that keeps us out of penalty territory before it's a problem, not after.
  • Build the cardholder fraud lifecycle: onboarding risk, first-card-use monitoring, BIN- and portfolio-level pattern detection.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to embed controls into the card issuance and wallet funding/spend flow directly, instead of bolting rules on after the product ships.
  • Own card dispute and chargeback strategy (network reason codes, representment approach) in partnership with Fraud Operations.
  • Be the fraud voice in ongoing vendor conversations — our current issuing infrastructure partner and any future ones — keeping the requirements doc current as the program evolves.
  • Use SQL/BigQuery hands-on to size fraud exposure, backtest authorization thresholds, and monitor post-launch indicators, iterating fast as real transaction data comes in.
  • Build the playbook, not just the launch — so the next card product or market expansion plugs in without renegotiating fraud ownership from scratch.


Requirements


  • 4–7+ years in fraud/risk strategy, with direct, hands-on experience in card authorization decisioning — issuer, acquirer, program manager, or processor side.
  • Working knowledge of card network mechanics: authorization/clearing/settlement flow, 3DS/SCA, network fraud-monitoring programs (Visa VAMP or equivalent, Mastercard excessive chargeback programs), and dispute reason codes.
  • Experience working with or evaluating BaaS / program-manager card issuing vendors (Stripe Issuing, Marqeta, Galileo, or similar), including fraud AoR/RACI negotiation.
  • Advanced SQL. This person needs to independently query and size risk, not route it to an analyst.
  • Demonstrated bias toward product and action-based fraud controls (step-up auth, holds, dynamic friction) over rules as the default fix.
  • Comfortable building in ambiguity on a 0-to-1 program — translating vendor documentation, legal, and compliance input into an actual operating model.
  • Strong cross-functional communication; this role sits at the intersection of Fraud, Product, Compliance, and an external vendor.
  • Advanced English.

Nice to Have


  • Prior experience specifically with card issuing at a fintech or program manager (rather than acquiring-side or card-not-present e-commerce fraud only).
  • Familiarity with stablecoin-backed card programs or general crypto experience.
  • Spanish or Portuguese, given the LATAM corridor focus.
  • Background in cross-border remittance or LATAM-market fraud.
  • Experience negotiating or managing a BIN sponsor / issuing bank relationship.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary
  • Initial stock options grant
  • Annual performance bonus
  • 401(k)
  • Work model: currently fully remote, with a future transition to a hybrid set up
  • Health, dental, and vision plans
  • Continuous learning opportunities
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Paid parental leave
  • Empowering opportunities for growth in a dynamic entrepreneurial environment



Equal Opportunity Employer

At Félix, we are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, religion, nationality, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, or disability. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruitment, hiring, placement, promotion, training, compensation, benefits, and termination.

title: 3rd Shift Manager
description:
3rd SHIFT MANAGER

MISSION: Chileda's mission is to improve the quality of life for individuals with cognitive and behavior challenges. Chileda's goal is to help students increase their appropriate social behaviors and develop independent living skills, through an enriched learning environment and individualized behavior programming. Chileda's population includes children and young adults with special needs including Autism, Attachment Challenges, related developmental delays, and intensive behavioral needs.

SUMMARY: The Shift Manager is responsible for the overall safety and coordination of the agency's program during the shift assigned. The Shift Manager works collaboratively with other departments, managers, and leads to ensure there is adequate staffing and support for the successful operations during their assigned shift.

REQUIRED EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:

  • Must possess a Bachelor's degree in human services field or at least 3 years of supervisory experience in working with people with developmental disabilities in licensed care.
  • Strong verbal and written communication abilities.
  • Must possess a minimum of intermediate computer skills and other software.
  • Must demonstrate leadership ability and a positive can-do attitude.
  • Ability to handle crisis situations in a safe and effective manner.
  • Experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities.

REPORTS TO:

Overnight Shift Manager: Director of Residential Services

JOB DUTIES:

  • Work collaboratively with all departments and teams to promote respect, learning, safety, collaboration, and compassion through daily shift operations.
  • Know and follow all procedures, including attendance procedures, incident report procedures, emergency intervention procedures, crisis response procedures, serious incident report procedures, etc.
  • Remain current on Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Planning, with the ability to implement these systems when needed. Maintain the ability to direct staff and residents during times of emergency.
  • Work collaboratively with other Shift Managers to plan for appropriate coverage of supervision.
  • Coordinate with program staff to ensure appropriate coverage for residential programming, educational programming, and community outings
  • Develop and maintain daily staff assignments and transition schedules for assigned shifts. Assign staff to areas in which they are trained and competent to work in.
  • Proactively create campus schedules to prepare for the upcoming shifts.
  • Ensure your personal schedule is consistently updated in outlook.
  • Work collaboratively with other Shift Managers and Scheduling Coordinator to call and message staff when staffing shortages occur due to staff absences.
  • Review time management software daily, documenting all attendance concerns, including trainings and failing to punch in or out on a daily basis. Follow up with staff as deemed necessary in the attendance procedure.
  • Provide active supervision of Chileda's campus by completing frequent laps at designated times to supervise employees working during assigned shifts.
  • Monitor employees to ensure all aspects of resident care and treatment are being implemented consistently and thoroughly, providing feedback to employees as needed following Chileda's Performance Counseling Procedure.
  • Ensure all supervised employees adhere to Chileda Policies and Procedures.
  • Respond to help calls and support staff during crisis.
  • Provide instructions for employees to seek medical attention when needed for workplace injuries and follow-up with employees who may need light-duty work.
  • Review, sign, and ensure Employee Accident Reports are completed thoroughly and submitted in Client Management Software.
  • Work with the Health & Wellness Care Staff on duty to report any relevant emergencies to agency administrators, parents/ guardians, licensing agents, and social workers.
  • Communicate any Serious Incidents, including allegations of abuse/neglect and grievances, to the appropriate staff members immediately.
  • Work with the Client's Rights Specialists to conduct investigations, complete documentation, and report to appropriate parties regarding student grievance and resident rights concerns relevant to the assigned shift.
  • Communicate information from the shift to the next Shift Manger regarding incidents, serious incidents, allegations of abuse/neglect, staff incidents, and emergency interventions.
  • Communicate information from the shift to the next Health and Wellness staff regarding any potential Serious Incident Reports, 24 Hour Checks, and student interventions.
  • Complete shift exit report at the end of assigned shift, including student census, serious incidents, and emergency interventions.
  • Report broken or damaged items to the Director of Buildings and Grounds, Director of IT, Education Manager, Residential Manager, and Director of Residential Services.
  • Ensure documentation is completed for all incidents, serious incidents, and emergency interventions during assigned shifts.
  • Update Direct Support Professional schedules in iSolved as needed to reflect changes due to staff switches and for staff needing to make up missed hours or shifts.
  • Work with other Shift Managers, House Managers, and Staff Development Manager to support orientation, mentorships, and retraining occurrences as needed.
  • Act as the shift liaison with parents in the absence of Case Managers, receptionist, and education administration.
  • Attend and participate in team meetings as identified by the direct supervisor.
  • Ensure that the supervisor's cell phone is in working order and on at all times during the shift.
  • Assist staff with Client Management Software login issues.
  • Collaborate with other managers and teachers to facilitate staff breaks.
  • Fill the role of a DSP as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned by supervisor.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to perform the Job Duties of this position successfully. While performing the duties of this job, there is frequent physical interaction with students in fulfilling self-care, behavioral interventions, and educational and recreational programs. The position involves implementing all aspects of Nonviolent Physical Crisis Intervention (CPI), including blocking, grab releases, physical transport, and physical restraint. Must be able to talk and hear to communicate with and exchange information with co-workers. Employees must be able to perform all essential functions without direct risk of harm to others or themselves. Please see the Essential Functions document for specific position physical demands.


WORK ENVIRONMENT: Shift Managers perform job duties across campus. Office work will be completed at a desk using a computer. Non-school days, 1st shift weekends, and all 2nd and 3rd shift work may be performed in the residential homes. First shift school days work may be performed in the classroom setting. Time may be spent outdoors with students in the courtyard.


DISCLAIMER: The statements of this Job Description are intended to describe the general nature of the work being performed and are not assumed to be a complete list of tasks. This Job Description does not establish a contract and are subject to change at Chileda's discretion at any time. Employment at Chileda is at-will.

title: Platform Delivery, Senior Director (Remote)
description:
About our Company:

Medidata is powering smarter treatments and healthier people through digital solutions to support clinical trials. Celebrating over 25 years of ground-breaking technological innovation across more than 38,000 trials and 12 million patients, Medidata offers industry-leading expertise, analytics-powered insights, and one of the largest clinical trial data sets in the industry. More than 1 million registered users across approximately 2,300 customers trust Medidata's seamless, end-to-end platform to improve patient experiences, accelerate clinical breakthroughs, and bring therapies to market faster. A Dassault Systèmes brand (Euronext Paris: FR0014003TT8, DSY.PA), Medidata is headquartered in New York City and has been recognized as a Leader by Everest Group and IDC. Discover more at . Listen to our latest podcast, from Dreamers to Disruptors, and follow us at @Medidata.

About the Team:

Reporting to the VP, Professional Services, EMEA, The Senior Director, Platform Delivery at Medidata serves as the ultimate champion for the customer at the services level. The core mission is to shift the delivery paradigm from fragmented, product-specific interactions to a unified platform-level experience (the Medidata Clinical Cloud). By unifying the Professional Services, Implementation, and Centre of Excellence (COE) teams, this leader ensures clients maximise the value of their tech investment. This, in turn, drives long-term retention, platform adoption, and operational excellence.

Additionally, you will lead our Multi-Product Enterprise Agreement (EA) Platform Delivery Strategy across one or more accounts. As the ultimate owner of multi-product platform delivery, you will manage large-scale governance structures. You will build out specialised Centres of Excellence (COE) and operate as a true peer to Sales, Product, and Engineering. Your goal is to ensure long-term customer health, adoption, and account expansion.

Responsibilities:

Holistic Customer Ownership (Services Level)

  • Unified Delivery Voice: Serve as the escalation point and strategic partner for key accounts, ensuring a seamless journey from post-sales implementation to ongoing lifecycle management.
  • Value Realisation: Shift the services relationship from tactical troubleshooting to strategic partnership, focusing on clinical trial optimisation, faster study build times, and Value.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment: Bridge the gap between Sales, Product/R&D, and Customer Success to ensure client feedback directly shapes the Medidata product roadmap.

Platform-Level Delivery Paradigm

  • De-silo the Experience: Eradicate the "individual product" approach (e.g., treating Rave EDC, RTSM, and eCOA as disconnected silos). Implement a delivery framework that presents Medidata as an interconnected ecosystem.
  • Integrated Solutions Architecture: Ensure implementation blueprints treat data as a continuous stream across the clinical trial lifecycle, optimising workflows for sponsors and CROs rather than configuring isolated modules.

Driving the COE & Implementation Teams

  • Scale the Centre of Excellence (COE): Transform the COE into a powerhouse for global best practices, standardising study build configurations, reusable templates, and governance models that accelerate time-to-live.
  • High-Performance Execution: Mentor a high-calibre implementation team, optimising resource allocation, utilisationrates, and delivery speed without sacrificing quality or regulatory compliance.
  • Change Management: Champion internal and external change management to help clients adopt modern, decentralised, or hybrid clinical trial designs enabled by the platform.

Deep Product & Domain Fluency

  • Technical Credibility: Maintain a strong conceptual and operational understanding of Medidata's core architecture, APIs, and data integrations.
  • Industry Expert: Combine product knowledge with deep life sciences/clinical trials domain expertise. This expertise enables you to speak the language of clinical operations executives. By doing so, you ensure data integrity, compliance (FDA, GCP), and security are baked into every services engagement.

Success Metrics (KPIs)

  • Objective: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
  • Client Success & Retention: Net Revenue Retention (NRR), Gross Revenue Retention (GRR), Net Promoter Score (NPS / CSAT).
  • Platform Adoption: Multi-product attachment rates; percentage of clients using the unified data platform vs. single-point solutions.
  • Operational Efficiency: Time-to-Live (TTL) for study builds, services margin/profitability, and COE template utilisation rates.

The Bottom Line: This role is not about managing software deployment. It is about leading a cultural and operational transformation that positions Medidata Services as an indispensable strategic asset. This transformation unlocks the full clinical and financial potential of the Medidata platform for global clients.

Qualifications:

  • Experience Level: Extensive and proven years of leadership experience within clinical trials life sciences operational delivery, including clinical technology deployment and adoption dealing with complex customer delivery programs Director or Senior Director level.
  • Organisational Transformation: Demonstrated experience turning fragmented, reactive operations into structured, scalable frameworks.
  • Matrix Leadership: Experience managing complex delivery teams consisting of Program/Project Managers, Specialised delivery teams globally, including customer-facing governance leadership.
  • Executive Presence: Outstanding stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence C-suite clients and internal product/sales peers.

Base pay is one part of the Total Rewards that Medidata provides to compensate and recognise employees for their work. Most sales positions are eligible for a commission on the terms of applicable plan documents, and many of Medidata's non-sales positions are eligible for annual bonuses. Medidata believes that benefits should connect you to the support you need when it matters most and provides benefits, including medical, dental, family leave, life and disability insurance, a generous pension, and 25+ paid holidays per year.

We will accept applications on an ongoing basis until we fill the position.

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in Bulgaria.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

title: Relationship Advisor
description:
Role:

The Relationship Advisor is responsible for assisting with member interactions to ensure outstanding service that reflects our commitment to our members. This role actively listens and engages with members to identify needs and recommend appropriate products or services to strengthen relationships and build long-term loyalty. The Relationship Advisor determines eligibility for memberships, opens and closes all types of accounts and updates member information as needed. With a focus on relationship-building and delivering excellent service, this role supports members in achieving their financial goals while ensuring a seamless and positive member experience.


Our Culture:

Our Core Values guide how we serve our members, support one another, and strengthen our community. Our WE Standards define how we show up every day ' across all branches, departments, and roles -ensuring a consistent experience for members and a supportive environment for our teammates. Demonstrating and upholding our Core Values and WE Standards is a fundamental responsibility of every employee and is required in all positions throughout the organization.


Essential Functions & Responsibilities:

  • Assists members with needs relating to products and services offered by TFCU. Cross-sells all credit union products and services. Processes member requests and transactions to include loan applications, opens and closes accounts, ordering checks, placing stop payments on checks, payroll authorizations and allocations, transferring funds from other financial institutions, as well as ordering and maintaining plastic cards.
  • Receives and processes member financial transactions, including deposits, withdrawals and loan payments, transfers amounts from member accounts as directed. Post transactions to member accounts and maintain member records and confidentiality. Balances cash drawer and assists with closing of branch vault as appropriate to branch location.
  • Receives and verifies information on all types of loan applications. Reviews and analyzes loan documentation to determine ratios, credit acceptability, and assesses loan product alternatives in making recommendations for loan decisions. Accountable for securing all loan documentation and disbursing loans to members. Research transactions posted to member accounts and explains transaction postings to member accounts. If an error is discovered, performs any account corrections according to established Credit Union policy and procedure.
  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory programs including but not limited to the Bank Secrecy Act, Office of Foreign Asset Control Program and Customer Identification Program. Assists other department personnel and performs other duties as assigned.

Performance Measurements:

  1. Consistently demonstrates professionalism, courtesy, and empathy in every interaction, ensuring members feel valued and respected. Actively listen to members, accurately assess their needs, and provide clear, helpful solutions that align with The Tyndall Way – WE Standards of Excellence.
  2. Maintain a working knowledge of the credit union's loan policies, procedures and governmental regulations.
  3. Cross sell credit union products and services.
  4. Maintain a professional, courteous, and friendly atmosphere for members and co-workers.
  5. Produce loan documents, reports, and new accounts in a timely fashion with zero errors.
  6. Completes required annual BSA/AML training with a passing grade of 80% or higher. Accurately completes Monetary Instrument logs for the cash purchase of Cashier Checks as needed. Completes required Customer Identification and Red Flags Program requirements to include documentation of discrepancy as needed.
  7. Process an average number of transactions as established in the performance plan.
  8. Have no more than one posting error per month.
  9. Ensure accurate daily cash drawer balancing and proper closing when supporting service operations.
  10. Must pass registration based on the SAFE Act requirements or already be registered.

This Job Description is not a complete statement of all duties and responsibilities comprising the position.

title: Restoration Technician/Labourer
description:

You'll assist with water extraction, demolition, and cleanup while learning to follow industry standards and safety protocols. Who We Are

At First Onsite, the work you do every day makes a real impact. You'll help communities rebuild and families recover after unexpected events. We offer competitive pay, comprehensive health and dental benefits, and RRSP matching because we believe in taking care of our people. You'll have opportunities to learn, grow, and build a lasting career across Canada in a culture that values care, collaboration, and doing the right thing. If you thrive in a team environment and want to make a meaningful difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Let's Rebuild Together

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges.                   • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

title: Field / Phone Enumerator Michigan

description:
The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture (NASDA) of Arlington, VA is looking to hire a detail-oriented part-time Field Enumerator to perform tasks that support our organization. Are you looking for a job with flexible hours? Would you like to work for an agriculture nonprofit that cares about its community and employees? If so, please read on!

This field enumerator position earns a competitive wage of $17.75/hour, plus mileage with opportunities for a promotion based on hours worked and performance ratings. We also offer exceptional perks, including a flexible schedule, the opportunity to work from home, the ability to work in your community, and knowledge about where your food comes from. If this sounds like the right opportunity in agriculture for you, apply today!

ABOUT NASDA

NASDA is a nonpartisan, nonprofit association that represents the elected and appointed commissioners, secretaries, and directors of the departments of agriculture in all fifty states and four U.S. territories. Founded in 1916, our mission is to grow and enhance American agriculture through policies, partnerships, and public engagement.

Since 1972, NASDA has employed enumerators to collect agricultural data on behalf of the United States Department of Agriculture's (USDA) National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS). In order to achieve our goals, we need employees who are as passionate about agriculture as we are and willing to put in the hard work. To find the right people, we strive to create a positive work environment that our employees can be proud of and want to build their careers with!

A DAY IN THE LIFE OF A FIELD ENUMERATOR

In this Field Enumerator position, you play a crucial role in serving our agricultural producers by providing reliable, accurate, and objective statistics and information that farmers, ranchers, and rural communities depend on. You actively interview farmers, ranchers, and other agricultural businesses either in person or on the phone. At times, you travel to designated fields in order to perform crop counts. After gathering all your information, you maintain and deliver detailed and legible records of the interviews, crop counts, mileage, expenditures, and your hours worked.

You conduct your enumerator work from a residence with an operable telephone free from any distractions. By maintaining a personal vehicle, you are always ready to travel in order to perform your field enumerator duties. The job brings something new every day, and you enjoy the flexibility and energetic nature of it!

QUALIFICATIONS FOR A FIELD ENUMERATOR

  • Experience multitasking in an energetic, deadline-oriented work environment
  • Ability to positively represent NASDA and the benefits of enumerators in all survey actions
  • Ability to make crop counts in designated fields
  • Ability to maintain a reliable personal vehicle
  • Ability to conduct interviews in person or by telephone with farm operators and other individuals
  • Knowledge about computers or iPads

Do you have excellent verbal and written communication skills? Are you able to demonstrate good time management in a fast-paced environment? Are you self-motivated? Do you enjoy working as part of a team? Are you organized? Can you maintain a positive and friendly attitude? If so, you might just be perfect for this field service position for our agriculture nonprofit!

WORK SCHEDULE

This part-time field service position works a flexible schedule that may include some evenings, weekends, and holidays. Weather, seasonal farm responsibilities, and community functions may affect work hours.

READY TO JOIN OUR TEAM?

We understand your time is valuable, so we have a very quick and easy application process. If you feel that you would be right for this Field Enumerator job, please fill out our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application. We look forward to meeting you!

title: Lead, Software Quality Assurance
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Lead, Software Quality Assurance based in the United States.

Join an innovative technology team developing AI-powered healthcare solutions that combine behavioral science, data science, and machine learning to improve patient engagement and health outcomes. As the Lead, Software Quality Assurance, you will define and drive quality engineering strategy across a cloud-native platform, user interfaces, APIs, and customer integrations. You will champion a shift-left approach, embedding automated testing, risk-based validation, and quality controls throughout the software development lifecycle. Working closely with engineering, product, cloud infrastructure, and customer operations teams, you will help ensure that releases are reliable, secure, scalable, and audit-ready in a regulated healthcare environment. You will also mentor QA engineers, establish shared testing standards, and continuously improve automation frameworks and delivery processes. This remote opportunity offers the chance to influence engineering excellence while helping deliver dependable technology that supports meaningful improvements in healthcare.

Accountabilities:

  • Lead quality assurance strategy: Define, implement, and maintain comprehensive testing strategies across platform services, APIs, web interfaces, event-driven workflows, and data pipelines.
  • Drive test automation: Build and evolve automated testing frameworks covering unit, integration, contract, regression, and end-to-end testing, complemented by risk-based manual testing where automation is not practical.
  • Establish quality gates: Define and maintain CI/CD quality controls, including coverage thresholds, contract test validation, critical-path end-to-end testing, and security scanning where applicable.
  • Embed quality early in development: Partner with engineers and product owners to review requirements, acceptance criteria, application logic, APIs, data models, event contracts, and user workflows to improve testability from the design stage.
  • Validate performance and reliability: Ensure appropriate testing of system performance, resilience, timeouts, retries, idempotency, failure scenarios, and other operational risks.
  • Strengthen event-driven testing practices: Establish standards for Kafka-based and similar messaging systems, including schema validation, backward compatibility, message replay, ordering assumptions, and failure handling.
  • Improve observability and release readiness: Collaborate with cloud and site reliability engineering teams to validate logging, metrics, tracing, operational dashboards, and production readiness before releases.
  • Maintain automation quality: Establish standards for reliable, maintainable automated tests, reduce flaky test behavior, assign clear ownership, and ensure timely remediation of broken tests.
  • Mentor and develop QA talent: Coach QA engineers, conduct code and test reviews, facilitate knowledge sharing, and develop playbooks, documentation, training, and cross-team testing practices.
  • Support product development: Collaborate with product owners and developers during backlog refinement, sprint planning, requirements clarification, and other Agile ceremonies to ensure features are testable and meet acceptance criteria.
  • Drive continuous improvement: Evaluate new testing tools and techniques, improve test data management, support local and ephemeral test environments, and identify opportunities to accelerate delivery without compromising quality.
  • Support production operations: Participate in release support, incident triage, defect investigation, and root cause analysis alongside engineering, cloud infrastructure, and customer operations teams.
  • Reduce recurring defects: Monitor escaped defect trends and implement corrective actions through improved tests, quality gates, and development processes.
  • Document and standardize processes: Maintain clear QA procedures, testing guidelines, and engineering quality standards that support consistency across teams and releases.

Requirements:

  • Professional experience: Five to seven or more years of relevant experience in software quality assurance, quality engineering, test automation, or a related technical discipline.
  • Education: A bachelor's degree in a related field is preferred.
  • API and service testing: Demonstrated experience automating tests for APIs and backend services, using tools such as JUnit, TestNG, or PyTest.
  • UI automation: Practical experience with browser and user interface automation tools such as Cypress, Playwright, or Jasmine, where applicable.
  • Performance testing: Familiarity with performance and load testing tools such as Gatling, k6, or JMeter.
  • Contract testing: Experience with contract testing frameworks such as Pact or equivalent tools.
  • CI/CD and version control: Strong understanding of continuous integration and delivery pipelines, quality gates, source control, and Git-based development workflows.
  • Observability: Familiarity with monitoring, logging, metrics, and distributed tracing concepts, including tools such as Datadog and OpenTelemetry.
  • Cloud and infrastructure: Experience working with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, with familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud-native application architectures.
  • Programming and scripting: Proficiency in one or more relevant programming or scripting languages, such as Java, TypeScript, Groovy, or Python.
  • Data and messaging technologies: Experience working with SQL databases and event-driven systems, particularly Kafka or comparable messaging technologies.
  • Agile methodologies: Familiarity with Agile development practices and frameworks, including Scrum, Extreme Programming (XP), or SAFe.
  • Leadership and mentoring: Demonstrated ability to guide QA engineers, share technical knowledge, establish best practices, and influence quality standards across multiple engineering teams.
  • Risk-based decision-making: Strong judgment in assessing testing priorities, evaluating release risks, and balancing quality, reliability, and delivery speed.
  • Process improvement: A proactive mindset and the ability to work through ambiguity, improve systems incrementally, and introduce practical solutions without waiting for perfect processes.
  • Communication and collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Organization and adaptability: Strong time management, prioritization, problem-solving, and organizational skills in a dynamic, cross-functional environment.
  • Work authorization: Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring employer-sponsored work authorization.
  • Onboarding requirement: Must be able to attend an initial one-week onsite onboarding period at an office in Tennessee. Travel expenses for this required visit are covered by the employer.

Benefits:

  • Competitive salary: Annual salary ranging from $130,000 to $150,000 USD.
  • Remote work flexibility: Work remotely within the United States, with a hybrid option available for employees located in Tennessee.
  • Healthcare coverage: Medical insurance with access to a Health Savings Account (HSA), plus dental and vision coverage.
  • Disability protection: Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance.
  • Life insurance: Company-paid life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment (AD&D) coverage.
  • Retirement savings: A 401(k) plan with employer matching.
  • Paid holidays: Ten paid holidays, along with quarterly company closure dates and an additional holiday-week company closure.
  • Flexible time off: A flexible paid time off policy to support personal needs and work-life balance.
  • Paid parental leave: Six weeks of paid parental leave to support employees and their growing families.
  • Travel-covered onboarding: Travel expenses covered for the required first week of onsite onboarding at a Tennessee office.
  • Meaningful impact: The opportunity to contribute to AI-powered healthcare solutions designed to improve preventive care, chronic disease management, patient engagement, and overall well-being.
  • Technical leadership opportunities: The ability to shape quality engineering practices, mentor team members, and influence reliability and testing standards across a cloud-native platform.
