title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in Germany.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                    • Additional qualifications considered an advantage

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Community credentials or roles such as CNCF Ambassador, AWS Community Builder, or Microsoft MVP.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

                      • Cloud certifications from providers such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.

                        • Benefits:

                        • Competitive fixed fee per course, agreed upfront based on course length and topic complexity, with higher compensation for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

                        • Paid freelance project that can be completed alongside an existing job, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement.

                        • A typical initial project duration of approximately three months, with a mutually agreed delivery plan.

                        • Potential to progress to a full-time role or take on additional course projects based on mutual fit.

                        • Fully remote working arrangements with flexible hours.

                        • Opportunity to collaborate with a global technical education team and reach a community of more than one million engineers.

                        • Dedicated production support for video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and course publishing, allowing you to focus on teaching and technical content.

                        • Opportunity to share your expertise in AI, DevOps, cloud, and Kubernetes through practical, hands-on education.

title: Back-End Software Engineer (Senior)
description:
Description

About Xe

Xe is a cross-border payments platform. We help SMEs and consumers in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand collect, convert, hold, and send money across markets. Each year, over 300 million people use Xe for currency information and over 350,000 use us to send money overseas.

Today, we're rebuilding the platform layer behind cross-border payments for corporate and consumer clients. We're small enough that your code ships fast and your decisions matter, and Euronet Worldwide (Nasdaq: EEFT) backs us so the problems stay real-scale.

About This Role

We're hiring a senior back-end engineer who owns real problems end-to-end and shapes how the team builds, from API design and data modeling through to service implementation, production reliability, and launch. You already use AI as part of how you think, build, test, and ship.

You'll write code that moves money in production, design and modernize the backend services the platform runs on, and lead delivery of new capability as Xe rebuilds its platform layer. You'll work in a small team with direct access to product, compliance, and operations, own architecture in your domain, lead design reviews, mentor mid-level engineers, and partner with architects and team leads on cross-domain decisions.

What You'll Do

  • Design and own backend services that move money and manage multi-currency balances across a range of domains, including onboarding, KYC and KYB, payment initiation, FX, settlement, and other supporting services.
  • Lead cross-functional delivery with product, compliance, and operations from problem framing through launch.
  • Lead the build of the partner integrations and settlement infrastructure your domain depends on.
  • Own production health for your domain, including reliability, observability, on-call, and incident response.
  • Lead design reviews, set technical direction for your domain, and mentor mid-level engineers.
  • Use agentic coding tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or equivalent) daily across the SDLC, and lead modernization from legacy services into the modern stack alongside architects and team leads in your domain.

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • 6 to 10+ years building production backend services, end-to-end.
  • Strong backend proficiency in C# / .NET preferred; other OOP languages welcome (Java, Kotlin, Go, or equivalent).
  • SQL and relational database fundamentals.
  • Writing and maintaining tests.
  • Daily use of agentic coding tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, or equivalent) across the SDLC.
  • Production experience with AWS, including hands-on deployment, CI/CD pipelines and modern deployment practices, and native services such as SQS, DynamoDB, S3, ECS, and Lambda.
  • Strong system design and architecture experience, including service-oriented or microservices and event-driven patterns.
  • Payments, FX, or regulated-industry experience.
  • Track record of technical leadership: mentoring engineers, leading design reviews, and making architecture decisions in your domain.
  • Strong written and verbal communication.

Nice-to-have

  • Experience with ledgers, double-entry accounting, or other financial-data systems.
  • Experience hiring, interviewing, or onboarding engineers.
  • Experience leading modernization or platform migrations.
  • Experience with caching solutions like Memcached or Redis.
  • Experience using project management and documentation tools like Jira and Confluence.
  • Knowledge of API testing tools such as Postman or Bruno.
  • Writing automated tests alongside development with AI tools (Claude Code or equivalent).

Perks & Benefits

  • Free Life Insurance
  • Supplemental Medical & Dental Insurance
  • Internal emergency loans
  • Birthday day off
  • Various discounts via Caja Los Andes
  • Euronet stock purchase (quarterly option)
  • Remittance service with no commission for immediate family
  • Annual salary reviews
  • Agreement with Smart Fit (Gym)

We want Xe to be a great place to work and to ensure that our communities are represented across our workforce. A vital part of this is ensuring we are a truly inclusive organization that encourages diversity in all respects.

All qualified applicants will be considered for employment regardless of age, national origin, race, color, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law. title: Data Engineer

Make an impact with NTT DATA. Join a company that is pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We are renowned for our technical excellence and leading innovations, and for making a difference to our clients and society. Our workplace embraces diversity and inclusion – it’s a place where you can grow, belong and thrive.

title: QA Engineer
description:
Looking for a job to get you out of bed?

We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our Quality Engineering team and own functional and end‑to‑end testing across our systems. We want someone genuinely passionate about testing - eager to hunt down the bug nobody else found, think outside the box, and take real ownership and accountability for the quality of what ships. You'll report directly to the QA Manager and help ensure consistent, reliable quality across our systems.

Casper (Casper.com) believes everyone should sleep better. That’s why we obsess over designing sleep products that actually make a difference—from the littlest dreamers and beyond. Including mattresses, pillows, and bedding, our entire collection is dreamed up and engineered in-house by our product and design teams. Sleepers can shop online, visit one of our 40+ retail locations across the United States, or find us through a growing network of trusted retail partners.

This is a hybrid role, requiring that you work 4 days per week from our Richmond, VA office.

When youʼre not catching zzzʼs, this is what youʼll do...

  • Design and execute functional and end‑to‑end test cases across web and back‑end systems, covering happy paths, edge cases, and negative scenarios
  • Own test planning for features and releases - clear, traceable test plans and test cases tied to requirements
  • Perform exploratory testing to surface issues that scripted cases miss
  • Validate complex, cross‑system workflows across multiple interconnected platforms
  • Test and validate workflows across SaaS applications commonly used in e‑commerce, Shopify, OMS, Salesforce, and ERP environments
  • Detect, isolate, reproduce, and document defects with clarity and insight
  • Contribute to our existing Playwright + TypeScript automation framework, starting with the most repetitive or highest‑risk manual cases
  • Write and maintain automated test scripts using Playwright and TypeScript, following our existing Page Object Model patterns
  • Get hands-on with our automation suite — running, debugging, and extending existing Playwright tests as you build up your automation skill set
  • Collaborate with Product, Engineering, and stakeholders to understand requirements and ensure proper test coverage
  • Write documentation for test cases and workflows to support long‑term scalability
  • Provide regular updates to the QA Manager on progress, risks, and opportunities for improvement

Our dream candidate is/has…

  • Strong in functional and end‑to‑end testing, with some hands‑on exposure to automation using Playwright and TypeScript
  • Experience testing an e‑commerce or SaaS product - you understand order lifecycles, payment or fulfillment flows, and how integrations between systems break in non‑obvious ways
  • Strong test case design and bug reporting skills - clear repro steps, good judgment on severity and priority
  • A creative problem‑solver who thinks outside the box - not satisfied testing only what's written in the ticket
  • Organized - able to juggle multiple test cycles and keep documentation current without letting anything slip
  • Passionate about testing - you find real satisfaction in catching the thing nobody else caught, and it shows
  • Comfortable with bug/task/test management tools such as JIRA and Coda
  • Comfortable working across multiple interconnected systems and validating end‑to‑end workflows
  • A clear communicator who collaborates closely with engineering, product, and DevOps

Nice to have…

  • Experience with API testing tools such as Postman
  • Exposure to CI/CD pipelines and how automated tests fit into them
  • Familiarity with AWS resources
  • Familiarity with AI‑driven workflows and tools like Copilot, Claude, Kiro, and Amazon Q Developer
  • B.S. in Computer Science or a related field

Targeted Annual Base Salary Range: $90,000-110,000 USD

Casper’s compensation philosophy ensures that the actual base salary is based on factors including but not limited to skills, education, experience, special training, time in position, and/or years of service.

We recognize that annual base salary is just one part of a total rewards package. In addition, we offer a comprehensive benefits package, wellbeing resources, and other perks including:

  • Medical, vision, and dental insurance to help you with those coughs or cavities (too many waffles)...
  • Paid Time Off. We believe in the power of rest so take the time you need to recharge.
  • Employee Discount to use on whatever you like (with a few exceptions) and product discounts for friends and family!
  • Dreaming of your next degree? After one year of service, we’ll help make that dream a little easier with tuition reimbursement.
  • … and more!

If you dream about this stuff this job is probably right for you. We look forward to learning more about you!

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for current or future employer-sponsored visa support.

As part of our hiring process, employment offers are contingent on the successful completion of a background check and drug screening, where permitted by law.

title: Forward Deployed Financial Engineer - Platform
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Forward Deployed Financial Engineer – Platform based in the United States.

Join a fast-growing financial technology environment transforming how finance teams operate through AI-powered automation, intelligent workflows, and seamless business system integrations. As a Forward Deployed Financial Engineer, you will work directly with customers to identify opportunities for AI-driven transformation and turn complex business challenges into practical, production-ready solutions. In the Platform focus, you will own the infrastructure, deployment, security, and operational reliability that enable these solutions to run effectively in customer environments. You will combine hands-on engineering with technical consulting, collaborating closely with customer IT and finance teams to deliver measurable business value. Working across engineering, product development, and customer success, you will help shape scalable platform capabilities and improve delivery efficiency. This fully remote opportunity is ideal for a customer-oriented engineer who enjoys solving ambiguous problems, taking end-to-end ownership, and building reliable systems that create lasting impact.

Accountabilities

  • Platform Deployment and Infrastructure: Own the deployment and operation of customer-facing solutions, including integrations, authentication, secrets management, cloud hosting, monitoring, and release processes. Ensure solutions are secure, reliable, maintainable, and suitable for production use.
  • Customer Discovery and Technical Consulting: Lead technical discovery sessions with customer IT and finance teams to understand existing systems, data, operational constraints, and business priorities. Translate findings into practical, deployable technical designs and recommendations.
  • End-to-End Solution Delivery: Take ownership of customer projects from initial discovery and solution recommendations through development, deployment, delivery, and handoff, ensuring the final solution addresses real business needs and is adopted successfully.
  • AI Solution Development: Build and deliver customer-facing solutions, including AI skills, routines, workflows, applications, and agents. Develop prototypes that address immediate requirements while identifying opportunities to create reusable capabilities.
  • Engineering Tooling and Standardization: Build internal tools, templates, infrastructure patterns, and reusable components that improve engineering productivity, accelerate implementation, and establish consistent quality standards across customer engagements.
  • Production Reliability and Operations: Implement appropriate monitoring, observability, release management, and operational practices to ensure deployed solutions remain functional and maintainable after delivery.
  • Customer Adoption and Change Management: Work directly with customer stakeholders to explain technical decisions, manage implementation changes, and support adoption. Help customer IT and finance teams integrate new solutions into their existing workflows.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Customer Success, Product, and R&D teams to troubleshoot technical challenges, communicate customer requirements, and contribute insights that inform product improvements.
  • Scalable Platform Innovation: Identify recurring customer challenges and translate them into opportunities for broader platform capabilities, reusable products, and improved implementation methodologies.
  • Documentation and Knowledge Sharing: Document technical architectures, implementation decisions, lessons learned, and repeatable approaches to strengthen team knowledge and improve future delivery.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Clearly explain technical concepts, infrastructure and security trade-offs, risks, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior finance leaders.

Requirements

  • Customer-Facing Technical Experience: Demonstrated ability to lead technical conversations with customers, facilitate discovery with IT and finance stakeholders, manage expectations, communicate trade-offs, and maintain confidence when project requirements change.
  • End-to-End Ownership: Proven ability to take a problem from initial discovery through implementation and production delivery, ensuring the resulting solution is practical, reliable, and actively used by customers.
  • DevOps and Infrastructure Expertise: Strong understanding of cloud deployment, APIs and integrations, CI/CD pipelines, authentication, secrets management, hosting, monitoring, and observability. Ability to move solutions from working prototypes into reliable production environments.
  • Software Engineering Skills: Production experience with Python or TypeScript, SQL, REST APIs, and at least one major cloud platform. Ability to build usable software and develop tools that help other engineers deliver more efficiently.
  • Business Systems Integration: Experience integrating applications with enterprise or business systems through APIs, including appropriate handling of authentication, credentials, and sensitive information.
  • Applied AI Knowledge: Familiarity with LLM-based systems, AI agents, and tool use, together with an understanding of the infrastructure, deployment, and operational requirements needed to support these technologies.
  • Technical Judgment and Problem-Solving: Ability to translate ambiguous business and technical requirements into clear, defensible recommendations and design solutions that balance customer needs, security, reliability, and maintainability.
  • Product-Oriented Mindset: Strong systems thinking and an interest in developing reusable solutions that can evolve beyond a single customer engagement.
  • Project Management and Independence: Ability to manage multiple responsibilities, work autonomously, adapt to changing priorities, and maintain ownership through implementation and handoff.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Strong communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively alongside Product, R&D, Customer Success, and other stakeholders.
  • Adaptability and Continuous Learning: Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to experiment, learn quickly, and solve unfamiliar problems creatively.
  • Preferred Experience: Experience in forward-deployed engineering, technical consulting, platform engineering, DevOps, or broad-scope engineering roles involving implementation and customer delivery.
  • Additional Advantage: Experience deploying LLM-based systems for real users, including production monitoring and evaluation, is beneficial. Familiarity with finance, accounting, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), Excel-based workflows, ERP systems, or other enterprise business applications is also an advantage, though direct finance industry experience is not required.

Benefits

  • Competitive Salary: Annual base salary ranging from $120,000 to $150,000 USD, depending on experience, skills, and location.
  • Meaningful Equity: Equity participation offering the opportunity to share in the company's long-term growth.
  • Remote Work: Fully remote employment anywhere in the United States, with flexibility to manage your schedule according to your local time zone.
  • Comprehensive Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with 100% of employee premiums covered and generous coverage for dependents.
  • Retirement Savings: 401(k) plan with an employer match of up to 4%.
  • Paid Time Off: Generous paid time off to support work-life balance.
  • Company Holidays: 12 paid company holidays annually.
  • Parental Leave: Paid leave to support employees and their families during important life transitions.
  • Life Insurance: Coverage to provide additional financial protection.
  • Collaborative Work Environment: Join an international, team-oriented organization that values innovation, ownership, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement.
  • Professional Growth: Opportunities to develop expertise across AI engineering, cloud infrastructure, enterprise integrations, and customer-facing technical delivery.

title: VP of Operations
description:
Your next role should come with a real seat at the table and a clear path to the top operating job. This one has both. As VP of Operations, you'll be the Founder/CEO's right hand and Embarc's future EOS Integrator.

You'll be joining a firm with real momentum. Revenue has nearly tripled in three years, Embarc Advisors® has made the Inc. 5000 three years running, and its hourly fee model is shaking up middle-market M&A. With three businesses to scale (M&A advisory, transaction diligence and strategic CFO advisory), your impact will show up in the numbers.

You're the kind of leader who remains steady when things are challenging and leads with a clear professional voice.

About Embarc Advisors

Embarc Advisors is disrupting the middle market M&A and CFO advisory industry. Built by a former Goldman Sachs banker and McKinsey consultant who identified a gap in this underserved market. We are one of the fastest-growing firms in our space, with revenue up nearly 3x over the past three years and multiple repeated rankings on the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. We are scaling fast, and we're doing it without sacrificing the culture that got us here.

We deliver best-in-class advisory work across M&A, transaction diligence, and strategic CFO services - partnering with lower-middle-market companies at every stage of their growth journey.

We operate as a team of elite athletes: trust-based, purpose-driven, and relentless about getting better; Kaizen isn't a poster on the wall here, it's how we operate. EOS gives us the structure and accountability to move fast without losing alignment, and it's exactly what lets us attract driven professionals and serious clients alike.

Embarc Intro Deck here:

Role Overview

Title: VP of Operations

Job Type: Full time

Position Location: Remote with a strong preference to be located near the San Francisco area and/or the ability to undertake frequent travel to the Bay Area.

Here's what you'll lead and how your first six months could unfold:

  • Month 1: Sit in on every leadership meeting, meet each practice lead, and learn the Scorecard, Rocks and open issues. By day 30, you run the weekly leadership meeting and own the operating rhythm. Learn how each business makes money. Go deep on M&A advisory, transaction diligence and strategic CFO advisory: pipeline, pricing, utilization and margin. Help lead your first quarterly planning session and you can explain how each business wins, with its numbers, and you've identified the biggest operational bottlenecks and a plan to fix them.
  • Months 2-3: Identify tasks the Operations team needs to do to ensure the client-facing staff members can reach their goals for the 1-year plan and 3-year picture. Build planning and capacity models and tighten the Scorecard so every leader owns measurable numbers. Build a work plan to achieve these goals. Present a data-backed answer to "How do we double revenue?" Step into growth. Turn the plan into Rocks, hiring plans and accountabilities.
  • Months 4+: Prove it in the results. Execute the plan, scale core systems (hiring, onboarding, HR, legal, IT, AI and automation), and report progress against targets every week.

This role isn't for you if:

  • You've mainly supported operations (project management, executive assistance, office management) rather than run them.
  • You'd rather work from reports than dig into the data yourself. Here decisions are made on facts, and every number has an owner.
  • You wait to be told where to look. Here we live by Extreme Ownership: you need to raise problems early and solve them.
  • You avoid conflict or hold on to a position after the data says otherwise. Here expect direct, high-intensity debate: hold your ground with data, change course when the facts warrant it, then commit.

What you need for this job:

  • You are currently in the right seat. You hold now, or held recently, a VP of Operations, Chief of Staff, General Manager or EOS Integrator role in which you reported directly to a founder/CEO and worked with the leadership team as a peer.
  • You've built and scaled growth. You've helped grow a professional services or multi-line firm of roughly 30 to 60+ people. You can point to the systems you put in place: meeting cadence, KPIs, and hiring and onboarding processes.
  • You have owned the numbers. You built and owned the forecast, budget or capacity model that leadership used to make decisions, and you're fluent in P&L, utilization and margin. Reporting someone else's numbers isn't enough.
  • You've successfully held leaders accountable. You've run the operating rhythm for a leadership team (weekly meetings, scorecards, quarterly priorities). You held senior people to their commitments without formal authority over them.
  • AI early adopter. You've put AI or automation into a real team workflow and can show the result, beyond using it for your own productivity.
  • An entrepreneurial track record. You've had at least one role in a founder-led or high-growth company. A corporate-only career won't be a fit.
  • You have a bachelor's degree, and the ability to travel for quarterly offsites plus about six trips a year with the CEO.

Preferred: Hands-on EOS experience; a background in M&A, investment banking, corporate development, strategic finance or consulting; experience leading marketing or business development; tools you've built with low-code or AI; a Bay Area base; a master's in finance, economics, math, business or social science.

Embarc and EOS:

Embarc operates according to the EOS® (Entrepreneurial Operating System) platform. We use a proven set of tools and processes to create clarity, accountability, and traction across our entire organization. EOS helps us align around a shared vision, track measurable progress, solve issues quickly, and ensure that the right people are in the right seats. Our team meets regularly using structured meeting cadences and operates with a strong emphasis on transparency, ownership, and results. To learn more about EOS®, click here.

Why Join The Embarc Team?

Diverse experience is a hallmark of the Embarc experience: we work across a broad range of project types, including M&A, transaction diligence, and strategic CFO advisory.

We offer:

  • A dynamic environment of a fast-growing startup, allowing you to make a significant impact across all aspects of our organization
  • High-octane experience of an advisory firm
  • Opportunity to work with highly skilled individuals from diverse backgrounds
  • Exposure to startup environments, at the senior management level, without the inherent risk of "putting all of your chips" on a single startup
  • A tight-knit culture, focused on fostering psychological safety and taking 100% responsibility
  • The opportunity to share on the upside
  • 100% remote work

Our benefits include:

  • Competitive compensation, plus a semi-annual performance bonus
  • 401(k) with a 3% employer contribution after one year
  • Full medical, dental, and vision benefits
  • Unlimited vacation time
  • Paid sick leave
  • Short-term disability insurance
  • Three team offsites per year, for connecting, recharging, and growing together

title: Software Engineer (Level I, II, or III)
description:
Space Tango is an innovative space technology company based in Lexington, Kentucky. We develop automated facilities and payloads that enable research, development, and manufacturing in microgravity. Our mission is to manufacture health and technology products in space that create value and transformational solutions for our partners, customers, and humanity.


We are looking for a software engineer to join the team that develops and maintains the software behind our automated payloads, facilities, and mission operations. Working alongside electrical, mechanical, science, and mission operations teammates, our software team builds full-stack applications, backend services, user interfaces, automation tools, and mission software that enable autonomous operations in microgravity.

We welcome candidates of all levels of experience. The position's scope of responsibility will be based on relevant experience and technical capabilities.


This position is based at Space Tango’s headquarters in Lexington, Kentucky. Travel may be required to support launches, customer activities, partner integrations, and mission operations.


Candidates should be comfortable supporting occasional evenings, weekends, holidays, and other non-standard hours when required for launch campaigns, testing, or on-orbit operations.


What You’ll Do

  • Design, develop, integrate, test, and maintain software supporting Space Tango payloads, facilities, and mission operations.
  • Build backend services, APIs, databases, automation tools, and user interfaces using Python and related technologies.
  • Contribute to reliable, maintainable, and reusable software architectures across projects.
  • Develop new capabilities while maintaining and improving software supporting active spaceflight missions.
  • Collaborate across disciplines to translate engineering and scientific objectives into practical software solutions.
  • Develop software that interfaces with hardware, robotics, laboratory automation, scientific instruments, and payload control systems.
  • Support integration, verification, debugging, and troubleshooting throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Create and maintain technical documentation, participate in code and design reviews, and follow Space Tango’s development processes and quality standards.
  • Evaluate and apply appropriate software tools, automation, and AI-assisted development practices to improve productivity and software quality.
  • At more experienced levels, lead technical efforts, mentor engineers, and contribute to software strategy and development standards.

Join a specialized rail and transit consulting environment dedicated to improving the safety, reliability, and performance of rail transportation systems across North America.
As a Lead Subject Matter Expert in Quality Assurance and Control, you will provide technical leadership across rolling stock engineering projects, including new vehicle procurement, fleet modernization, rebuilds, and fleet management initiatives.
You will oversee manufacturing quality, conduct inspections and audits, and ensure that rail vehicles meet applicable technical specifications, industry standards, and client expectations.
Working alongside engineers, management consultants, clients, and subcontractors, you will help deliver complex projects with a strong focus on safety, quality, and operational excellence.
You will also contribute to design reviews, first article inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives throughout the vehicle lifecycle.
This role combines hands-on technical expertise with team leadership, stakeholder engagement, and independent project delivery.
It offers an opportunity to influence the quality and long-term performance of passenger rail and transit fleets while supporting the future of sustainable mobility.

Accountabilities:

  • Lead and support rolling stock engineering projects from concept through completion, including new vehicle procurement, existing vehicle modifications, rebuilds, and fleet management activities.
  • Oversee quality assurance and quality control activities across different rail vehicle types, including locomotives, multiple units, and passenger rail cars.
  • Conduct first article inspections and assess manufacturing quality before and after vehicle delivery to verify compliance with technical specifications and contractual requirements.
  • Perform on-site manufacturing inspections, including welding inspections where applicable, to identify defects, verify workmanship, and ensure adherence to quality standards.

Requirements:

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in engineering or a related technical field, with relevant experience in rolling stock engineering and quality assurance and control.
  • Rail industry experience: Demonstrated experience supporting rail vehicle or transit procurement projects, particularly in manufacturing quality, inspections, quality control, and compliance verification.

  • Regulatory knowledge: Experience working with rail regulatory authorities, including the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) and Federal Transit Administration (FTA), in relation to rail vehicles.
  • Fleet performance experience: Familiarity with fleet management, vehicle delivery performance, manufacturing quality oversight, and post-delivery inspections is preferred.
  • Technical inspection capabilities: Ability to assess rail vehicle construction, evaluate manufacturing quality, participate in design reviews, and verify compliance with technical standards and specifications.
  • Leadership and supervision: Experience coordinating or supervising inspectors, subcontractors, and multidisciplinary project teams, including during audits and on-site inspections.
  • Communication skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare accurate technical reports and communicate effectively with clients, manufacturers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Project management: Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, meet deadlines, and deliver high-quality work within defined project scopes and budgets.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills: Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify quality issues, assess risks, recommend corrective measures, and support continuous improvement.
  • Working arrangements and travel: Comfortable working remotely from a home office or an appropriate indoor office environment, with travel required for project implementation, manufacturing inspections, audits, and site visits.
  • Physical requirements: Ability, with or without reasonable accommodation, to work at a computer for periods of up to four hours, participate in telephone conversations for up to three hours daily, sit through meetings for up to three hours without breaks, and walk or stand for up to four hours during site visits. Job Summary:

As an Early Diversion Outreach Specialist, you'll provide short-term outreach, engagement, and care coordination for adults living with mental illness and co-occurring substance use disorders who may be at risk of criminal justice involvement. This role exists to help people connect to the right behavioral health supports earlier-before crises escalate.

Key responsibilities include building rapport in the community; coordinating with behavioral health providers, healthcare organizations, emergency responders, law enforcement, and other partners; offering behavioral health education; completing screenings; providing motivational support; and linking individuals to appropriate treatment and community resources. You'll also support community education and training efforts that strengthen awareness and referral pathways.

Job Duties:

1. Conduct community outreach and engagement activities to identify adults with mental illness and co-occurring

substance use disorders who are at risk of criminal justice involvement.

2. Build collaborative relationships with law enforcement, EMS, fire departments, hospitals, behavioral health

providers, courts, and other community partners to promote early diversion and improve referral pathways.

3. Screen individuals for behavioral health needs and assist with early identification of mental health and

substance use concerns.

4. Provide brief engagement, motivational support, and crisis stabilization services to encourage participation in

treatment and recovery.

5. Coordinate care by connecting individuals with appropriate behavioral health, substance use treatment,

healthcare, housing, employment, and other community support services based on individual needs.

6. Maintain ongoing follow-up and navigation services until individuals are successfully linked to long-term

treatment and recovery supports, with services generally lasting no more than three months.

7. Educate individuals, families, and community partners regarding available behavioral health services, evidence-

based treatment options, and recovery resources.

8. Assist with the development, coordination, and delivery of community education and training on behavioral

health, substance use disorders, suicide prevention, trauma-informed care, crisis intervention, and early

diversion practices.

9. Participate in community system mapping, coalition meetings, and collaborative planning efforts to strengthen

local early diversion initiatives.

10. When available and appropriate, Early Diversion Outreach Specialists will respond alongside law enforcement

officers and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) personnel during behavioral health-related calls for service.

11. Maintain timely, accurate, and confidential documentation of outreach activities, referrals, service

coordination, and client progress in accordance with agency policies and grant requirements.

12. Document in the electronic health record and other systems as required by programming.

13. Collect and report required program data and outcome measures to support grant compliance and program

evaluation.

14. Participate in required supervision, staff meetings, professional development, and ongoing training.

15. Perform other duties as assigned to support the goals of the Early Diversion Program and Community Counseling Center.

title: Quality Control Coordinator
description:
SUMMARY

Perform material handling, data and documentation activities that prepare product for inspection and disposition.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (include the following, however, other duties may apply.)

  • Coordinate with WH/receiving and shop for timely delivery of parts to the Inspection Area. Maintain an organized queue of jobs awaiting inspection according to priorities set by the QA Lead.
  • Stage pallets, crates and parts for inspection so QA Inspectors can begin work without delay. Move product between receiving, inspection, hold/MRB and shipping areas using a fork truck, pallet jack or by hand.
  • Unpackage, uncrate and repackage parts, protecting product from damage and keeping tags, labels and paperwork with the correct parts.
  • Verify part numbers, revisions, heat/lot numbers and quantities against purchase orders, packing lists and shipping documentation. Report count discrepancies, missing paperwork or shipping damage to the QA Lead.
  • Prepare inspection packets for QA Inspectors, including drawings, specifications, engineering change notices, material test reports, customer requirements and prior inspection records.
  • Create dimensional inspection reports, including ballooned drawings and report forms, for use by QA Inspectors. Enter recorded inspection data into reports and the ERP system.
  • Take, label and file photographs of parts, packaging, labels, nonconformances and shipping damage.
  • Initiate Discrepant Material Reports (DMRs) in the non-conformance reporting system based on inspection findings. Tag and segregate nonconforming material in designated hold areas.
  • Track the status of open DMRs, Corrective Action Reports (CARs) and RMAs, and follow up with responsible parties as directed.
  • Compile, scan, file and retain quality records, such as certifications, material test reports, inspection reports and Certificates of Conformance, according to document control procedures.

title: Project Manager / Environmental Engineer
description:
Matrix New World Engineering, a part of True Environmental and its partner firms, have united their strengths to establish the nation's premier environmental and engineering services consulting firm. This powerhouse organization offers an extensive range of services aimed at revolutionizing the built environment and preserving the natural one. Its diverse expertise encompasses environmental remediation, urban planning, engineering iconic coastal and marine structures, developing sustainable energy sources, and pioneering resource extraction methods. Explore further at and to discover the full scope of our capabilities.

We are seeking an experienced Project Manager / Environmental Engineer to play a pivotal role in our growing environmental consulting practice in NYC. We are prioritizing candidates with a Professional Engineer (PE) license who bring deep technical authority, client-facing leadership, and a proven track record of managing complex environmental consulting and engineering projects.

In this role, you will take ownership of high-profile projects in the NYC metropolitan area, direct field and office engineering efforts (including Phase I/II Site Assessments, remediation designs, and Remedial Action Workplans), provide oversight of quality control and quality assurance reviews of environmental and hazardous materials deliverables, and mentor junior-to-mid-level engineering and scientific staff. This position offers significant autonomy, path-to-leadership advancement, and direct involvement in key client and regulatory relationships.

  • Salary Range: Starts at $90,000+ (commensurate with experience and PE licensure, if applicable)
  • Benefits & Culture: True Environmental offers comprehensive benefits focused on holistic employee well-being, including health insurance, 401(k) with company match, and generous PTO. They prioritize work-life balance through flexible options and foster professional growth via tuition reimbursement and continuous learning in a supportive culture.

What You'll Do

  • Lead and manage end-to-end site investigation and remediation projects—from initial scoping and proposal preparation to workplan design, engineering controls, field oversight, and final regulatory approval.
  • Direct site characterizations and environmental investigations to determine the nature and extent of contamination across soil, soil vapor, sediment, groundwater, and air for public, private, commercial, industrial, and infrastructure clients.
  • Oversee the preparation of Phase I ESAs (ASTM E1527), Phase II Investigations, Remedial Action Workplans (RAWPs), and complex engineering reports; perform critical peer reviews and engineering sign-offs.
  • Direct field programs and oversee specialty subcontractors (drillers, remediation contractors) during soil boring advancement, monitoring well installation, excavation, and remedial system construction.
  • Manage, mentor, and train junior-to-mid-level engineers and scientists; ensure deliverables meet high technical standards while maintaining project budgets, timelines, and profitability.
  • Serve as the primary technical point of contact in project meetings with clients, municipal stakeholders, and regulatory agencies (NYSDEC, NYCDEP, OER).

Minimum Requirements

  • BS or MS in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering with an environmental concentration, Geology, or a closely related discipline.
  • 8-10+ years of progressive environmental engineering and consulting experience, with demonstrated project management and team leadership skills.
  • Hands-on experience executing Phase I ESAs and Phase II Site Investigations, including soil, sediment, soil vapor, air, and groundwater sampling.
  • Working knowledge of NYSDEC/NYSDOH Rules, Regulations, and Guidance documents (DER-10, Part 360, Part 375, Vapor Intrusion Technical Guidance) and Chapter 12 (Hazardous Materials) of the New York City Environmental Quality Review Technical Manual.
  • OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER certification with current 8-hour refresher.
  • Valid driver’s license with a clean record and willingness to conduct field oversight across the five boroughs of NYC, Westchester, and Long Island.
  • Exceptional technical writing, analytical, quantitative problem-solving, and project financial management skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, Outlook).
  • Ability to wear a respirator, pass a pre-employment drug screening, and comply with DOT-regulated random drug testing programs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Professional Engineer (PE) license (NYS PE registration or ability to obtain via reciprocity is a major asset).
  • Advanced experience designing and executing complex remedial solutions and engineered controls across various environmental media.
  • Working knowledge of environmental investigation implications with the CEQR process (Chapter 12) and NYC Brownfield Cleanup Program (BCP) / OER projects.
  • OSHA 10-Hour or 30-Hour Construction Safety certification.
  • GIS (Geographic Information Systems) competency.
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

title: E-Commerce Photographer
description:
ABOUT THE LUCAS MUSEUM OF NARRATIVE ART
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is dedicated to illustrated storytelling. Founded by George Lucas and Mellody Hobson, the museum’s collection features works by artists including Norman Rockwell, Kadir Nelson, Jessie Willcox Smith, N. C. Wyeth, Beatrix Potter, Judith F. Baca, Frida Kahlo, and Maxfield Parrish; as well as comic art legends such as Winsor McCay, Jack Kirby, Frank Frazetta, Alison Bechdel, Chris Ware, and R. Crumb; and photographers Gordon Parks, Henri Cartier-Bresson, and Dorothea Lange. The Museum also houses the Lucas Archives, containing models, props, concept art, and costumes from Lucas’s filmmaking career.
Designed by Ma Yansong of MAD with a landscape by Mia Lehrer of Studio-MLA, the Museum is in Exposition Park, Los Angeles, on an 11-acre campus that includes new green space and a 300,000-square-foot building with galleries, two theaters, a library, restaurant, café, retail store, and community spaces.

POSITION SUMMARY

The E-Commerce Photographer is responsible for creating high-quality, accurate, and visually compelling product photography for use across the museum’s e-commerce and digital platforms. This role supports the presentation of retail merchandise by producing consistent imagery that reflects established brand and visual standards

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Photograph retail merchandise for e-commerce, digital marketing, and other online platforms.

  • Set up and operate cameras, lighting, backdrops, and other studio equipment to produce consistent, high-quality product images.

  • Capture multiple product views, including front, back, side, detail, packaging, and other required angles.

  • Style and position merchandise to accurately represent product features, scale, color, texture, and details.

  • Maintain consistency in lighting, composition, cropping, backgrounds, and overall image quality across product categories.

  • Perform basic post-production, including color correction, cropping, exposure adjustments, resizing, and minor image cleanup.

  • Prepare, name, organize, and deliver digital image files according to established e-commerce specifications and workflows.

  • Partner with E-Commerce and Retail Merchandising team to prioritize products based on launch dates, inventory availability, campaigns, and business needs.

  • Maintain photography equipment and keep the studio and workspace organized, clean, and ready for production.

  • Track photographed products and completed assets to support an efficient product-to-site workflow.

  • Ensure product photography accurately represents merchandise and meets established brand standards.

  • Assist with lifestyle, promotional, or other photography projects as needed.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Analytical Rigor: Simplifies complex problems by using critical thinking to evaluate problems, gathering information, incorporating multiple perspectives, understanding causes, and identifying best-possible solutions. Invests time in planning, discovery, and reflection to drive better decisions and more efficient implementations. Adopts an audience-centric approach, understanding the needs of the audience and incorporating them, as appropriate, into the decision.

Courageous Communication: Intentionally works well with others both on the team and cross-functionally to achieve individual, team, department, or organizational goals. Values diverse input and working with others as a way to achieve the best output possible.

Collaborative Excellence: Displays courage when handling difficult conversations and genuinely and intentionally communicates. Relays key messages effectively, targeted to specific audiences. Identifies others' communication styles and perspectives, adjusting language and approach accordingly. Employs active listening to understand, rather than reply. Asks for, integrates, and values feedback from team, peers, and leaders.

Adaptive Resilience: Thrives and grows in a rapidly changing and complex environment. Displays flexibility, activates networks, and adopts a continuous growth mindset to learn from mistakes and bounce back from adversity.

Inclusive Interaction: Actively contributes to an environment in which all employees feel a sense of belonging, valued for their differences and empowered to participate and contribute freely.

Building Trust & Relationship Management

  • Accountable Ownership and clearly shares information and the "why" behind decisions.

  • Asks for and values the opinions of others. Displays empathy when listening.

  • Acknowledges when trust has been broken and focuses on rebuilding.

  • Relates comfortably with people across levels, functions, cultures, and geographies. Identifies interpersonal and group dynamics and reacts effectively.

Accountable Ownership

  • Takes ownership of outcomes, positive or negative, without blaming others within the team or cross-functionally.

  • Recognizes when they are not approaching a situation with accountability but instead with a blame mindset.

  • Takes accountability for assigned tasks and executes on deliverables in a timely manner.

Strategic Alignment & Execution

  • Contributes to the organization by understanding and aligning actions with the organization's goals, core functions, needs, and values.

  • Seeks out and incorporates multiple perspectives, experiences, and industry trends to develop a holistic perspective. Operationalizes ideas within the business model.

  • Displays critical thinking when faced with a challenge by asking probing questions and looking for connections.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

The physical demands described below are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, up to 8 hours per shift.

  • Ability to move throughout multiple Museum locations, including galleries, theaters, outdoor spaces, and other public areas.

  • Ability to maintain an active and visible presence while providing exceptional guest service.

  • Ability to work in a high-volume, public-facing environment with large groups of guests, including school groups, tours, special events, and peak attendance periods, while maintaining professionalism, situational awareness, and composure.

  • Ability to frequently bend, reach, stoop, kneel, crouch, and climb stairs as needed.

  • Ability to occasionally lift, carry, push, and pull items weighing up to 25 pounds, including wheelchairs, stanchions, signage, guest service equipment, and other operational materials.

  • Ability to communicate clearly and effectively with guests and colleagues in person, by telephone, and over two-way radio.

  • Ability to work both indoors and outdoors in varying environmental conditions.

  • Ability to maintain awareness of guest activity and surrounding conditions while monitoring galleries, queues, and public spaces.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 1–3 years of professional photography experience, preferably in e-commerce, retail, product, commercial, or studio photography.

  • Digital portfolio demonstrating strong product photography and post-production skills.

  • Proficiency with DSLR or mirrorless camera systems, professional studio equipment, and strobe lighting.

  • Proficiency with Adobe Photoshop, Lightroom, Capture One, or comparable photography software.

  • Experience with post-production, including color correction, cropping, image optimization, resolution, and file preparation.

  • Experience managing high-volume photography workflows and large product catalogs.

  • Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain consistent visual and brand standards across product imagery.

  • Strong organizational, file-management, and time-management skills with the ability to meet production deadlines.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with creative, retail, merchandising, and e-commerce teams.

  • Experience photographing retail merchandise in an e-commerce environment preferred.

  • Must provide and use personal camera equipment.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY AND OUR COMMITMENT TO DEAIB
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art embraces diversity and equal opportunity. We are committed to building a team that represents and supports a variety of backgrounds and perspectives. The Lucas Museum fosters a work environment that is free of discrimination and harassment, whether based on race, national origin, gender, gender expression, religion, ethnic background, age, disability, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other criterion prohibited by applicable federal, state, or local laws. We believe that diversity and inclusion among our team is critical to our success, and we seek to recruit, develop, and retain the best qualified people from a diverse candidate pool. Applications from traditionally underrepresented communities are encouraged.
The statements in this description represent typical elements, criteria, and general work performed. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required for the job.
***************************************************************************************************************
MISSION AND VISION
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is dedicated to the art of illustrated stories. Our mission is to inspire and connect people through the exploration of visual stories and their influences in society.
VALUES
Our internal and external practices are shaped by the following beliefs and behaviors.
People First: We meet people wherever they are (physically, intellectually, emotionally). Our inclusive practice connects who people are and what they find emotional in works of art.
Inspired: We believe that art can move you to feel, think, reflect, and act.
Collaborative: We believe that nimble thinking and working together yield exponential results.
STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
Narrative Art:
Amplify the social impact of storytelling and illustration.
Community:
Connect to a broad and diverse public.
Operational Excellence:
Create a healthy and durable institution.
All staff at the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art lead through a deep commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, both within the Museum and with the communities that we serve.
Salary and titles will be assigned commensurate to the successful candidates’ education and experience. An attractive compensation package will be offered to the successful candidate(s).

title: Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — AI / DevOps based in Colombia.

As a Senior Technical Trainer, you will combine hands-on DevOps expertise with a passion for teaching to develop practical, engaging courses on AI-powered engineering workflows. You will help engineers understand how to apply AI agents, coding assistants, and modern AI tools to real-world infrastructure and automation challenges. Working alongside a curriculum team and experienced technical educators, you will design lessons, develop hands-on lab specifications, and record clear, compelling instructional videos. This remote freelance opportunity begins with a paid course project, typically lasting around three months, with the potential for ongoing projects or a full-time position. You will have the flexibility to work alongside existing commitments while contributing your technical knowledge to a global engineering community. The ideal candidate is a practising DevOps engineer who can simplify complex concepts, communicate confidently on camera, and create learning experiences that make advanced technologies accessible.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop technical courses

    • Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, learning objectives, lesson sequences, and practical lab exercises focused on AI for DevOps.

    • Develop content that demonstrates how engineers use AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation in real infrastructure environments.

    • Ensure lessons are technically accurate, relevant, practical, and aligned with the needs of working engineers.

    • Create engaging instructional content

      • Write concise, story-driven video scripts designed to explain technical concepts clearly, with individual lessons typically lasting around six minutes.

      • Use AI tools where helpful during drafting while ensuring the final scripts reflect your own voice, expertise, and teaching style.

      • Narrate and present lessons confidently in English, making complex technical topics approachable for learners at different experience levels.

      • Develop and validate hands-on labs

        • Write detailed specifications for practical labs that demonstrate real-world DevOps and AI workflows.

        • Collaborate with the dedicated labs team responsible for building the lab environments.

        • Test completed labs, validate technical accuracy, and ensure exercises deliver the intended learning outcomes.

        • Record demonstrations and walkthroughs explaining how to complete lab exercises and solve practical challenges.

        • Collaborate on quality and editorial development

          • Work closely with curriculum and production teams throughout the course development process.

          • Incorporate structured editorial feedback, particularly during the initial course section, to align content with established teaching standards.

          • Participate in regular team syncs and maintain communication through collaboration tools such as Slack.

          • Focus on technical expertise, teaching, scripting, and recording while the production team manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

            • Requirements:

            • Hands-on DevOps and infrastructure experience

              • Strong practical knowledge of Linux, containers, Kubernetes, at least one major cloud platform, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code (IaC).

              • Experience building, operating, and maintaining infrastructure rather than relying solely on theoretical knowledge.

              • The ability to demonstrate real engineering workflows and translate practical experience into effective learning materials.

              • Current experience with AI technologies

                • Practical experience using AI tools in engineering work, including AI agents, coding assistants, and LLM-based automation.

                • Genuine curiosity about emerging AI capabilities and a commitment to staying current with new tools and techniques.

                • The ability to explain how AI can support infrastructure engineering and DevOps workflows; deep specialization in AI research is not required.

                • Teaching and communication skills

                  • A demonstrated passion for teaching, supported by experience creating courses, publishing tutorials, delivering talks or workshops, mentoring colleagues, or sharing technical knowledge with a community.

                  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly, naturally, and confidently on camera.

                  • Strong storytelling skills and the ability to break down complex technical concepts into simple, structured explanations.

                  • Empathy for learners, particularly beginners, and an understanding of how to make technical material engaging and accessible.

                  • Collaboration and adaptability

                    • Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology and incorporate constructive editorial feedback.

                    • Ability to work independently, organize deliverables, and meet an agreed project schedule.

                    • Comfort working remotely with a distributed team, including participation in weekly syncs and some time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

                    • Additional qualifications considered an advantage

                      • Previously published online courses on platforms such as Udemy or Pluralsight, or experience authoring a technical book.

                      • Experience speaking at conferences or meetups, maintaining a technical YouTube channel or blog, or contributing to technical communities.

                      • Community credentials or roles such as CNCF Ambassador, AWS Community Builder, or Microsoft MVP.

                      • Relevant Kubernetes certifications, including CKA, CKAD, or CKS, or recognition such as Kubestronaut.

                      • Cloud certifications from providers such as AWS or Microsoft Azure.

                        • Benefits:

                        • Competitive fixed fee per course, agreed upfront based on course length and topic complexity, with higher compensation for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

                        • Paid freelance project that can be completed alongside an existing job, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement.

                        • A typical initial project duration of approximately three months, with a mutually agreed delivery plan.

                        • Potential to progress to a full-time role or take on additional course projects based on mutual fit.

title: Engineer III - Electrical Power System Protection and Control (Remote)
description:
JOB SUMMARY

The Engineer III will provide engineering services and support to an assigned group. The position will demonstrate proficiency in technical expertise in a designated work group area while developing skills and familiarity in related technical areas. The role will be responsible for a range of assignments and workmanship will be subject to limited checks and verification by expert team members.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES, FUNCTIONS, AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop reports and work plans and recommend action based on short/long-range objectives and economic/budget considerations.
  • Develop and coordinate individual project work plans and manage through completion, redirecting when necessary.
  • Complete status reports for all work assignments and communicate progress to management.
  • Communicate major developments or changes in project direction to supervisors.
  • Function as a technical representative in customer, vendor, and contractor meetings.
  • Complete increasingly complex assignments on a routine basis.
  • Provide work directions to other staff/contractors on projects as assigned.
  • Manage multiple assignments while training and developing less experienced engineers and other staff.
  • Complete preparation of estimates (cost, work order, schedules).
  • Analyze data and make recommendations and/or decisions.
  • Maintain technical records (e.g. drawings, files, databases).
  • Collaborate with other team members and supervisors in carrying out assignments.
  • Provide engineering assistance for customers and internal staff.
  • Contribute to the creation of corporate standards and specifications related to respective expertise.
  • Remain current in the industry by pursuing ongoing technical expertise and awareness of job-related field.
  • Demonstrate working knowledge of sound engineering practices and standards.
  • Perform analysis of system disturbances to determine proper operation of the protection scheme and assist in investigation of root cause.
  • Investigate all technical aspects of protective relaying and controls to apply new ideas or technology that would improve procedures and overall results.
  • Provide protective relay scheme insight to help establish the arrangement and location of substation facilities.
  • Develops and works with digital computer programs as needed including power quality, fault, and system coordination studies, loss evaluations, relay software, relay event analysis, protection asset databases, and arc flash.
  • Develop detailed drawings for relaying single lines, secondary protective relay schemes and schematics, low voltage equipment power, and control system connections for generation, transmission, and distribution protection.
  • Design and manage the installation of generation, transmission, distribution and industrial facility replacements and upgrades.
  • Develop cabling requirements for relay cabinets, equipment, and relay panels.
  • Prepare building layout drawings for control houses and battery buildings.
  • Create customer system protection equipment bidding documents for industrial, distribution, and transmission substations.
  • Develop protective relay settings as required for new facility (generation, transmission, distribution and industrial) equipment protection and modify existing facility protective relay settings to maintain optimum system protection.
  • Perform SME tasks on assigned NERC and/or CIP Compliance standards.
  • Prepare construction, equipment, material specifications, and work scope.
  • Evaluate customer bids and recommend suppliers/contractors for system protection.
  • Maintain and coordinate contracts with equipment suppliers and monitor progress, expediting as required to meet schedules.
  • Coordinate and oversee substation and industrial control system field testing and modification, phasing tests, and other commissioning and check-out activities for all generation, transmission, distribution and industrial protection schemes, with contractors and other Telex departments, at the customer substation and industrial sites.
  • Develop protection system switching procedures.
  • Coordinate contractors or staff on project related work, certification of completed work, and recommendation of final acceptance of the project.
  • Monitor the project during construction start-up and recommend modifications necessary to support project success.
  • Perform project management duties for small and larger projects simultaneously and assist other engineers with their projects.
  • Gains understanding of commercial and contractual aspects of company business.
  • Exhibit exemplary attendance and punctuality.
  • Comply with company policies and procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
  • Perform all work in a safe and timely manner.

Based on the essential duties listed above, this position is considered safety-sensitive and therefore all work must be performed following quality standards and established safety procedures.

EDUCATION & RELATED EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering from an ABET accredited school is required.
  • A minimum of four (4) years of engineering work experience is required.
  • Experience developing computer programs or scripts is required.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, CADD, and other common business applications is required.
  • A valid driver's license and a good driving record are required.
  • A specific engineering discipline may be preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Awareness of all relevant procedures, specifications, and applicable codes, regulations, compliance rules, and standards (e.g. IEEE, NERC, etc.).
  • General understanding of how decision making and work product impacts other systems, operations, and processes.
  • Seasoned engineering knowledge and sound judgement of engineering practices and standards.
  • Proficient knowledge and judgement in the area of protection and control in generation, transmission, distribution and industrial environments.
  • Strong understanding of business acumen, company financial structure, and business plans.
  • Basic understanding of negotiation and conflict resolution processes.
  • A logical thinker who can understand instructions on specific objectives, complex features, and possible solutions and formulate high-quality engineering workmanship.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including, but not limited to communicating technical information to a wide range of audiences and produce reports, emails, and presentations.
  • Good interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate with internal and external company contacts.
  • Analytical skills, including interpretive and complex problem-solving and decision-making skills pertaining to electric power systems, engineering, economics, and/or financial analysis.
  • Exceptional project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Ability to lead and provide work direction to others.
  • Proven ability to creatively apply technical skills to projects and activities.
  • Ability to plan, schedule, conduct, and coordinate detailed phases of engineering.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and prepare system and equipment manuals, schematic diagrams, and engineering drawings.
  • Must be capable and willing to learn on-the-job and advance to the next level of engineering responsibility.
  • An individual capable of working in both a team environment and independently with minimal oversight.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES AND INTERACTIONS WITH OTHERS

The Engineer III role may direct assigned personnel and contractors. The role will interact with coworkers, management, customers, vendors, and service providers daily.

KEY COMPETENCIES

  • Technical/Professional Knowledge and Skills
  • Contributing to Team Success
  • Decision Making
  • Customer Focus
  • Adaptability

WORKING CONDITIONS

This is primarily a remote work position with occasional travel, overnight included, to customer locations. Customer sites are typically indoor and outdoor construction environments. The indoor work environment is usually well-lit, environmentally controlled with a moderate level of noise. The outdoor environment may require the employee to be exposed to temperatures above 100 degrees Fahrenheit and below 32 degrees Fahrenheit. This position may also be exposed to danger, vibrations, rough/uneven terrain, dirt/shavings, fumes, grease/oil, excessive noise, electricity, flying objects, fire/steam/hot surfaces, and moving equipment. This position regularly lifts up to twenty (20) pounds; and occasionally lifts up to fifty (50) pounds. This position is full-time and work hours, including evening, weekend, and overnight work may vary depending on the operational activities and required duties of the role.

  • Any four-year combination of higher education and qualifying experience, or

Job Summary:

As an Early Diversion Outreach Specialist, you'll provide short-term outreach, engagement, and care coordination for adults living with mental illness and co-occurring substance use disorders who may be at risk of criminal justice involvement. This role exists to help people connect to the right behavioral health supports earlier-before crises escalate.

Key responsibilities include building rapport in the community; coordinating with behavioral health providers, healthcare organizations, emergency responders, law enforcement, and other partners; offering behavioral health education; completing screenings; providing motivational support; and linking individuals to appropriate treatment and community resources. You'll also support community education and training efforts that strengthen awareness and referral pathways.

Job Duties:

1. Conduct community outreach and engagement activities to identify adults with mental illness and co-occurring

substance use disorders who are at risk of criminal justice involvement.

2. Build collaborative relationships with law enforcement, EMS, fire departments, hospitals, behavioral health

providers, courts, and other community partners to promote early diversion and improve referral pathways.

3. Screen individuals for behavioral health needs and assist with early identification of mental health and

substance use concerns.

4. Provide brief engagement, motivational support, and crisis stabilization services to encourage participation in

treatment and recovery.
