title: Vice President, Data Center Operations
description:
5C DATA CENTERS

Join the Future of Digital Infrastructure

Are you a passionate Vice President, Data Center Operations looking to make a meaningful impact? We're building the next generation of digital infrastructure powering hyperscalers, AI innovation, and high-performance computing across North America.

JOB TITLE

Vice President, Data Center Operations

DEPARTMENT

DC Operations

LOCATION

USA

WORK ARRANGEMENT

Remote

TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS

20-40%

Role Summary

We are seeking a senior operations leader to own the performance, reliability, scalability, and operational readiness of our US hyperscale and AI data center portfolio.

This role leads site operations, critical facilities, operational readiness, workforce planning, health and safety, maintenance, incident management, vendor performance, and continuous improvement across all US sites. The role partners closely with Construction, Commissioning, Engineering, Quality, and Cloud Operations to move new facilities from construction into stable production operations.

This leader must be equally effective in a live mission-critical environment and in a high-growth organization where facilities, teams, processes, and operating infrastructure are being built at the same time. This role reports to our Senior Vice President, Operations.

How We Work at 5C

Our core values guide how we collaborate, make decisions, support one another, and serve our customers. We're looking for people who embrace them and help us build something great.

What You Will Do

Multi-Site Data Center Operations

  • Provide executive leadership for operations across all US data center sites (e.g., MEM, PHX, CMH, AUS)
  • Establish a consistent operating model across sites while accounting for site-specific infrastructure and customer requirements
  • Hold site leadership accountable, including Site Operations Directors, Chief Engineers, critical facilities teams, and data center technicians
  • Ensure 24x7 coverage and escalation capability, and intervene when operational, staffing, reliability, or safety risks emerge

Reliability & Critical Infrastructure

  • Drive operational excellence across:
    • Electrical distribution, switchgear, UPS, and generators
    • Mechanical and cooling systems, including liquid cooling
    • BMS/EPMS, controls, and fire/life-safety systems
  • Establish preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs
  • Enforce controls for maintenance, switching, change management, and work on or near critical infrastructure
  • Partner with Quality, which owns reliability engineering, and ensure sites act on findings through maintenance program changes, procedure updates, and corrective actions

AI & High-Density Compute Operations

  • Own operational requirements for AI, GPU, and HPC environments, including direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant quality, and leak detection and response
  • Align facility capacity, power, cooling, and readiness with Cloud Operations and deployment schedules
  • Serve as the operations executive for key customers at each site, owning SLA performance, escalations, and post-incident reviews

New Site Launch & Operational Readiness

  • Lead operational readiness for new data centers and major capacity expansions, delivered through the site critical facilities engineering teams
  • Ensure readiness plans cover:
    • Staffing and training
    • SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs
    • Maintenance programs and spare parts
    • Vendor support, access control, and escalation procedures
  • Establish formal turnover and acceptance criteria before facilities enter production
  • Ensure new-site engineering staff are hired and trained early enough that readiness work does not compete with live operations
  • Build repeatable site-launch models to bring capacity online faster and more consistently

Operational Governance & Incident Management

  • Maintain consistent standards across all sites for:
    • SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs
    • Preventive maintenance and change management
    • Incident management, escalation, and shift turnover
    • Training and qualification programs
  • Provide executive oversight during major events and outages, and ensure root-cause analysis and corrective actions are completed

Health, Safety & Security

  • Lead the HSE function and champion a strong safety culture across all sites
  • Ensure compliance with electrical safety, lockout/tagout, energized work, contractor safety, and regulatory requirements
  • Partner with Security on physical security and access control, and support customer, insurance, and regulatory audits

Workforce Planning & Leadership

  • Build scalable staffing models based on site capacity, infrastructure, and growth plans
  • Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to forecast hiring and build pipelines for critical roles
  • Coach and develop Site Operations Directors, the HSE leader, Chief Engineers, and other operational leaders
  • Build succession plans and a culture of accountability, technical discipline, and continuous learning

Financial, Vendor & Capacity Management

  • Develop and manage operating budgets, and partner with Finance on plans, forecasts, headcount, and capital
  • Set service-level expectations for critical vendors and monitor performance, cost, and safety
  • Translate business growth into requirements for power, cooling, space, staffing, and maintenance

Performance Management & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish operational KPIs and executive reporting, including:
    • Availability, critical incidents, and MTTR
    • Preventive maintenance completion and repeat failures
    • Safety performance and training completion
    • Operating expenses, energy efficiency, and site-readiness milestones
  • Use performance data to identify trends, fix root causes, and standardize improvements across sites

What You Bring

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in data center operations or critical facilities, including 7+ years of senior leadership
  • Experience operating hyperscale, colocation, cloud, HPC, or AI/GPU data center environments
  • Proven experience leading operations across multiple data centers or a large-scale data center campus
  • Experience opening new data centers and transitioning them from construction and commissioning into production operations
  • Experience supporting customer-facing data center environments with demanding uptime, capacity, and service requirements
  • Hands-on experience operating liquid-cooled, high-density environments (direct-to-chip or similar cooling technologies)
  • Ability to travel 20-40% and provide executive escalation support outside normal hours

Why Join 5C Data Centers?

At 5C, we believe great people build great companies. You'll build a rewarding career while helping shape the future of digital infrastructure - one of the fastest-growing industries in the world.

Career Growth

Build a rewarding career in one of the world's fastest-growing industries.

Industry Leadership

Help power the infrastructure behind AI and high-performance computing.

Entrepreneurial Culture

Your ideas matter - we empower employees to help shape our future.

Comprehensive Rewards

Competitive pay plus meaningful, lasting impact on the work you do.

Life at 5C

We're more than a workplace - we're a team of builders, innovators, and problem-solvers united by a shared purpose: creating infrastructure that powers the technologies transforming our world. Your voice matters here, and we encourage fresh ideas at every level.

Ready to Apply?

If this opportunity sounds like the right fit for you, we'd love to hear your story. Apply today and discover what your future could look like at 5C Data Centers.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. 5C evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

title: Coding Consultant Outpatient - PRN
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Coding Consultant Outpatient – PRN based in the United States.

Join a healthcare technology environment dedicated to making medical data more secure, accessible, and actionable.
As a Coding Consultant Outpatient, you will leverage your medical coding expertise to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of outpatient healthcare records.
You will review clinical documentation, assign appropriate diagnosis and procedure codes, and support accurate reimbursement and hospital reporting.
Working remotely, you will collaborate with healthcare professionals and coding specialists to resolve documentation issues and maintain high-quality coding standards.
This part-time, as-needed position offers flexibility while allowing you to contribute to essential healthcare information management processes.
You will work with complex outpatient cases, including emergency department encounters, procedures, injections and infusions, and evaluation and management leveling.
If you are a credentialed coding professional with strong attention to detail and a commitment to continuous learning, this role offers an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on healthcare data quality.

Accountabilities

  • Review and code outpatient medical records: Analyze clinical documentation and accurately assign diagnosis and procedure codes in accordance with applicable coding guidelines and established standards.
  • Ensure coding accuracy and sequencing: Assign and sequence codes based on medical record documentation, including appropriate discharge dispositions and facility-level coding classifications.
  • Support hospital reporting and reimbursement: Abstract and enter coded data to meet hospital statistical, reporting, and reimbursement requirements, including accurate Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) assignments.
  • Handle complex outpatient specialties: Apply coding expertise across emergency department encounters, same-day surgery, observation services, ancillary services, injections and infusions, procedures, modifiers, and evaluation and management (E/M) leveling.
  • Identify documentation improvement opportunities: Communicate coding discrepancies, documentation gaps, and potential improvement opportunities to the appropriate personnel for follow-up and resolution.
  • Maintain quality and productivity standards: Achieve a target coding accuracy rate of at least 95% and an APC assignment accuracy rate of at least 95%, while meeting site-specific productivity expectations.
  • Collaborate with healthcare stakeholders: Communicate professionally with colleagues, management, and hospital personnel regarding clinical documentation, coding decisions, and reimbursement-related issues.
  • Maintain professional credentials: Track and complete continuing education requirements to keep certifications current and remain informed about changes in coding guidelines and industry practices.
  • Participate in ongoing education: Attend employer-sponsored training sessions, educational meetings, and in-service programs to strengthen technical knowledge and coding performance.
  • Follow ethical and compliance standards: Adhere to the American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA) Code of Ethics, applicable Health Information Management policies, HIPAA requirements, and relevant confidentiality standards.
  • Demonstrate professional excellence: Maintain a customer-focused, dependable, flexible, and collaborative approach while exercising sound judgment and taking initiative in a remote working environment.

Requirements

  • Professional certification: An active coding credential from AHIMA, such as RHIA, RHIT, or CCS, or from AAPC, such as CPC, CPC-H, COC, CIC, or CRC. CCS certification is specifically required for the highlighted emergency department and complex outpatient coding needs.
  • Relevant experience: At least 2 years of hospital-based or coding consulting experience, with 3 or more years of outpatient coding experience preferred for the specialized requirements of this position.
  • Outpatient coding expertise: Strong working knowledge of outpatient diagnosis and procedure coding, with proficiency in emergency department coding, injections and infusions, procedures, modifiers, facility leveling, and E/M leveling.
  • Specialty coding knowledge: Experience in areas such as same-day surgery, observation services, ancillary services, and Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) assignment.
  • Medical terminology and documentation: Excellent understanding of medical terminology, clinical documentation, coding guidelines, and the relationship between accurate coding, reimbursement, and reporting.
  • Coding software proficiency: Experience using computerized coding, encoding, and medical record abstraction systems. Familiarity with Epic and Clintegrity is strongly preferred.
  • Accuracy and analytical skills: Exceptional attention to detail, sound judgment, and the ability to interpret complex clinical records while maintaining high coding quality standards.
  • Communication and teamwork: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain coding issues clearly and collaborate effectively with healthcare staff and remote colleagues.
  • Organization and time management: Ability to manage competing priorities, meet productivity targets, work independently, and maintain consistent performance in a remote, flexible environment.
  • Professional development: Willingness to complete annual introductory HIPAA examinations and other required assessments, maintain continuing education credits, and stay current with relevant coding standards.
  • Ethics and confidentiality: Commitment to professional integrity, patient confidentiality, data security, and compliance with applicable healthcare regulations.
  • Work authorization: Must be authorized to work in the United States. Employment sponsorship is not available for this position.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: Estimated total cash compensation range of $20–$35 USD, depending on location, responsibilities, experience, skills, and other relevant factors.
  • Flexible PRN schedule: Part-time, as-needed work that offers flexibility in managing professional commitments and personal responsibilities.
  • Retirement savings: Access to a 401(k) savings plan with employer matching contributions for eligible PRN employees.
  • Continuing education: Free continuing education units (CEUs) provided annually to support ongoing professional development and certification maintenance.
  • Professional development stipend: Financial assistance toward education expenses and professional membership dues, including AHIMA and AAPC.
  • Remote work equipment: Provision of essential equipment, including a laptop, monitor, mouse, keyboard, and headset.
  • Comprehensive onboarding: Structured training led by an experienced, credentialed coding manager to support role readiness and consistent performance.
  • Mentorship and management support: Access to supportive, service-oriented management and professional guidance throughout your assignment.
  • Full-time benefits distinction: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid time off, and paid holidays are listed for full-time employees and are not specified as benefits for this PRN position.

title: Designated Safeguarding Lead
description:
About The Role

Working Hours: 35 Hours per week
Contract Type: Full time / Temporary (24 Months)
Working style: Onsite - Employees carry out their job primarily from a physical workplace, such as an office
Closing date: 05 November 2026
Interview Method: In Person (Face to Face)
Location: Manchester (North, Central or South locality)


Skilled Worker Sponsorship
You must already have a valid right to work in the UK documentation, as we cannot offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Are you an experienced school Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) looking to influence safeguarding outcomes across the whole of Manchester?

Manchester is seeking an outstanding safeguarding professional from the education sector to join our new Multi-Agency Child Protection Teams (MACPTs) during this exciting period of transformation. This is a unique opportunity to bring your school-based safeguarding expertise into a city-wide role, helping to shape decisions for children at risk of significant harm and ensuring that the education voice is fully embedded within child protection practice.

As Manchester implements the Families First Partnership reforms, education is a critical safeguarding partner. The MACPT Education DSL will work alongside Children's Social Care, Health, Police and Family Help colleagues to ensure that children's educational experiences, attendance, inclusion and lived experiences are central to safeguarding decision-making.

The role sits at the heart of multi-agency safeguarding and child protection activity.

You will:

  • Provide expert safeguarding advice and consultation to schools and partner agencies.
  • Act as the key conduit for safeguarding information sharing between schools, education services and the MACPT.
  • Review and analyse safeguarding concerns, education intelligence, attendance information and inclusion data.
  • Contribute directly to multi-agency child protection decision-making where there are concerns about significant harm.
  • Liaise with schools, academies, colleges, alternative provision, SEND, Attendance, Children Missing Education (CME) and Elective Home Education (EHE) services.
  • Support strategy discussions, child protection conferences and safeguarding planning.
  • Identify patterns, risks and emerging safeguarding issues affecting children and communities.
  • Help strengthen relationships between schools and safeguarding partners across Manchester.
  • Contribute to safeguarding quality assurance, audits, learning reviews and inspection readiness.

Who are We Looking For?

An exceptional safeguarding leader who has:

  • Significant experience as a school Designated Safeguarding Lead.
  • Extensive safeguarding expertise and a strong track record of working with children, young people and families.
  • Experience of complex child protection decision-making and multi-agency working.
  • Excellent knowledge of safeguarding legislation and guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education and Working Together to Safeguard Children.
  • Strong analytical skills, professional curiosity and sound judgement.
  • Experience of attending and contributing to Child Protection Conferences and safeguarding processes.
  • The credibility and confidence to work effectively with senior leaders, social care, health and police colleagues.

Why Apply?

This is a rare opportunity to:

  • Influence safeguarding practice and decision-making across the city.
  • Develop strategic and operational expertise in child protection and multi-agency safeguarding.
  • Be part of Manchester's transformational Families First programme.
  • Help shape how education contributes to child protection in the future.
  • Work within a highly skilled multi-agency environment focused on achieving better outcomes for vulnerable children and families.

If you are passionate about safeguarding, have substantial DSL experience, and want to make a difference for some of Manchester's most vulnerable children, we would love to hear from you.

For queries about the role, please contact Raamona Johnson Statutory Lead for Safeguarding and Community Education team on [email protected] to arrange a convenient time to discuss the role. This route is for vacancy related enquiries only and should not be used to submit applications.

Pre-employment Checks

If you are successful, your appointment will be subject to completing the relevant pre-employment checks. These checks will be carried out as part of our recruitment process and may include:

  • DBS (Disclosure and Barring Service) Clearance – This post is covered by the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 (Exceptions) Order 1975 (amended in 2013). Appointable candidates will be required to apply for an Enhanced DBS check as appropriate. Information provided by you or the DBS will be handled confidentially and in accordance with the DBS Code of Practice. We have policies covering the secure handling of DBS information and the recruitment of ex-offenders, which are available on request. - If you have lived or worked abroad for 3 months or more in the last 5 years, or 12 months or more in the last 10 years (while aged 18 or over), please refer to GOV.UK guidance on obtaining overseas police checks or Certificates of Good Character.
For more information on these checks, please visit checks page.

About the Candidate

We are looking for an experienced school Designated Safeguarding Lead to join our new Multi-Agency Child Protection Teams (MACPTs) to bring your school-based safeguarding expertise into a city-wide role, helping to shape decisions for children at risk of significant harm and ensuring that the education voice is fully embedded within child protection practice.

You will have significant experience as a school Designated Safeguarding Lead, strong safeguarding expertise and experience of complex child protection decision-making and multi-agency working.
You will need excellent knowledge of safeguarding legislation and guidance, including Keeping Children Safe in Education and Working Together to Safeguard Children as well as strong analytical skills, professional curiosity and sound judgement.

We’ll use the following essential criteria to decide which candidates to invite to assessment. Use your personal statement to provide evidence of how you meet each one, supported by relevant examples:

  • Significant experience as a school Designated Safeguarding Lead, including oversight of child protection and safeguarding records
  • Extensive safeguarding experience knowledge of safeguarding practice as well as a strong track record of working with children, young people and families
  • Experience of attending and contributing to Child Protection conferences and multi-agency decision-making
For guidance on how to write your personal statement, please visit How to Apply - Manchester City Council.

If you’re invited to assessment, we’ll look at a wider range of the role requirements. For more detail, please see the role profile.

Use of AI

You may use AI to support your application, but all examples must be your own and based on real experience. Applications may be withdrawn if content is misleading or presents someone else's experience as your own. Internal candidates may also face disciplinary action.

Guaranteed Assessment Scheme
Applicants who meet the essential shortlisting criteria and are eligible under the Guaranteed Assessment Scheme will be progressed to the assessment stage.

Support and Adjustments
If you're successful in securing a role, we'll make every effort to provide the support, equipment and reasonable adjustments you need to carry out your duties. Where needed, we'll consider adapting aspects of the role. Find out more about our inclusion and wellbeing.

About Us

Working for Manchester City Council is a chance to make a real difference in a diverse city. You’ll help improve lives and support our local communities. Working together, we can create better public services for everyone.

title: Mohs Assistant
description:
Job Summary:

The Clinical Medical Assistant will assist the provider with patient care. He/She will create an atmosphere that reflects the level of standards and care that patients can expect to receive from this practice. The provider entrusts the goodwill of patients to the assistant, therefore, extending the provider's relationship with the patient.

To be successful in this position, the assistant must be friendly, polite, tactful, and professional in appearance and manner at all times. He/She will be able to communicate with the physician and patient and be mindful of patient confidentiality. He/She will be able to evaluate and respond to a patient's needs and relay the provider's instructions. The successful medical assistant will be a team player and respectful of his/her co-workers.

Hours:

Monday-Friday:

  • 6:40 a.m. until completion of cases.
  • Lunch: Varying times and lengths based on case load.
  • The office closes at 5:00 p.m.; however, cases may extend later requiring assistance until completion. This occurs without notice.

Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • Certified Medical Assistant or Licensed Practical Nurse preferred but not required.
  • Experience with surgical procedures preferred but not required.
  • Additional roles may be available with 4-year Bachelor of Science degree

Compensation:

Competitive pay based on education and experience plus paid time off and benefits.

Work Environment:

  • DASWLA is a high-volume, private medical facility where the work environment is sometimes busy, hectic and/or noisy with interruptions.
  • There is exposure to routine dermatological diseases and procedures with a risk of exposure to bloodborne pathogens.

Skills:

  • Able to speak English clearly and make self-understood.
  • Good verbal and written communication skills including grammar and spelling.
  • Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and fractions.
  • Compassion and care in dealing with others.
  • Prioritization of tasks.
  • Comprehension of provider's instructions and the ability to relay this information to patients as well as the wherewithal to seek clarification, additional information or advice when necessary.
  • Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Windows, Microsoft Word and Microsoft Outlook software.
  • General knowledge of electronic medical records is helpful but not required.

Physical Demands:

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position whether standing or sitting for extended periods of time.
  • Must be able to occasionally move about the office to access shared office equipment or access charts.
  • Must be able to operate a computer and accessories such as printer, mouse, keyboard, and other office productivity machinery such as a calculator.
  • Must have dexterity necessary to operate surgical instruments such as scissors.
  • Must be able to occasionally ascend/descend a ladder to access some medical supplies.
  • Must be able to position self to maintain computers and other desk equipment on top of and under the desk as well as in exam rooms when positioning patients and assisting the provider.
  • Must be able to accurately communicate information to and from patients and providers in person, in writing and on the telephone.
  • Must be able to visually inspect and observe patient's skin conditions including, but not limited to, color variations and the presence of abnormal conditions.
  • Must be able to assist in transporting and positioning patients for exam or procedure.
  • Must be able to occasionally transport movable medical equipment such as mobile lasers, surgical lamps, etc.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

As assigned, but not limited to the following:

  • Interact and assist patients in person and phone calls. Escort patient to and from exam room. Maintain the physical and electronic medical record by confirming all information has been documented. Take and log patient vitals.
  • Assist provider with patient care, including, but not limited to, Mohs micrographic surgery, biopsy, wound care, suture removal, order preparation, prepare injections for administration (Kenalog, sclerotherapy, etc.), photodynamic therapy (PDT) and cosmetic services.
  • Manage medical record insofar as written requests and phone calls.
  • Referrals from physician/to physician: scheduling as well as preparing and sending the referral.
  • Fax referral status notes to referring physicians for office visits.
  • Initiate prior authorizations, when necessary, such as for medications or imaging studies.
  • Handle/route questions regarding schedule or procedure insofar as the physician's clinic is concerned.
  • Prepare and send noncompliance letters to patients, or informative letters regarding upcoming appointments or procedures.
  • Discuss, schedule and consent surgeries and cosmetic procedures.
  • Assist with clinic preparatory duties including, but not limited to, restocking supplies, instrument washing and sterilization, laundering surgical wraps/drapes.
  • Assist general dermatology providers with clinical duties as assigned.
  • Clerical duties, including, but not limited to, assisting the call center in answering incoming phone calls, scheduling appointments, and managing incoming referrals and/or assisting the reception check-in center.

This description is intended to provide only basic guidelines for meeting job requirements. Responsibilities, knowledge, skills, abilities and working conditions may change as needs evolve.

    • Excellent English proficiency: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to write natural scripts, deliver clear narration, and communicate confidently on camera.

        • Flexible working arrangements: Work remotely from anywhere in the world, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement and a delivery schedule agreed in advance.

This position is responsible for scheduling, maintenance and construction activities, as well as working in the field as a member of the crew within the Public Works Department. May be requested to fulfill some responsibilities of Director of Public Works in his or her absence.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

Supervises departmental personnel

  • Assists with the daily supervision of all employees, the establishment of scheduling practices and assigning appropriate tasks
  • Provides on-site supervision of Public Works crew as directed
  • Answers field questions from Public Works crew and the public
  • Ensures proper work zone signage is in place on job site
  • Ensures Public Works crews utilize proper safety equipment and procedures on project sites
  • Assists with directing Snow and Ice Removal Operations.

Perform administrative duties related to departmental functions

  • Maintains adequate inventories of supplies and equipment as directed
  • Purchasing supplies following City policies and procedures
  • Advises Director of Public Works regarding progress of projects and assigned jobs
  • Assists and works with the Director of Public Works on departmental projects
  • Assists with the development of bid specifications for equipment and/or projects as directed
  • Completes all reports and paperwork as required

Operates the dump truck and other large equipment

  • Transports materials to and from the work site
  • Operates other equipment as required

Install and Maintain Potable Water System

  • Removes and Replaces distribution components as needed.
  • Determines if distribution components can be repaired or must be replaced.
  • Ensures distribution components are operating properly.

Performs other duties related to departmental activities

  • Attend training and other professional development as needed or required

Performs similar duties for other City departments as assigned

Performs other duties as directed

Education and Experience

The person in this position must have a high school diploma or its equivalent; some college or vocational training in civil engineering or a related field is encouraged. At least five (5) years of progressive responsibility in Water construction and maintenance experience is strongly recommended, with a min of three (3) years of supervisory experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.

Licenses and Certifications

The person in this position must have a valid Missouri CDL Class B with airbrakes and tanker endorsement or be able to obtain. Must be able to obtain a Missouri DS3 license. Must be able to pass pre-employment drug and alcohol test and random drug and alcohol testing. Must be able to complete confined space training, competent person training/certification, vactor truck training, CCTV equipment training, backhoe training.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Knowledge

  • Apply supervisory principles, practices and procedures
  • Project management practices and procedures
  • City's purchasing policies and procedures
  • Inventory management principles and methods
  • Proper maintenance, repair and use of heavy equipment, including aerial bucket lift truck, tandem axle dump truck and skid loader
  • Minor mechanical repairs on the truck and other machinery
  • Proper installation, maintenance and repair of water and wastewater systems
  • Proper storage and use of various chemicals
  • Layout of city streets
  • Basic carpentry, plumbing, electrical and concrete techniques
  • Maintenance methods of grounds, buildings and equipment
  • Basic equipment maintenance and repair
  • Basic civil engineering principles
  • Proper materials and equipment
  • Federal and state statutes concerning the work of the department
  • Basic mathematical skills.
  • General functions and operations of municipal government
  • City and Department policies and procedures

Skills and Abilities

  • Apply supervisory techniques to practical situations
  • Manage a departmental budget
  • Develop bid specifications
  • Ability to use a personal computer, MS Office software, internet, and other departmental programs
  • Effectively managing personnel, equipment and supplies to maximize departmental efficiency
  • Use various types of heavy equipment, including single axle dump truck and skid loader
  • Examine a repair or maintenance issue and determine an effective solution
  • Use common sense
  • Pay attention to detail
  • Complete detailed work accurately
  • Work effectively with a wide range of people
  • Meet specified deadlines
  • Prioritize daily workflow
  • Work as a team member with other employees
  • Communicate effectively with others, both oral and written
  • Work autonomously when necessary
  • Handle multiple tasks simultaneously with frequent interruptions
  • Deal with others in a professional manner
  • Maintain professional composure in heated situations
  • Develop, implement and follow departmental and City policies and procedures
  • Effectively communicate with the public in a professional manner

title: Senior Technical Trainer — Machine Learning
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Technical Trainer — Machine Learning based in France.

We are seeking a hands-on machine learning practitioner with a passion for teaching to design and deliver engaging technical courses for engineers. In this remote freelance role, you will help learners progress from core machine learning concepts to training and evaluating their own models through practical, lab-based learning. You will collaborate with curriculum specialists and production teams to develop clear lessons, hands-on exercises, and real-world demonstrations. The focus is on sharing your technical expertise through compelling scripts, video presentations, and lab walkthroughs rather than managing production tasks. The initial paid course project typically lasts around three months and can be completed alongside existing professional commitments. With flexible hours and a delivery plan agreed in advance, the opportunity may lead to further projects or a full-time position.

Accountabilities

  • Design and develop course content: Collaborate with the curriculum team to define course structure, sections, lessons, practical labs, and notebooks that support progressive learning.

  • Create hands-on learning experiences: Write detailed lab specifications for the dedicated lab development team, then test the completed environments to ensure they work as intended.

  • Write engaging educational scripts: Develop short, story-driven video lessons of approximately six minutes each, making machine learning concepts accessible, intuitive, and relevant to engineers.

  • Deliver technical presentations: Narrate scripted lessons confidently in English and record demonstrations and lab-solution walkthroughs that reinforce key concepts.

  • Apply practical machine learning expertise: Build course material grounded in real experience with training, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models.

  • Incorporate editorial feedback: Work through structured reviews, particularly during the initial course section, and refine content to meet established quality and teaching standards.

  • Collaborate remotely: Coordinate with curriculum and production teams through weekly syncs and Slack, maintaining sufficient time-zone overlap with colleagues based in Europe and Asia.

  • Focus on teaching and technical content: Partner with the production team, which manages video editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

    • Requirements:

    • Hands-on machine learning experience: Demonstrated ability to train, evaluate, and ship models using frameworks such as scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.

    • Strong technical communication skills: Ability to explain machine learning concepts, including the reasoning behind different approaches, clearly to engineers who are new to the field.

    • Excellent English proficiency: Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to write natural scripts, deliver clear narration, and communicate confidently on camera.

    • A genuine passion for teaching: Evidence of enjoying knowledge-sharing through online courses, tutorials, technical talks, workshops, mentoring, or other educational activities.

    • Current technical knowledge: An active interest in machine learning developments and a commitment to continuously learning and improving.

    • Presentation confidence: Comfort presenting technical material on camera in a clear, engaging, and accessible way.

    • Openness to feedback: Willingness to follow an established teaching methodology, collaborate with editors, and improve course content through structured feedback.

    • Preferred qualifications:

      • Experience publishing courses on platforms such as Udemy, Pluralsight, or Coursera, or creating educational content on YouTube.

      • Experience writing a technical book or teaching at a university, bootcamp, or similar educational setting.

      • Practical knowledge of fine-tuning, MLOps, or deploying machine learning models in production.

      • Cloud machine learning certifications related to AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or Databricks.

        • Benefits:

        • Competitive project-based compensation: A fixed fee is agreed upfront for each course, based on its length and technical complexity, with competitive rates for advanced topics and exceptional instructors.

        • Flexible working arrangements: Work remotely from anywhere in the world, with no fixed weekly-hour requirement and a delivery schedule agreed in advance.

        • Compatible with existing commitments: Complete the initial freelance course project alongside your current job or other professional responsibilities.

        • Defined project scope: The initial course project typically takes around three months, providing a clear timeframe for planning and delivery.

        • Payment upon completion: Receive the agreed course fee when the completed course is delivered.

        • Long-term career potential: Successful collaboration may lead to additional course projects or a full-time opportunity as part of a growing trainer network.

        • Dedicated production support: Focus on instructional content and teaching while the production team handles editing, animation, lab infrastructure, and publishing.

        • Collaborative remote environment: Work closely with curriculum and production specialists through regular team syncs and Slack communication.

        • Professional visibility: Showcase your technical expertise and teaching ability by developing practical learning experiences for a broad engineering audience.

title: Head of Communications
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Head of Communications based in the United States.

The Head of Communications will establish and lead the communications function for a growing healthcare organization delivering patient-centered care across multiple states. As the first dedicated communications leader, you will shape the public relations strategy, strengthen media relationships, and elevate executive visibility across the healthcare industry. This role combines strategic leadership with hands-on execution, spanning external communications, employee engagement, thought leadership, and crisis management. You will work closely with executive leadership, marketing, social media, legal, compliance, and operations to ensure clear, consistent messaging aligned with business priorities. You will also manage external public relations partners, oversee communications around organizational growth and acquisitions, and build scalable processes that support a distributed workforce. This is an opportunity for a communications professional who thrives in a fast-moving environment and wants to make a meaningful impact on reputation, employee connection, and organizational growth.

Accountabilities

  • Develop and lead the overall public relations and communications strategy, establishing annual priorities and plans for media engagement, thought leadership, conference participation, and industry recognition.

  • Build and maintain relationships with healthcare trade publications, national business media, and regional outlets, serving as a primary spokesperson and preparing press releases, fact sheets, organizational descriptions, and other media materials.

  • Manage external public relations agencies and communications advisors, setting objectives, overseeing budgets and deliverables, and evaluating performance against measurable outcomes.

  • Strengthen executive visibility by securing speaking engagements, contributed articles, opinion pieces, and industry awards that position senior leaders as credible voices in home-based care, palliative care, and the broader healthcare sector.

  • Lead issues management and crisis communications in collaboration with legal, compliance, operations, and external advisors, maintaining response protocols and prepared statements that support timely, accurate, and HIPAA-conscious communications.

  • Own internal communications for a geographically distributed workforce, including leadership updates, company announcements, organizational changes, and integration communications that keep employees informed and connected to the organization's mission.

  • Coordinate communications around strategic milestones, business growth, acquisitions, and other major developments, ensuring consistent messaging across internal and external audiences.

  • Partner with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to support organizational priorities, recruitment, referral development, and payer relationships.

  • Collaborate with marketing, brand, and social media teams to maintain a consistent organizational voice while respecting the distinct responsibilities of communications and marketing.

  • Establish and monitor key performance indicators, including earned media coverage, share of voice, executive visibility, and employee engagement, using insights to refine communications strategies.

  • Build the communications function from the ground up, establishing processes, priorities, external partnerships, and scalable capabilities, with the potential to develop a team as needs evolve.

    • Requirements:

    • At least 7 years of experience in communications or public relations, including responsibility for both internal and external communications.

    • Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, or a related discipline.

    • Experience in healthcare communications, ideally within home-based care, value-based care, palliative care, hospice, or a related healthcare environment.

    • Established relationships with healthcare media outlets or the ability to develop them quickly, along with a demonstrated record of securing meaningful media coverage.

    • Proven experience positioning executives as trusted public voices through media interviews, conference appearances, thought leadership, bylines, and industry recognition.

    • Experience managing public relations agencies, external advisors, and communications vendors, including setting expectations, managing budgets, and measuring results.

    • Exceptional writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear, compelling communications across press releases, executive speeches, opinion pieces, employee announcements, and crisis statements.

    • Strong judgment and experience managing sensitive issues, reputational risks, and crisis communications in collaboration with legal, compliance, and operational stakeholders.

    • Ability to communicate complex or sensitive information clearly, accurately, and appropriately to employees, executives, media representatives, and other audiences.

    • Demonstrated ability to operate independently as an organization's first communications hire, establishing structure, setting priorities, and executing strategy while collaborating effectively with marketing and social media teams.

    • Experience working in a fast-paced, scaling, or startup-like environment, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, adapt to changing priorities, and deliver results efficiently.

    • Strong strategic thinking, project management, stakeholder engagement, and measurement skills.

    • Ability to work remotely within the United States and travel as needed, with travel expected to be up to 20%.

    • Willingness to disclose any current or future need for employment-based immigration sponsorship or related employer action before an offer is extended.

      • Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible full-time employees.

      • Flexible spending accounts: Options for eligible medical and dependent care expenses.

title: Shift Operations Supervisor
description:
Panchero's - NOW HIRING TEAM LEADS

Panchero's Mexican Grill is looking for friendly and enthusiastic people to join the team! You will have the opportunity to be part of a positive and fun culture while enhancing your job skills for further opportunities within our company!

**Flexible schedule**
**Competitive pay**
**Food Discounts**
**Career Advancement Opportunities**
**Fun Workplace Culture**

JOB DUTIES INCLUDE (but not limited to):

· Food Prep & Burrito Building

· Customer Service

· Leadership & Employee Management

· Cash Handling

· Kitchen and Restaurant Sanitation

· Other duties as assigned

EDUCATION AND TRAINING: No educational requirements.

WORKING EXPERIENCE: Leadership experience required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Bending, stooping, reaching, twisting, lifting, pushing, pulling and moving items
  • Able to lift up to 50 lbs. without assistance
  • Requires the ability to move and stand for long periods of time

WHO WE ARE

Pancheros grew from our very first restaurant-a local favorite in the college town of Iowa City back in 1992-to one of the most beloved Mexican Fast casual brands in the country. Scratch-made dough and fresh-pressed flour tortillas are integral to our burritos. Ingredients perfectly mixed into every bite is also a key component of Burritos Better Built, so in 2002 we introduced Bob The ToolÂ® to mix before roll. And of course, our homemade queso, which has earned a fan following for its ooey, gooey, extra cheesy, velvety texture and zip of zesty, mouthwatering flavor perfect for chip-dipping or slathering on your burrito.

WHAT SETS US APART

Delicious starts with a solid foundation.

Our fresh-pressed tortillas are the key to Burritos Better Built. Each one, made from house-made dough every morning and fresh-pressed in front of your eyes until perfectly golden brown. Then tightly wrapped to support all the freshest ingredients of your choice for a burrito that stands up to your wildest cravings.

URRITO. Burritos without the B.S.

When you keep things as fresh as we do, there's simply no need for the B and the S. (Otherwise known as shortcuts like fryers, freezers, packaged tortillas-we'd never!) We take pride in putting in the extra effort to do things the right way-from scratch, by hand-because that's what delivers the flavor that really sets us apart.

All the right stuff in all the right places.

The key to our burritos is mixing every ingredient together in every bite, because no one wants a mouthful of sour cream or rice. We take mixing so seriously, we even created our very own tool to get the job done right: Bob the Tool. Your single-handed assurance that every burrito you order at Pancheros won't just meet your expectations, it'll exceed them.

We take a fresh approach to service, too.

Every time you walk into one of our restaurants, we're on a mission to make your day even better. Carefully preparing your food from scratch, keeping our restaurants in tip top shape, making online ordering, delivery, and catering as smooth as our queso, and providing quick, courteous service that makes every meal an unforgettable one.

Location:4701 1st Ave SE, Ste 1, Cedar Rapids, IA 52402

Reports to the Assistant Manger on duty.

title: Director, Field Operations
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Field Operations based in the United States.

The Director, Field Operations will lead the development and implementation of commercial field operations capabilities in preparation for a major pharmaceutical product launch. This leadership role will translate commercial strategy into scalable processes, systems, and operational frameworks that support high-performing customer-facing teams. You will oversee field infrastructure, territory management, CRM workflows, targeting deployment, incentive compensation, and performance reporting. Working across Commercial, Analytics, IT, Finance, Compliance, and other business functions, you will ensure seamless coordination and operational excellence. The position offers the opportunity to build launch-ready capabilities within a fast-paced, late-stage biopharmaceutical environment focused on advancing innovative treatments for psychiatric and neurological conditions. You will establish the governance, technology, and processes needed to support successful commercialization and sustainable business growth. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced pharmaceutical operations professional who thrives in dynamic environments and enjoys building scalable solutions from the ground up.

Accountabilities

  • Field Operations Strategy and Execution: Develop and implement the field operations roadmap, including launch milestones, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, service levels, and escalation processes.

  • Field Force Readiness: Coordinate onboarding, system access, equipment, training logistics, roster administration, and ongoing operational support in collaboration with HR, IT, sales leadership, and external vendors.

  • Territory and Targeting Management: Operationalize field force design, territory alignments, healthcare professional (HCP) and healthcare organization (HCO) affiliations, account hierarchies, target lists, call plans, and phased launch transitions.

  • CRM Ownership and Optimization: Serve as the commercial business owner for Veeva Vault CRM field workflows, overseeing requirements gathering, user acceptance testing (UAT), software releases, adoption, and ongoing support in partnership with IT and Data Strategy.

  • Data Quality and Process Automation: Maintain accurate operational data across accounts, affiliations, assignments, and field activities while introducing automation and approved AI-enabled workflows to improve efficiency and consistency.

  • Incentive Compensation Administration: Manage incentive compensation processes, including eligibility, goal setting, payout validation, dispute resolution, governance, documentation, and field communications.

  • Analytics and Performance Management: Partner with Commercial Analytics to support targeting, segmentation, sizing assumptions, KPI definitions, dashboards, performance reporting, and regular business reviews.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Sales, Market Access, Finance, HR, IT, Legal, Compliance, and Analytics to ensure aligned execution, operational controls, incentive plan approvals, and effective change management.

  • Vendor and Budget Oversight: Manage field operations vendors, budgets, deliverables, and service quality while implementing standardized workflows, documentation, and business continuity plans.

  • Scalable Commercial Infrastructure: Build reliable operational capabilities that support the initial launch and can evolve with future commercial expansion, maintaining compliance and operational readiness throughout growth.

    • Requirements

    • Education: Bachelor's degree required; a degree in business, life sciences, analytics, healthcare, or a related discipline is preferred.

    • Professional Experience: At least 10 years of relevant professional experience, with progressive responsibility in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or life sciences commercial operations, sales operations, or field force effectiveness.

    • Launch Experience: Demonstrated experience supporting pre-launch preparation or commercial product launches, ideally involving specialty pharmaceuticals or complex therapeutic areas.

    • CRM and Commercial Technology: Hands-on experience with commercial CRM operations, including Veeva Vault CRM, Veeva data products, Salesforce, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable platforms.

    • Field Operations Expertise: Strong knowledge of territory management, targeting deployment, call planning, incentive compensation, field reporting, and operational governance.

    • Strategic and Operational Execution: Ability to translate commercial strategies into practical processes, system requirements, internal controls, and measurable business outcomes.

    • Leadership and Collaboration: Excellent cross-functional leadership, communication, project management, analytical judgment, and stakeholder management skills.

    • Vendor and Process Management: Experience overseeing external vendors, managing deliverables, improving workflows, and building standardized processes that support business continuity and scalability.

    • Compliance and Data Privacy: Working knowledge of pharmaceutical compliance standards and data privacy requirements applicable to commercial field operations.

    • Preferred Experience: Familiarity with HCP/HCO account hierarchies, account-based field teams, reimbursement support models, and specialty pharmacy or patient hub-related field interfaces.

    • Additional Preferred Skills: Experience with incentive compensation governance, territory alignment platforms, phased field deployment, workflow automation, and approved AI-enabled business applications.

    • Travel Requirements: Willingness to travel up to 10% based on business needs.

    • Personal Attributes: A hands-on, adaptable leader who can operate effectively in a lean, fast-moving environment, manage competing priorities, and build operational capabilities from the ground up.

      • Benefits

      • Competitive base salary: $190,000–$240,000 per year, depending on experience, skills, and geographic location.

      • Additional compensation: Potential eligibility for performance-based bonuses and equity awards.

      • Comprehensive healthcare: 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for employees and their dependents.

      • Retirement savings: 401(k) plan with company matching contributions, with vesting after the first month following the employee's start date.

      • Flexible time off: Flexible paid time off to support personal well-being and work-life balance.

      • Parental leave: Generous parental leave benefits.

      • Additional perks: Supplementary employee perks and benefits designed to support a positive workplace experience.

      • Remote work: Remote position based in the United States, with travel of up to 10% as business needs require.

title: Senior Systems Administrator
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Systems Administrator based in the United States.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Systems Administrator to oversee and optimize enterprise IT infrastructure in a fully remote, healthcare-focused environment. In this role, you will take ownership of critical systems spanning Windows and Linux servers, cloud platforms, virtualization, networking, storage, and endpoint management. You will play a key role in maintaining infrastructure reliability, strengthening security, and ensuring optimal system performance across the organization. From leading infrastructure upgrades and migrations to improving disaster recovery capabilities, your expertise will directly support operational continuity. You will also serve as a senior technical escalation point, helping teams resolve complex challenges efficiently. This is an opportunity to combine hands-on technical leadership, proactive problem-solving, and infrastructure innovation in a mission-driven healthcare technology environment.

Accountabilities:

  • Administer, maintain, and optimize Windows and Linux server environments, including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, and file services.

  • Manage virtualization platforms such as VMware vSphere or Microsoft Hyper-V, ensuring stability, performance, and efficient resource utilization.

title: Data Engineer - 12 Month Max Term Contract
description:
A great opportunity to work with one of Australia’s largest general insurers

Be part of a collaborative and innovative data team

Open to Sydney candidates only - Hybrid working

About Hollard

Hollard Insurance is part of the Hollard Group of Companies and one of Australia’s largest general insurers Australia and New Zealand. We underwrite a broad range of general insurance products, including motor, home, contents, business, bicycle and pet, in proud partnership with some of Australia's biggest consumer brands and broker businesses. As an independent and privately owned company, we believe we can go further together – for our people, customers, communities and partners – through an innovative approach to providing insurance.

Our state-of-the‑art facilities in North Sydney reflect our commitment to providing innovative workspaces that support hybrid and remote work.

Your Team

You will be part of a multi-disciplinary technology team, working closely with our customers (business, software vendors and partners) and strategic project teams. The team is responsible for the development, implementation and maintenance of the Hollard Data Platform that support our customers through all aspect of the insurance value chain. The team is involved in all aspects from design through to testing, implementation, maintenance and support. You will be surrounded by data professionals that strive for excellence and implement data best practices to realise business value.

Your Role

As a Data Engineer, you will report to the Product Owner your key focus areas will be to design, build, and support the delivery of modern data engineering solutions in the Azure data platform and legacy SAS platform, balancing the enhancement of ETL/ELT processes while supporting short term data requirements from across the business.

You will work collaboratively with cross‑functional teams within Hollard, including the Infrastructure DevOps team, solution architects, subject matter experts, data modelers, Finance, Underwriting, Operations, etc. This collaboration aims to ensure that Hollard’s data platform ecosystem is optimal in supporting business needs. Additionally, you will work collaboratively with vendors and partners to ensure that data engineering delivery and practices meet Hollard’s standards.

Your duties and responsibilities

Develop, maintain, and enhance SAS 9.4 programs (Base SAS, SAS Macros, PROC SQL, and DI Studio/Enterprise Guide where applicable) for ETL, data preparation, and analytics.

Load and refresh data in SQL Server from SAS, using SAS/ACCESS, LIBNAME, and pass through SQL, with attention to load performance and data integrity.

Monitor and support production SAS jobs and schedules, resolve failures, and meet data quality standards and business SLAs

Optimise SAS code and SQL (including T‑SQL and stored procedures) for performance and efficient resource use.

Maintain related Python scripts and SQL Server stored procedures as part of the data pipelines.

About You

Hands on experience in SAS 9.4 development within data warehousing or analytics environments.

Strong Base SAS and SAS Macro skills, and proficiency in PROC SQL and commonly used procedures

Experience integrating SAS with SQL Server, including SAS/ACCESS, ODBC/OLE DB, LIBNAME engines, pass‑through SQL, bulk loading

Proven experience in data validation, reconciliation, and quality controls

Clear communicator who can explain data and analytical outputs to non‑technical stakeholders

Experience with SAS Data Integration Studio, SAS Enterprise Guide, or SAS Management Console is preferred

Working at Hollard

At Hollard, you'll discover an environment where you can truly make an impact. We offer the best of both worlds – the opportunity, agility and creativity of a company growing with scale, alongside a focus on becoming a catalyst for enduring, positive, social change.

We're a tight‑knit team, where authentic voices and unique perspectives matter. We work supportively, collaboratively and inclusively to help shape our future and create shared value for our communities.

Hollard proudly promotes flexible work including remote work, non‑traditional work patterns, and work‑family balance. We're also unapologetically committed to creating a workplace that values your diversity with a true sense of inclusion. We actively seek to hire for your different lived experiences, including as it relates to disability, ethnicity, faith, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, gender diversity, sexual orientation, age, neurodiversity.

We're building something special. Working closely with our industry partners to reshape insurance for the better, we're people changing insurance.

Please note: Even if you don't meet all our selection criteria, we encourage you to apply.

A full background check will be completed on the successful applicant.

Australian work rights are required for this position.

Visit the Hollard careers page to learn about how Hollard will collect, store and handle your personal information.

  • Work involves following detailed written operating instructions, procedures, and specifications in the manufacture of MQ products in a contamination-controlled (e.g. clean room) limited access facility.
  • Operate manual and computer-controlled equipment such as vacuum systems, H-furnaces, evaporators, and final bake out stations.
  • Other fabrication processes include chemical cleaning, etching, electroplating, thin film evaporation and thick film metallization, laser, resistance, and electron beam welding, machining, optical comparator operations, Coordinate Measurement Machine procedures, X-ray Digital Radiography, Computed Tomography, brazing, epoxy joining and encapsulation, subassembly, final assembly, flame spraying, neutron tube exhaust processing, and high voltage product testing.

Verify the readiness of operators, work direction, equipment, tooling, fixtures, and gauges to ensure effective performance.

Some assignments require RAD-worker or explosives training and certification.
  • As assigned, the individual may act as a lead person, which includes responsibilities such as making schedule commitments, assigning work to coworkers, and instructing and training others. Planning and performing work using industry-standard safety practices is essential. Requirements include successful completion of the Sandia National Laboratories Neutron Generator Apprentice Training Program, certified by the NM State Apprenticeship Council, and/or the Sandia Production Trades Training Program as well as obtaining and maintaining DOE-approved neutron generator process qualifications.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DOE Q Clearance

Degrees could be in the following degree concentration: Metals Technology with a Concentration in Machine Tool Technology, Electronics Technology or Electronic Engineering Technology or Manufacturing Technology with any concentration.

One post-secondary Algebra I (or higher Math) course
One post-secondary Writing (or higher English) course

  • Completion of a State approved Materials Specialty apprenticeship program
  • Attainment of an associates degree with an emphasis in a relevant area
  • Possess the equivalent on-the-job work experience

  • Proven ability to adhere to written work instructions
  • Committed to conducting work safely
  • Skilled in collaborating within a team environment
  • Proficient in computer usage
  • Background in high-consequence component production
  • Knowledgeable in handling radioactive materials
  • Experienced in process improvement initiatives
  • Familiarity with Oracle software
  • Effective communicator with strong interpersonal skills

Posting Duration

This posting will be open for application submissions for a minimum of seven (7) calendar days, including the 'posting date'. Sandia reserves the right to extend the posting date at any time.

About Our Team

Department 7565, responsible for the Ferroelectric Neutron Generator (FENG) Final Assembly & Test Value Stream, engages in a variety of specialized activities essential for delivering Neutron Generator products and ensuring product quality. Our goal is to surpass customer expectations by consistently providing top-quality products on schedule while achieving high yield rates.

About Sandia

Sandia National Laboratories is the nation’s premier science and engineering lab for national security and technology innovation, with teams of specialists focused on cutting-edge work in a broad array of areas. Some of the main reasons we love our jobs:

  • Challenging work with amazing impact that contributes to security, peace, and freedom worldwide
  • Extraordinary co-workers
  • Some of the best tools, equipment, and research facilities in the world
  • Career advancement and enrichment opportunities
  • Flexible work arrangements for many positions include 9/80 (work 80 hours every two weeks, with every other Friday off) and 4/10 (work 4 ten-hour days each week) compressed workweeks, part-time work, and telecommuting (a mix of onsite work and working from home)
  • Generous vacation, strong medical and other benefits, competitive 401k, learning opportunities, relocation assistance and amenities aimed at creating a solid work/life balance*

World-changing technologies. Life-changing careers. Learn more about Sandia at: http://www.sandia.gov

Applicants for employment need to be able to obtain and maintain a DOE Q-level security clearance, which requires U.S. citizenship. title: Partnerships Solutions Lead - X (Twiter) Partnership
description:
Are you ready to join our digital revolution journey?
At Aleph, we’re not just part of the digital advertising landscape—we’re shaping its future. Representing the world’s leading platforms, including TikTok, Amazon, Google, and nearly 55 others, we operate in 130+ markets across new and existing geographies.

As Partnerships Solutions Lead, you will design, deliver and scale integrated solutions for clients and sales teams, drawing on deep X platform expertise. You will oversee the X Customer Success Management (CSM) group and make sure standards are upheld across solution delivery, reporting and partner engagement.

You will act as a strategic bridge between X, our internal teams, and our global and regional clients. Your work ensures business objectives are met while driving client satisfaction, X platform adoption and revenue growth.

While this role is based in Riga, Latvia, we welcome applications from candidates in any other location in Europe, and we are open to hiring in other EU countries.

Process optimization and operational excellence

title: Senior Director, Patient Advocacy
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Senior Director, Patient Advocacy based in the United States.

As Senior Director, Patient Advocacy, you will shape the strategy that ensures patients, caregivers, and communities play a central role in the development of innovative medicines. You will lead patient advocacy initiatives across kidney and metabolic diseases, building meaningful partnerships with advocacy organizations and community stakeholders. Working closely with Medical Affairs, clinical development, regulatory, and executive leadership teams, you will translate patient insights into actionable strategies that influence clinical trial design, enrollment, and patient support. You will establish and grow the patient advocacy function while fostering a culture of collaboration, inclusion, and accountability. This leadership opportunity comes at a pivotal stage in clinical development, when patient engagement will be essential to advancing upcoming clinical trials. Your work will help strengthen community trust, improve the patient experience, and ensure that scientific innovation remains firmly focused on patient needs.

Accountabilities:

  • Define and lead the patient advocacy and community engagement strategy, aligning initiatives with clinical development priorities, Medical Affairs objectives, pipeline needs, and broader organizational goals.
  • Manage the function's budget, resource allocation, and strategic planning, regularly communicating progress, performance, and impact to Medical Affairs leadership and executive stakeholders.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between the organization and patients, caregivers, patient advocacy groups, professional societies, and community-based organizations across kidney disease, metabolic disease, and future therapeutic areas.
  • Develop and maintain strategic partnerships at the national and international levels, with particular attention to communities disproportionately affected by kidney disease and other relevant conditions.
  • Design and implement patient education, communications, community outreach, and engagement programs that increase disease awareness and improve understanding of clinical research and the therapeutic pipeline.
  • Represent patient and caregiver perspectives in cross-functional discussions, ensuring that lived experiences inform clinical trial design, recruitment and enrollment strategies, regulatory planning, patient support programs, health equity initiatives, and broader business decisions.
  • Establish and lead patient and caregiver advisory groups to gather actionable insights and incorporate patient priorities throughout the drug development lifecycle.
  • Ensure that all advocacy activities, partnerships, grants, sponsorships, and patient interactions comply with applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, and internal policies.
  • Lead, mentor, and expand the patient advocacy team, including recruiting new talent, establishing performance expectations, supporting professional development, and fostering inclusive leadership.
  • Define and monitor meaningful performance indicators that demonstrate the function's contribution to clinical trial enrollment, patient experience, community relationships, and long-term organizational impact.
  • Promote strong communication, cross-functional collaboration, effective delegation, strategic execution, and continuous development across the team.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, with a graduate degree in public health, nursing, social work, public policy, or a related discipline considered an advantage.
  • At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in patient advocacy and community engagement, including responsibility for leading a function and managing a team, ideally within the biopharmaceutical or life sciences industry.
  • Strong understanding of the biopharmaceutical industry, the drug development lifecycle, patient engagement practices, and the compliance requirements governing interactions with patients and advocacy organizations.
  • Demonstrated success in building and managing strategic partnerships with patient advocacy organizations, professional societies, and community groups at national and international levels.
  • Experience engaging executive leadership, providing strategic recommendations, and delivering clear, compelling presentations that influence decision-making.
  • Proven people management capabilities, including recruiting, mentoring, developing, and leading high-performing teams while establishing clear goals and accountability.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust, navigate complex stakeholder relationships, negotiate effectively, and find common ground among diverse perspectives.
  • A patient-first, ethical, and collaborative mindset, combined with strong business judgment and the ability to translate patient insights into measurable strategic outcomes.
  • Strong leadership capabilities, including transparent communication, active listening, cross-functional influence, strategic prioritization, resource management, and effective delegation.
  • A commitment to inclusive leadership, continuous learning, and employee development, with the ability to identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, and align team activities with organizational priorities.
  • Experience in kidney disease, metabolic disease, or related therapeutic areas is highly desirable, as is familiarity with the needs of communities disproportionately affected by these conditions.
  • A demonstrated understanding of patient and caregiver perspectives, with established relationships within relevant patient communities, is an additional advantage.

Candidates who meet many, but not necessarily all, of these qualifications are encouraged to apply.

Benefits:

  • Competitive annual salary: The expected annual salary range for employees based in the San Francisco Bay Area is $270,000–$300,000, depending on experience, skills, location, and other job-related factors.
  • Performance-based compensation: Eligibility for an annual performance bonus.
  • Equity incentives: Access to an equity incentive plan, subject to applicable eligibility and plan terms.
  • Healthcare coverage: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible employees.
  • Mental health support: Access to mental health offerings that support employee well-being.
  • Retirement savings: A 401(k) program with an employer match.
  • Paid time off: A generous holiday and paid time off policy.
  • Professional development: Opportunities to lead and grow a strategic function, develop talent, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams across clinical development and Medical Affairs.
  • Meaningful impact: The opportunity to ensure patient and caregiver perspectives influence the development of innovative treatments for kidney and metabolic diseases.
  • Collaborative culture: A supportive environment that values integrity, teamwork, initiative, inclusive leadership, scientific excellence, and measurable impact.
  • Compensation transparency: Salary benchmarking is informed by industry market data, and the final starting salary will depend on relevant professional experience, skills, geographic location, and other job-related considerations. Compensation ranges may be adjusted over time.
